contract.settlement_definition: Five single-game side series, all with rules text. KXNCAAFGAME and KXNCAAFCSGAME/KXNCAAFD3GAME settle YES if the named team wins the game ('If Utah St. wins the Utah St. vs Oregon St. college football game'); the GAME text does not say whether overtime counts or what a tie pays, while the historical CSGAME and D3GAME texts say a declared tie resolves 50/50 and refer to the winner 'or participant awarded a tie'. KXNCAAFSPREAD settles YES if the named team wins by more than the half-point strike (Florida Atlantic by more than 41.5); overtime inclusion is not stated. KXNCAAFWINMARGIN settles on a bucket of final point differential in the 'Full game (including overtime)'. Postponement: GAME, SPREAD and WINMARGIN stay open if the game starts within 48 hours and otherwise resolve to a fair price; CSGAME and D3GAME stay open until a rescheduled game finishes within two weeks and otherwise resolve to a fair price. No statistics provider is named.

rules_evidence.quote: If Florida Atlantic wins by more than 41.5 points in the UTSA vs Florida Atlantic college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: Spread rung is a strict greater-than on a .5 strike, so no push exists and the question is P(margin >= 42).

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponement under 48 hours does not void; after 48 hours the same rules text resolves to a fair price, so weather and scheduling delays matter only if they cross that line.

rules_evidence.quote: Between 7 to 14 points against Miami (FL) in the Full game (including overtime)
rules_evidence.establishes: Margin buckets use the full game including overtime, so overtime points enter the margin; overtime games end with small margins (mostly 3 to 8 points), which concentrates mass in the lowest buckets.

rules_evidence.quote: If Utah St. wins the Utah St. vs Oregon St. college football game originally scheduled for Nov 21, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The FBS winner market is a plain win condition; the text names neither overtime nor tie treatment, so both remain unstated rather than read.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is declared a tie, the market will resolve to 50/50 for both teams.
rules_evidence.establishes: The Division III (and FCS) winner texts give a 50/50 tie payout and a two-week rescheduling window, edge-case wording that differs from the 48-hour clause of the FBS series.

rules_evidence.quote: the market will remain open and close after the rescheduled game has finished (within two weeks)
rules_evidence.establishes: FCS postponement handling is a two-week window, not the 48-hour window of KXNCAAFGAME and KXNCAAFSPREAD.

variants_and_edge_cases: Two postponement regimes inside the archetype: GAME, SPREAD and WINMARGIN use a 48-hour start window then fair price; CSGAME and D3GAME (historical texts) keep the market open for a rescheduled game finished within two weeks, then fair price.
Tie handling is stated only in CSGAME and D3GAME (declared tie pays 50/50); KXNCAAFGAME and KXNCAAFSPREAD are silent, which matters little in FBS (overtime prevents ties) but is unread.
KXNCAAFWINMARGIN buckets are custom strikes ('Between 7 to 14 points'); inclusive endpoints at 7 and 14 are implied by the wording, but adjacent bucket boundaries are not shown in the sample.
KXNCAAFSPREAD says only 'wins by more than 41.5 points' and resolves on the official final result; overtime inclusion is not stated (contrast WINMARGIN 'Full game (including overtime)').
KXNCAAFD3GAME is a Division III playoff game (North Central (IL) vs John Carroll); team-strength data for D3 and FCS comes from scores only, not from FBS play-by-play.
contract.settlement_data_source: Kalshi text cites the official final result of the game; the specific Source Agency or stats provider is not named in the sampled rules for the game markets. NCAA and conference box scores are the likely truth, but the exact provider is unresolved.

mechanism.summary: Final margin = true strength difference (opponent-adjusted offense and defense, each uncertain) + site effect + situational and availability shifts, plus a game-level noise term whose size grows with fewer possessions, high variance styles and weather. College football has thin connectivity, a very wide spread of team strength (spreads above 30 are common), and no reliable injury feed, so the prior and its uncertainty matter as much as the mean. The realized margin is then truncated and reshaped by script: favourites with big leads pull starters and run clock, trailing teams chase, and scoring comes in lumps of 3, 6, 7 and 8, so probabilities at adjacent half-point rungs differ by key-number mass. Moneyline settles on the winner after overtime (no ties), spread rungs on margin including overtime.

stages.name: Team-strength prior and its uncertainty
stages.description: Each team's true strength is a latent opponent-adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency, estimated from last season (shrunk by returning production, portal net gains and recruiting talent) and updated through the year. Connectivity across the 130-plus FBS teams is thin, so a Group-of-Five team's rating relative to a Power team is calibrated by few cross-conference games. The width of the estimate, not just its centre, matters for P(cover).
stages.distribution: Latent Gaussian rating with prior SD roughly 5-6 points in week 0 shrinking toward 2-3 by midseason; mean-reverting, heavy-tailed for teams with massive roster churn.

stages.name: Availability and personnel substitution
stages.description: Starting quarterback, offensive line and a handful of high-snap defenders determine the actual units on the field. Information is released late and partially (there is no mandatory injury report in most conferences), so what matters is both the expected points value of each loss and the vintage at which it became knowable. A quarterback swap is a discrete shift with a wide posterior on the replacement.
stages.distribution: Discrete shocks (zero most weeks, 3-10 point magnitude for a QB) with a mixture of confirmed and doubtful states; replacement quality is itself uncertain.

stages.name: Site, travel, weather and motivation adjustments
stages.description: A home-field term that differs by team (crowd, altitude, visiting travel and body clock), neutral-site games where it vanishes, short-week or bye effects, and games with unusual stakes such as rivalry, bowl eligibility or opt-outs. Weather mostly changes the variance and the run-pass balance of the game rather than the mean margin.
stages.distribution: Mostly small additive shifts (0.5-3 points) with a few large conditional ones (altitude visitors, bowl opt-outs); weather widens variance.

stages.name: Matchup-specific scoring process and variance
stages.description: Two teams of equal rating can produce different margin distributions: a pressure defence against a thin line, an explosive passing attack against a poor secondary, a run-heavy slow offence that shortens the game. Possession count and play style set how many independent scoring trials there are, which controls margin variance and thus underdog cover frequency, and head-coach aggression bends the tail of late scoring.
stages.distribution: Margin variance scales roughly with the number of possessions; style pairings create heteroscedastic, skewed margin errors rather than mean shifts.

stages.name: Game-script truncation and score lattice
stages.description: Once a lead exceeds roughly three scores, college coaches substitute starters, run the ball and burn clock, and trailing teams score late garbage points, so realized margins compress at high spreads relative to a Gaussian. Football scoring is lumpy (3, 6, 7, 8), producing mass on margins of 3, 7, 10 and 14 and differences between rungs such as 6.5 and 7.5. The final result includes overtime, which cannot end tied.
stages.distribution: Truncated, key-number-lumpy margin distribution with a right tail that depends on opponent class (FBS vs FCS) and on coach behaviour.

stages.name: Contract mechanics: strike, overtime scope and postponement
stages.description: Spread rungs are strict greater-than on a .5 strike, so the target is P(margin >= ceiling of the strike) with no push; WINMARGIN buckets are read as full game including overtime, while SPREAD and GAME overtime scope is not stated (CSGAME and D3GAME only say a declared tie pays 50/50). GAME, SPREAD and WINMARGIN stay open for a postponement that starts within 48 hours and otherwise resolve to a fair price; CSGAME and D3GAME stay open until a rescheduled game finishes within two weeks, then fair price, so the lifecycle feed defines the information set and the void-like state.
stages.distribution: Binary payoff per rung (bucket for WINMARGIN) as a deterministic function of the final margin; a small fair-price mass for long postponements.

stages.name: Division III and FCS winner markets from score-only ratings
stages.description: KXNCAAFD3GAME (for example North Central (IL) vs John Carroll) and KXNCAAFCSGAME (Montana at Montana St.) are winner markets on games outside FBS data coverage. The outcome is still margin > 0, but the margin mean must come from a score-based rating with weak inter-region connectivity, the home edge applies to the playoff host seed, and the margin spread is wider than in FBS because talent gaps are larger; dominant D3 programs produce very lopsided favourites. These historical texts also differ in edge-case wording: a tie pays 50/50 and a postponement stays open for up to two weeks.
stages.distribution: Probit in rating gap over a division-specific margin SD, with extra variance from rating uncertainty; probabilities near 0 or 1 for dominant programs.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted efficiency, talent and returning production feed the latent rating; rating_posterior_sd adds the uncertainty term the existing set lacked.

opponent_matchup.note: Unit-on-unit matchups; value is in crosses (rush rate vs protection) not levels.

role_personnel.note: Replacement quality at quarterback and snap-weighted loss across positions.

availability_news.note: Coverage rests on timestamped quarterback status, snap-weighted availability loss and eligibility news; cfb.injuries is WEAK (no official feed in most conferences) and removed, the feed gap is listed as injury_feed_gap.

coaching_scheme.note: Aggression and clock management plus scheme identity; coach-change resets are an open definition issue.

environment.note: Home field, altitude, neutral site and weather; kickoff body-clock effects are not separately defined.

game_context_script.note: Starter-removal and clock behaviour truncate large margins.

pace_volume.note: Possession count and tempo are measured by cfb.pace (seconds per play, plays per game, no-huddle rate) and cfb.drives (drives per game, plays per drive), crossed with offense_style and clock behaviour; the combined possession count sets margin variance.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-play efficiency with a luck adjustment for fumble recoveries.

distribution_variance.note: Margin SD, truncation and key-number mass.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry, bowl eligibility and opt-outs.

officiating_rules.note: Crew penalty tendencies move a game by about one or two penalties and under a point of margin; the one rule-driven item that matters (targeting ejection) is carried by cfb.suspension_eligibility, so no separate officiating input is justified for sides.

settlement_contract.note: Strict greater-than rungs, overtime inclusion and 48-hour postponement rule read from the sampled rules; ML and FCS series text is missing.

cfb.qb_replacement_value.label: Quarterback replacement value in points
cfb.qb_replacement_value.mechanism: Converts a confirmed or doubtful quarterback change into an expected-margin shift in points per game.
cfb.qb_replacement_value.rationale: Identity of the starter (cfb.qb_status_pit) is a vintage, not a number. A backup with 40 career dropbacks has a very wide EPA/play posterior, so the swap cost is both a mean shift and a variance increase; the market tends to over- or under-react depending on prior-year snaps.
cfb.qb_replacement_value.measurement: Starter value = opponent-adjusted EPA per dropback (incl. designed QB runs) over the last 2 seasons with 1-season half-life weights, shrunk to a recruiting-composite prior (mapping of 247/On3 rating to EPA/dropback fitted on historical FBS QBs) with k = 150 dropbacks; the same for the replacement. Swap value in points per game = (starter - replacement) EPA/dropback x team dropbacks per game (35-45, from script inputs); no extra conversion factor. Report mean and posterior SD. As-of timestamp = last confirmed depth chart or beat-report vintage before kickoff.
free_sources: CFBD plays and PPA endpoints (free key)
raw_data: play-by-play with passer id, EPA, dropbacks
cfb.qb_replacement_value.why: Quarterback change is the biggest discrete news item in a college spread, and the replacement pool is thin and unevenly observed, so a point value with uncertainty is required, not just a flag.

cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.label: Snap-weighted availability loss
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.mechanism: Aggregates all known absences (any position) into a single points-per-game value using snap share times player value over replacement.
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.rationale: College injury information is sparse, so the model needs a way to price a partial list (two starting linemen out, a corner doubtful) consistently; counting injuries is wrong because snap load and positional value differ by factors of five or more.
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.measurement: For each player i reported out or flagged: loss_i = P_out_i x snap_share_i x (value_i - value_replacement_pos) in points, where value is on-field PPA/EPA per play (or PFF grade converted by a fitted regression to points per game) and P_out takes the share of historical 'flagged' cases that missed the game, estimated per source type (coach statement, beat report, team release) from captured history, not fixed constants. Sum over players (offence and defence separately), with QB handled by cfb.qb_replacement_value. Timestamp every report; as-of pregame.
free_sources: CFBD player usage and season stats (free key)
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.why: Turns an unstructured injury list into the same unit as the spread, so a +/- 1.5 point late shift can be compared with the quote move rather than judged qualitatively.

cfb.rating_posterior_sd.label: Team-rating posterior standard deviation
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.mechanism: Per-team uncertainty about true strength given games played, connectivity and roster churn; sets the width of the margin distribution.
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.rationale: A rating gap of 7 with SDs of 2.0 and 2.0 gives a different win probability than the same gap with SDs of 5.0 and 5.0 early in the season; ignoring estimation error makes September favourites look too safe and moves cover probabilities at every rung.
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.measurement: Bayesian state-space rating per team: prior mean from last season rating x returning-production shrinkage, prior SD 6 points at week 0 falling toward 2.5 by week 10 per the observed rating update; implement as posterior variance = 1 / (1/prior_var + n_eff / game_sd^2) with game_sd = 13 points and n_eff = sum of connectivity-weighted game weights. Add portal-churn variance inflation proportional to 1 - returning production. Use margin-difference SD sqrt(sd_home^2 + sd_away^2 + 13^2 x (1 + 0.3 x pace_variance_term)).
free_sources: CFBD games and returning production (free key)
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.why: Margin SD and the shape of P(cover) across rungs depend on rating uncertainty, which no existing input supplies.

cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.label: Large-spread cover curve from non-market rating gap
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.mechanism: Empirical probability that the favourite's margin exceeds k, as a function of pre-game rating gap and opponent class (FBS vs FCS, G5 vs P4).
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.rationale: Rungs such as FAU by more than 41.5 sit in a regime where starters are removed, the clock runs and margin growth is truncated; a Gaussian around the rating gap overstates the tail, and the truncation point differs for FCS opponents and for coaches who keep scoring.
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.measurement: From historical FBS games (2014 onward), bin pre-game rating gap (non-market, SP+ or own rating) in 3-point buckets; for each bucket compute the empirical survival function P(margin >= k) for k in {1..60} with isotonic smoothing and a beta prior of strength 30 games on the pooled curve. Estimate separate curves for FCS opponents, neutral site, and for coaches in the top and bottom tercile of historical starter-pull time. Output is a vector of probabilities per rung, evaluated as-of kickoff.
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.why: The sampled KXNCAAFSPREAD and KXNCAAFWINMARGIN rungs reach 41.5 and 7-14 buckets; probabilities across 40 rungs must come from a calibrated truncated distribution, not a normal.

cfb.fourth_down_aggression.label: Fourth-down aggression and clock-management index
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.mechanism: Coach tendency to go for it, onside, and to run or save clock, which changes margin variance and end-of-game scoring.
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.rationale: Aggressive coaches convert field goals into possible touchdowns or turnovers on downs, widening the margin distribution; conservative leaders reduce late scoring. Two teams of equal rating but different aggression produce different cover rates for a rung.
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.measurement: For each head coach, 4th-down go-for-it rate over expected from a fitted model (yard line, distance, score diff, time) = observed go rate - model go rate for the same situations, computed over last 2 seasons with k = 40 situations shrinkage; add mean seconds of clock burned per play when leading by 8-24 in Q4 versus the conference median. Coach change resets to a coach-career prior; compute as-of week.
raw_data: play-by-play down, distance, yard line, score, time
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.why: Coaching_scheme was uncovered for sides; aggression and clock management bend the margin distribution without changing its mean.

cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.label: Division III and FCS single-game margin model from scores
cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.mechanism: Win probability for a Division III (KXNCAAFD3GAME) or FCS (KXNCAAFCSGAME) game from a score-based rating difference, a division-specific home edge and a division-specific margin spread, because no play-by-play efficiency or SP+ exists for these teams.
cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.rationale: D3 and FCS winner markets cannot use FBS efficiency ratings: D3 has about 240 teams with almost no out-of-region games before the playoff, so connectivity is weak and rating uncertainty is large; talent gaps are wider than in FBS, so the margin spread is larger and blowouts are common; and the sampled D3/FCS games are playoff games where the higher seed usually hosts, so the home edge must be estimated on postseason games, not regular-season averages.
cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.measurement: Shares the score-based team rating of cfb.lower_division_title_model (one rating fit per division, not a second rating; harmonise margin cap, carry-over and home edge with that input) and adds only the single-game layer: ridge-regularised margin rating fitted on all completed games of the division since 2010 (margin capped at 35 points, home edge estimated separately for regular season and playoff, game weight halving every 1.5 seasons, ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-season-out log loss); preseason value = 0.6 x prior final rating shrunk to conference mean; P(win) = Phi((rating gap + home edge) / sigma_div) with sigma_div fitted per division on residuals (expected larger than FBS); posterior SD per team from the ridge Hessian added to sigma_div. As-of the last completed game before kickoff; no market input.
raw_data: game date, home/away/neutral, team ids and division, final score including overtime, playoff round and seed since 2010
cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.why: KXNCAAFD3GAME and KXNCAAFCSGAME are winner markets on teams outside FBS data coverage; their probability comes from this score-based rating, not from SP+ or PPA.

cfb.market_ratings.reason: A rating backed out of sportsbook or Kalshi prices already contains QB, weather and injury news; feeding it into a model that is then compared with the same price removes any chance of finding incremental information. Keep only as the comparator for edge measurement.

cfb.sp_plus.reason: SP+ is an opponent-adjusted, tempo-free rating with a preseason prior built partly from recruiting and returning production, so it is correlated with cfb.talent and cfb.roster_continuity; useful as a second independent strength estimate but must be lagged to the pre-kickoff publication date, not the season-end value.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Opponent-adjusted offensive PPA is the structural scoring component of the margin, but the label bundles PPA, success rate and explosiveness; needs pass/rush splits, garbage-time filtering and a decay window, otherwise blowout-inflated plays overstate teams that beat weak opponents badly.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Defensive counterpart of off_ppa with the same caveats (garbage time, FCS and low-connectivity opponents); also double counts part of pass_rush, secondary_coverage and run_defense, so those matchup rows should be modelled as deviations from this baseline, not added to it.

cfb.cross_conf_calibration.reason: Needed because 12-game schedules inside 10 conferences give thin connectivity; matters most for Group-of-Five vs Power-conference games and early-season Week 1-4 ratings, nearly irrelevant by November within a conference.

cfb.talent.reason: Recruiting composite gives a prior on depth and ceiling that is informative in September and decays as in-season efficiency accumulates; its weight should be a declining function of games played, which the label does not state.

cfb.roster_continuity.reason: Returning production regresses last year's rating toward the mean and drives the early-season prior width; overlaps with cfb.transfer_roster which is its portal-adjusted extension, so the two should be merged into one net-production measure.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: Starting QB identity with vintage is the single largest discrete late-news term in college spreads; however it supplies only identity, not the points value of the swap, which is why cfb.qb_replacement_value is added.

cfb.injuries.reason: No official injury report exists in most conferences, so as defined this input is a wish rather than a feed; it only becomes usable with a self-captured, timestamped news archive, and even then coverage is partial.

cfb.ol.reason: Offensive-line continuity (starts together, games missed) is a real driver of sack rate and rush efficiency; the label also lumps in the defensive line, which duplicates pass_rush and run_defense and should be split out.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: Fumble recovery is close to a coin flip (about 50 percent) so results-based ratings over-credit lucky teams; a regression-to-expected adjustment to rating is valid but only matters for teams with extreme turnover margin.

cfb.venue.reason: Home-field value is team-specific (altitude, crowd, travel for the visitor) and absent at neutral sites; keep, but split neutral-site flag, altitude and visiting-team time-zone shift into separate fields.

cfb.rest_travel.reason: Bye-week and short-week effects are real but small, around a point at most, and are partly priced; keep as a context adjustment, not a primary driver.

cfb.motivation.reason: Rivalry, bowl eligibility and clinched or eliminated status shift effort and lineup choices in specific games; partial knowability and a thin sample of comparable situations mean the coefficient will be noisy.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Matters for large-spread rungs, where starters are pulled and clock is run, compressing the favourite's margin below what ratings imply; the effect is coach-specific and needs a measured pull-point, not an assumption. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind and precipitation mostly move totals; for the margin it changes variance and slightly favours the run-heavy side, so it is context for sides rather than a primary driver.

cfb.score_resid.reason: Defined as residuals around lines, so it is market-derived; the non-market content (mass at margins 3, 7, 10, 14) is carried by cfb.mismatch_cover_curve and rating_posterior_sd, so score_resid is removed from stage and coverage wiring.

m.external_lines.reason: De-vigged sportsbook sides are the reference price to beat, not an input; use them to measure whether a fundamentals estimate adds information and to detect Kalshi staleness after news.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung consistency of the spread ladder (KXNCAAFSPREAD rungs) is an arbitrage and staleness diagnostic derived from prices; it says nothing about game outcome.

cfb.transfer_roster.reason: Portal arrivals reshape starters before the season and eligibility rulings can land mid-year; mostly a preseason prior input and effectively merged with roster_continuity once week 4 has passed.

cfb.opt_out_departures.reason: Only relevant for bowl and CFP games and for four-game redshirt decisions; regular-season sides rungs are unaffected, so keep as a conditional input for postseason games.

cfb.suspension_eligibility.reason: Suspensions and targeting first-half ejections remove players for part of a game; low frequency and partial knowability, but when known pregame (named suspension) it is a clean availability shock.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price history is the market's own output; it measures when information was absorbed (useful for timing studies and closing-line value) but is not a cause of the game side outcome and must not enter a fundamentals model.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread govern whether a game side edge is tradable, not whether the event occurs; keep for execution and sizing, not as an outcome input.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule changes net edge on game side contracts (largest near 50c) but has no causal link to the result; an execution parameter, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe liquidity and price reliability for game side quotes; useful to weight benchmark trust, irrelevant to the outcome process.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades show informed flow and fill realism for game side contracts; it is market microstructure used to validate fills, not a determinant of the outcome.

m.lifecycle.reason: Open/close/halt/postponement events matter here because the 48-hour postponement clause converts a delayed game side market to a fair-price settlement; needed to define the information set and void handling.

cfb.pass_rush.reason: Pressure rate for and against interacts with OL health; as an additive term it duplicates def_ppa pass splits, so its value is the matchup product (rush rate vs protection rate), not the level.

cfb.secondary_coverage.reason: Explosive-pass-allowed rate is a component of def_ppa and success_explosiveness; keep as the matchup partner of the opponent's deep-pass rate, not as a standalone strength term.

cfb.run_defense.reason: Front-seven run defence is a component of def_ppa rushing; adds information only when crossed with the opponent's rushing share and quarterback mobility.

cfb.offense_style.reason: Option, tempo and RPO identity changes possession count and therefore margin variance more than margin mean; valuable mainly for the underdog-cover shape at constant rating gap. Reverification: the catalog measurement uses style-specific residuals of spread/total, which are residuals around market lines (the same defect as cfb.score_resid); only residuals against own non-market ratings are admissible, the line-residual version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.reason: The conference 10-win count series (SECWINS, BIGTENWINS, BIG12WINS, ACCWINS) it served are filed under season_futures after the reconciliation; no single-game side series here depends on a conference win grid.

cfb.season_max_total_tail.reason: KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE, the Division I season-maximum total it was written for, is filed under game_total; a season extreme-value tail has no role in pricing one game's winner, spread or margin bucket.

cfb.qb.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on cfb.qb_status_pit x cfb.market_ratings x cfb.qb: QB status x spread: a QB change in college moves the line more because of depth and system fit; Kalshi quotes) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.coaching.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on cfb.blowout_management x cfb.score_resid x cfb.coaching: Spread size x blowout management: cover probability for big favorites depends on whether the coach keeps press) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.pace.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on cfb.pace x cfb.off_ppa x cfb.def_ppa: Tempo mismatch x efficiency: when a fast offense meets a slow, ball-control team, variance falls and margin sh; stage s4) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.drives.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s4) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: A backup quarterback behind a depleted offensive line loses more than the sum of the two separate effects because inexperienced passers rely on protection and play-action tied to a functioning run game; the penalty is largest when the replacement is a first-year player with fewer than 50 dropbacks.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit margin residual on replacement value, OL games-missed index and their product; compare slope on the product term in games with both vs one shock.

interactions.mechanism: Past a lead of about 21 points in the second half the favourite's marginal scoring rate drops sharply for conservative coaches, while aggressive coaches keep scoring; this makes the cover rate for 30+ point rungs a coach-dependent step, not a smooth function of rating gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised P(margin >= 30) for games with gap > 28 split by aggression tercile; test a step at pre-game gap 21-24.

interactions.mechanism: In weeks 1-4 the prior dominates, so talent and returning production explain more of the margin than in-season efficiency and the posterior SD is wide; from about week 8 the weights flip and the same variables become nearly redundant.
interactions.how_to_test: Rolling regression of margin on prior vs in-season rating by week; identify the crossing week and test stability across seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Wind or rain compresses passing, which helps a run-heavy option team against a weak front and hurts an air-raid favourite; the weather effect on margin depends on which side is pass-reliant and on opposing run defence.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact style (pass share), wind speed above 15 mph and opponent run-defence rank in a margin residual model; check sign by pass-reliant favourite vs underdog.

interactions.mechanism: Home-field value is not constant: it grows with altitude and crowd for visitors on a short week and shrinks in rivalry games where both teams are fully motivated; opt-outs at neutral-site bowls remove it altogether.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate home-edge by team and test interactions with days of rest and rivalry flag; neutral-site bowls as a control group.

interactions.mechanism: In the D3 and FCS playoffs the higher seed hosts until the final, so the home edge is confounded with seed strength and applies only in rounds before the neutral-site final; a regular-season home edge applied to a playoff host overstates the favourite when both seed and host status carry the same information.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the playoff home edge separately with seed difference as a covariate on D3 and FCS postseason games and compare with the regular-season estimate.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in rating gap beyond ~21 points, with a floor from garbage-time scores
nonlinearities.why: Expected margin does not grow one-for-one with rating gap once starters sit, so P(margin >= 42) rises far more slowly than a Gaussian predicts and differs by opponent class.

nonlinearities.shape: Inverse-square-root decay in games played, with a jump after portal-heavy offseasons
nonlinearities.why: Rating uncertainty shrinks with sample size but resets with roster churn; it changes win probability by several points at constant rating gap.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in dropbacks of the replacement: very wide posterior below ~50 career dropbacks
nonlinearities.why: Swap cost for an unknown backup is a fat-tailed mixture, not a normal shift; the mean is little changed but the downside tail is heavy.

contract.settlement_definition: Nine team/game stat series. KXNCAAFTEAMRECYDS settles YES if the named team records at least N receiving yards (325+ = strike 324.5) and KXNCAAFTEAMYDS if it records at least N total yards of offense (475+), where total yards = rushing plus receiving yards and sacks and quarterback kneels are negative rushing yards; yards in the first or second overtime count and 2-point conversions do not. Touchdown-count series: KXNCAAFTEAMTD (team touchdowns), KXNCAAFTOTALTD (both teams), KXNCAAFTEAMRSHTD and TEAMRECTD (rushing/receiving touchdowns; a teammate's fumble-recovery touchdown is not credited), KXNCAAFDSTTD (at least one defensive or special-teams touchdown by either team); overtime touchdowns count and 2-point conversions never do. KXNCAAFFIRSTTDTEAM settles on the team scoring the first touchdown of any kind, overtime included, with a separate 'No team scores a TD' outcome. KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT (team rushing attempts) is TITLE_ONLY with no listed market. Postponement under 48 hours stays open; otherwise a fair price. No statistics provider is named.

rules_evidence.quote: Any receiving yards recorded in the first or second overtime periods count toward a team's total.
rules_evidence.establishes: Overtime periods 1 and 2 add yards to the total, so overtime probability is a (small) positive contribution to the distribution.

rules_evidence.quote: Successful 2-point conversions, including those in overtime, do not count for this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Yards gained on 2-point attempts are excluded, which matters for third-overtime-and-later periods that consist only of 2-point tries.

rules_evidence.quote: If Notre Dame records 325+ receiving yards in the Miami (FL) vs Notre Dame college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: The strike is stated as 325+ (floor_strike 324.5), a greater-than-or-equal threshold on the sum of the team's receiving yards.

rules_evidence.quote: Any touchdowns recorded in overtime count toward a team's total.
rules_evidence.establishes: Team touchdown counts include overtime touchdowns; whether defensive and special-teams touchdowns by the team count is not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: All touchdowns count for this market, including offensive, defensive, and special teams.
rules_evidence.establishes: The first-touchdown race has three arrival channels (offence, defence, special teams) for each team, and overtime touchdowns can decide it.

rules_evidence.quote: collectively record at least 1 defensive or special teams touchdown
rules_evidence.establishes: DSTTD is a game-level rare-event union over both teams' return and turnover touchdowns, not a team count.

rules_evidence.quote: A touchdown scored by another player after recovering a fumble by the rushing player does not count as a rushing touchdown
rules_evidence.establishes: Rushing-touchdown credit follows the official play credit, so teammate fumble-recovery scores are excluded from the rushing count.

rules_evidence.quote: If Wisconsin and Notre Dame collectively record 8+ touchdowns
rules_evidence.establishes: TOTALTD is a combined count with an N+ (greater-than-or-equal) strike, a right-tail rung of a nested ladder.

rules_evidence.quote: Sacks and quarterback kneels count as negative rushing yards for the team on offense.
rules_evidence.establishes: Total offense is net of sack and kneel yardage, so sack proneness and late-lead kneels lower the settled total.

rules_evidence.quote: Any receiving touchdowns recorded in overtime count toward a team's total.
rules_evidence.establishes: Receiving-touchdown counts include overtime touchdowns, like the rushing and team touchdown series.

variants_and_edge_cases: Nine series share the archetype after reconciliation: team receiving yards, team total yards, five touchdown-count series (team, total, rushing, receiving, defensive/special teams), the first-touchdown race and team rushing attempts; their volume drivers differ (dropbacks, plays, scoring trips, return chances, run plays).
Overtime period 1 and 2 yards count; from the third overtime the format is alternating 2-point attempts whose yards are excluded, so the rule has an effect only for very long games.

Receiving yards can be negative on a catch behind the line; whether negative receiving yards net against the total, whether sacks or laterals affect it, and whether team receiving yards equal completions' yards under official NCAA statistics are NOT stated in the sampled text; this is domain knowledge only and the definition is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.
Threshold rungs are .5 strikes written as N+ (for example 325+), so there is no push; the ladder of rungs for one team and game is a monotone survival curve.
Postponement of more than 48 hours or cancellation resolves to a fair price rather than void.

Overtime wording differs: RECYDS and DSTTD say 'first or second overtime periods', TEAMTD, TOTALTD, RSHTD and RECTD say 'overtime'; since the third overtime onward consists of two-point attempts that never count, the two wordings are equivalent in effect.
KXNCAAFTEAMTD counts touchdowns 'recorded by' the team; whether a defensive or special-teams touchdown scored by that team counts is not stated (TOTALTD and FIRSTTDTEAM state all touchdowns count).

KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT is TITLE_ONLY (no listed market, no rules text), so whether sacks and kneel-downs are rushing attempts (they are under NCAA statistics) and whether overtime attempts count is not read.
FIRSTTDTEAM has a 'No team scores a TD' outcome covering regulation plus overtime, a small point mass for very low-total games.
KXNCAAFTEAMYDS overtime wording ('first or second overtime periods') matches RECYDS; its sampled secondary text is cut at 600 characters, so any clause after the postponement sentence is unseen.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game statistics per the Kalshi wording (official final result); the specific provider (NCAA stats, conference, ESPN or Sportradar) is not named in the sampled rules, so reconciliation against CFBD box scores is required before using it for labels.

mechanism.summary: A team's receiving yards equal its passing-game completions' yardage (excluding 2-point tries), so the outcome is dropbacks x completion rate x yards per completion, truncated by what the game looks like. Dropbacks come from plays in regulation (tempo and possessions) times the pass share, which swings 15 to 20 percentage points with score state; efficiency per attempt depends on the quarterback, receiver depth and opposing pass defence and pressure; the distribution is right-skewed because explosive completions are rare and large. Overtime adds a small right tail (periods 1 and 2 count). Settlement depends on which statistics provider is the source of truth. The reconciliation added touchdown-count series and team rushing attempts: touchdowns are scoring trips times the touchdown (not field-goal) finish rate plus return and turnover touchdowns, split by run/pass at the goal line; the first-touchdown market is a race between two teams' arrival processes with the opening possession as a head start; rushing attempts are plays times a run share that rises with the lead and, under NCAA scoring, includes sacks. Team total yards (KXNCAAFTEAMYDS, re-filed here) are plays times net yards per play, with sack and kneel yardage charged to rushing per the rules note.

stages.name: Snap budget from tempo and possessions
stages.description: The number of offensive snaps a team gets in 60 minutes comes from drives and seconds per snap; both vary with score state and the season's clock rule regime (running clock after first downs since 2023). The budget sets the ceiling for dropbacks, and overtime adds one or two extra possessions with probability under ten percent.
stages.distribution: Roughly Gaussian per-game plays (SD around 9) with heavier right tail in shootouts; overtime adds a discrete lump.

stages.name: Pass share conditional on game script and scheme
stages.description: Out of the snap budget, dropbacks equal plays times the pass rate, which depends on the offence's scheme, quarterback strength, weather and above all expected score state: trailing teams drop back much more, leading ones run. Quarterback scrambles and sacks are dropbacks that do not produce receiving yards, so the relevant count is attempts, not dropbacks.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (negative binomial) conditional on expected margin; pass share piecewise in lead size.

stages.name: Completion rate and yardage per completion
stages.description: Each attempt becomes a completion with probability set by the quarterback, protection against the opposing pressure rate, receiver quality and coverage; the yards per completion are air yards plus yards after catch, with a long tail for explosive plays. The opposing secondary's explosive-allowed rate acts multiplicatively on a deep-passing offence.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli completions with heavy-tailed positive yards per completion; team receiving yards skew right (median below mean).

stages.name: Pass-catcher and quarterback availability
stages.description: The effective passing unit depends on who plays quarterback and which receivers are available; with sparse college injury reporting these shocks arrive late. A missing receiver shifts targets to replacements, lowering yards per target more than the number of targets; a quarterback change lowers both completion rate and yards per attempt and widens uncertainty.
stages.distribution: Discrete availability states with replacement-quality uncertainty; effect size is a mixture, not a smooth shift.

stages.name: Dispersion and joint script correlation
stages.description: The final yardage is a sum of a correlated set of components (plays, pass share, yards per attempt) that move together with the game script: a shootout lifts all three. The tail above a high rung such as 325 is dominated by those correlated high-script games, so independent marginals understate it.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed, correlated mixture; the threshold probability is a tail quantity sensitive to variance and covariance.

stages.name: Settlement and stat-source reconciliation
stages.description: Yards in overtime periods 1 and 2 count and 2-point yards do not; the official provider may differ from public box scores, so labels and live checks must use the same definition. A postponement beyond 48 hours resolves to a fair price rather than a win or loss.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the provider; risk comes from definitional mismatches of a few yards near the strike.

stages.name: Touchdown counts and the first-touchdown race
stages.description: For the TEAMTD, TOTALTD, RSHTD, RECTD, DSTTD and FIRSTTDTEAM series the count is drives that reach scoring range times the share finished with six points, so a team that stalls into field goals has the same points but fewer touchdowns. Goal-line play calling and a running quarterback decide the rushing versus receiving credit; interceptions, fumbles and kick returns create defensive and special-teams touchdowns that count for totals, the first-touchdown race and DSTTD but never for rushing or receiving counts. The receiving team of the opening kickoff gets the first chance in the race, and overtime touchdowns settle a race left open after regulation.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed (negative-binomial) touchdown counts with variance growing in expected scoring; rare-event Poisson for return touchdowns; competing hazards with a head start and a small no-touchdown mass for the race.

stages.name: Team rushing attempts under expected game script
stages.description: KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT has no listed market, so its definition is unread; under NCAA statistics a rushing attempt includes designed runs, scrambles, sacks and kneel-downs, so the count equals snaps times run share plus sacks taken. Run share rises sharply when protecting a lead and falls when chasing, which makes the attempt count a mirror image of the dropback count used for receiving yards and strongly dependent on the non-market expected margin.
stages.distribution: Approximately Gaussian count per game (SD of several attempts) with a lead-dependent mean; piecewise in expected margin.

stages.name: Team total offense: plays times net yards per play
stages.description: KXNCAAFTEAMYDS (SMU 475+) settles on rushing plus receiving yards, with sack and kneel yardage charged to rushing. Total yards are the snap budget times net yards per play, where the run/pass split comes from the expected script, a sack-prone quarterback lowers net yards on dropbacks, and a late-leading team gives back yards on kneels. Explosive plays create a right tail, and a big favourite reaches high rungs early and then runs clock, so the right tail is truncated by blowout management.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal team yardage (SD near 100 yards) with right skew from explosive plays and a lead-dependent truncation; overtime periods one and two add a small lump.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted team strength (SP+, offensive and defensive PPA) supplies the non-market expected margin that cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts depends on, alongside pass efficiency and the yardage profile.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing explosive pass defence and pressure rate for passing series; opposing run defence for total yards and rushing touchdowns.

role_personnel.note: Receiver availability and personnel groupings. A running quarterback shifts goal-line touchdown credit to rushing.

availability_news.note: Quarterback status (team receiving yards are his completions) and receiver availability through timestamped vintages; cfb.injuries (WEAK, no official feed) is removed and the feed gap stays in injury-related unresolved items.

coaching_scheme.note: Offensive scheme and play-calling tendencies in neutral situations.

environment.note: Wind and precipitation vintages; crowd noise and dome effects are not captured.

game_context_script.note: Expected score state drives pass volume and tempo.

pace_volume.note: Snap budget and dropbacks. Drives (scoring trials) for touchdown counts and plays x run share for rushing attempts.

efficiency_conversion.note: Yards per attempt, completion and explosive completion rates. Touchdown finishing per scoring trip and return/turnover touchdowns for the touchdown series.

distribution_variance.note: Right-skewed team-yardage dispersion and correlation with game script. Touchdown-count overdispersion for the TD ladders.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, travel and rivalry effects on passing volume are not defined for this contract; the effect is probably small but nothing in the archetype lets it be tested.

officiating_rules.note: Crew penalty rates change drive length marginally; the one rule that matters for yardage, the clock rule regime, is inside cfb.state_dependent_pace, so no separate officiating input applies to a team receiving-yards total.

settlement_contract.note: Overtime 1 and 2 counted, 2-point yards excluded, provider mismatch risk. TD series: overtime touchdowns count, 2-point tries never; TEAMRSHATT definition unread.

cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.label: Script-adjusted team dropbacks
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.mechanism: Expected team pass attempts plus sacks given the expected game flow, rather than the season-average pass rate.
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.rationale: Pass volume is the largest driver of receiving-yards variance: a team that trails by two scores throws 50-plus times, a team leading by 21 throws 20. Using season-average attempts mixes games of both kinds and understates the spread in the mean.
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.measurement: Fit dropbacks per game on team neutral-situation pass rate (first and second down, score within 7, first three quarters), opponent neutral pass-rate allowed, expected margin from non-market ratings (not a quote), and plays; then predict at the pre-game expected margin with a piecewise term at +/-14 and +/-21. Window: current season with 6-game half-life, shrunk to previous season with k = 4 games; as-of the Saturday preceding kickoff. Output: mean attempts and a negative-binomial dispersion.
free_sources: CFBD plays with down, distance, score and play type (free key)
raw_data: play-by-play with play_type, down, distance, score diff, period, clock
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.why: Receiving yards = completions x yards per completion, and completions scale with dropbacks that depend on score state, so the mean and its spread must be conditioned on expected flow.

cfb.state_dependent_pace.label: State-dependent tempo (seconds per play by score state)
cfb.state_dependent_pace.mechanism: Plays per minute differ when leading, tied or trailing, and by clock situation; determines total plays inside 60 minutes plus any overtime.
cfb.state_dependent_pace.rationale: A hurry-up team trailing can add 8 to 12 plays versus its average; a ball-control team leading runs the clock. The season mean hides this, and the rule set since 2023 (clock running after first downs outside the last two minutes) changed the baseline.
cfb.state_dependent_pace.measurement: Per offence: mean seconds per snap (clock elapsed between snaps, excluding two-minute drills, timeouts and the final 4 minutes of a half) in four score-state buckets (trailing by 9+, within 8, leading 9-16, leading 17+) over the last 12 games with 0.9 per-game decay, shrunk per bucket to the conference mean with weight n/(n + 200) (k = 200 snaps). Expected snaps = 3600 clock seconds adjusted for the season regime divided by the opponent-adjusted bucket seconds weighted by the expected score-state mix (cfb.script). As-of last completed game.
raw_data: play-by-play with period, clock, score, offense, play_type
cfb.state_dependent_pace.why: The yardage threshold is crossed mostly in games with high snap counts; state-dependent tempo is the mechanism linking expected margin to those counts.

cfb.completion_yardage_profile.label: Completion yardage profile (depth of target and yards after catch)
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.mechanism: Splits yards per completion into air yards and yards after catch and records the explosive-completion rate.
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.rationale: Two offences with the same yards per attempt can have very different variance: one dinks and runs screens, the other throws deep. Threshold probabilities depend on the tail of long completions and on the opponent's tackling and safety depth.
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.measurement: Per team: average depth of target, YAC per completion, share of completions of 20+ and 40+ yards, all opponent-adjusted by the opponent's allowed values; 10-game window with 0.7 per-game decay and shrinkage k = 60 completions to conference mean. Where air-yards data is missing (CFBD has limited coverage), approximate with yards per completion and 20+ rate. Report mean and SD of yards per completion.
free_sources: CFBD plays (yards, play text parse, free key)
PFF/SIS charting for air yards (paid, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for CFB depth)
raw_data: pass plays with yards gained and receiver
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.why: Sets the dispersion of per-completion yards, and so P(325+) relative to the mean.

cfb.wr_personnel_rate.label: Receiver personnel-grouping rate
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.mechanism: Share of snaps with 3 or more receivers (11 personnel, 10 personnel, empty sets) versus heavy sets.
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.rationale: Receiving-yards volume depends on how many pass-catchers are deployed: spread offences convert dropbacks into more targets to receivers and fewer to backs and tight ends, and the loss of a receiver matters more when the team lives in 4-wide sets.
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.measurement: For each offence, share of snaps by personnel group (RB/TE/WR counts) over the last 8 games, opponent-weighted; compute the 3+ WR snap share and empty-set rate with k = 150 snap shrinkage to conference average. Combine with receiver snap shares and starters out as of the pregame vintage.
free_sources: No free CFB personnel feed confirmed (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.why: Links availability of specific pass-catchers to team yardage via formation, instead of treating every receiver as interchangeable.

cfb.script_rush_attempts.label: Script-driven team rush attempts including sacks
cfb.script_rush_attempts.mechanism: Expected team rushing attempts as plays times run share given the expected lead, counting sacks as rushing attempts under NCAA statistics.
cfb.script_rush_attempts.rationale: KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT sits in this archetype and counts a team stat, not points; in NCAA statistics a sack is recorded as a rushing attempt with negative yards, so attempts rise with sack-prone offences, and run share rises sharply for leaders.
cfb.script_rush_attempts.measurement: Rush attempts = (plays - dropbacks) + sacks under NCAA convention (sacks and kneels count as rushes). Run share on neutral situations (1st/2nd down, score within 7) per team over the last 10 games decay 0.8, then lead effect from a logistic on plays fitted by score margin (piecewise at +-14), opponent run-defence adjust by opponent rush attempts allowed, shrink with k = 6 games to FBS mean. Add sack rate x expected dropbacks (sack rate shrunk with k = 150 dropbacks). As-of last game; no market input.
free_sources: CFBD plays with play types incl. sacks (free key)
cfb.script_rush_attempts.why: KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT counts team rushing attempts, and KXNCAAFTEAMYDS charges sacks and kneels to rushing; both need the script-driven run-play count.

cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.label: Net yards per play expectation (rush plus pass, sacks included)
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.mechanism: Expected team total yards from plays times net yards per play, built from rushing and passing components under NCAA accounting.
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.rationale: Total yards is plays times yards per play, and under NCAA conventions sack yardage lost is charged to rushing, so net yards per play depends on the sack rate; explosive plays create heavy right tails and yards correlate strongly with pace and script.
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.measurement: Per team: NCAA accounting where sack plays count as rush attempts with negative yards and kneels count as rushes. Expected plays N (from pace inputs), pass share p from script-adjusted attempts; E[yards] = N x [(1-p) x rush_ypa_adj + p x pass_ypa_adj], where rush_ypa includes sack and kneel yardage and pass_ypa excludes sacks (per NCAA pass attempt definition), each opponent-adjusted by the opposing allowed values over the last 10 games with 0.8 decay and k = 6 games shrinkage. Dispersion from historical residuals by bucket. As-of last game.
free_sources: CFBD plays and team stats (free key)
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.why: KXNCAAFTEAMYDS settles on total offense = rushing plus receiving yards with sacks and kneels as negative rushing yards, i.e. plays x net yards per play.

cfb.victory_formation_yardage.label: Victory-formation and end-of-half kneel yardage loss
cfb.victory_formation_yardage.mechanism: Expected negative rushing yardage from quarterback kneels at the end of a half or game, which the KXNCAAFTEAMYDS note charges to the offence's rushing (and so total) yards.
cfb.victory_formation_yardage.rationale: The rules make kneels negative rushing yards, so a team that leads late loses a few yards per kneel series; the loss is near zero for trailing teams and concentrated in the favourite's distribution, slightly shifting rung probabilities near the strike for teams expected to win comfortably; it also lowers rushing attempts' yards per carry.
cfb.victory_formation_yardage.measurement: From play-by-play 2014 onward, classify kneels (play text contains 'kneel' or rush of -1 to -3 yards with zero time-out usage in the final 2:00 of a half while leading or tied); estimate P(kneel series | expected lead at 2:00 of the 4th quarter and of the 2nd quarter), using the team kneel-down rate already defined in cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency as the team-level prior rather than re-estimating it, by logistic fit on the non-market expected margin, and mean yards per kneel series (count of kneels x mean loss, about -1 to -2 yards each). Expected kneel yards = sum over halves of P(series) x mean loss; as-of kickoff.
raw_data: play-by-play: play_type, play_text, yards_gained, period, clock, scores
cfb.victory_formation_yardage.why: Small but rule-specified deduction in KXNCAAFTEAMYDS for the leading team; ignored by gross-yardage models.

cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.label: Touchdowns per scoring trip (drives reaching opponent 40) with type split
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.mechanism: Expected touchdown count from the number of drives reaching scoring range and the touchdown conversion rate, split into rushing, receiving and non-offensive.
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.rationale: All live series count touchdowns, not points: a drive that ends in a field goal produces no TD, so TD count depends on finishing (TD versus FG versus turnover) more than on points; the type split determines TEAMRSHTD and TEAMRECTD.
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.measurement: For each team: trips = drives with a first down at or inside the opponent 40; TD per trip over last 10 games with 0.85 decay, opponent-adjusted by the opponent defence's TD per trip allowed, shrinkage k = 25 trips to the FBS mean; split of TDs by type (rush, pass, other) over 2 seasons with shrinkage k = 30 TDs. Expected team TDs = expected trips x TD per trip; variance from negative binomial with fitted dispersion.
raw_data: drives with start/end field position and result
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.why: TEAMTD, TOTALTD, TEAMRSHTD and TEAMRECTD settle on touchdown counts: expected scoring trips times TD per trip with the rush/pass split is the core count model.

cfb.td_count_dispersion.label: Touchdown count dispersion and tail probabilities
cfb.td_count_dispersion.mechanism: Variance-to-mean ratio of team and game touchdown counts and tail probability of 5+ team rushing or 8+ game touchdowns.
cfb.td_count_dispersion.rationale: Counts like total touchdowns 8+ and rushing touchdowns 5+ sit in the upper tail where a Poisson underestimates the probability because scoring drives cluster in mismatches and shootouts.
cfb.td_count_dispersion.measurement: Fit a negative binomial to game TD counts by expected-total and gap bins from FBS 2014 onward: mean mu(bin) and dispersion r(bin); report P(N >= k) for k in 1..12 with a 95 percent interval from bootstrapped games; shrinkage to pooled dispersion with k = 150 games. For team rushing TD counts fit separately by team style bucket.
free_sources: CFBD games and scoring plays (free key)
raw_data: touchdowns by game, team and type
cfb.td_count_dispersion.why: TOTALTD and TEAMTD ladders sit in the upper tail (8+ game TDs, 5+ rushing TDs) where a Poisson understates probability; the fitted dispersion prices each rung.

cfb.dst_td_propensity.label: Defensive and special-teams touchdown propensity
cfb.dst_td_propensity.mechanism: Probability that a game contains at least one touchdown scored by a defence or special teams, from turnover returns, kick returns and blocked kicks.
cfb.dst_td_propensity.rationale: DST touchdowns require the opposing offence to turn the ball over in a returnable place or special teams to give returns; they depend on interception and fumble rates, return specialists and the rules for kickoff returns, and are rare events with fat tails.
cfb.dst_td_propensity.measurement: Expected DST TDs per team-game = interceptions forced per game x pick-six rate (shrunk k = 40 INTs to the FBS mean) + fumbles forced x return-TD rate + kick/punt return TD rate for the returner + blocked-kick rate, each opponent-adjusted by the opposing offence's turnover rate; game probability = 1 - exp(-lambda_total) with lambda total = sum of both teams. Kickoff rule regime recorded by season. As-of last game.
raw_data: plays with interception, fumble, return, blocked kick and TD flags
cfb.dst_td_propensity.why: KXNCAAFDSTTD settles on at least one defensive or special-teams touchdown by either team, and TOTALTD/FIRSTTDTEAM count them too.

cfb.first_td_race_rate.label: First-touchdown race (hazard and no-touchdown mass)
cfb.first_td_race_rate.mechanism: Rate at which each team scores its first touchdown, including defensive and special-teams touchdowns, and the probability that neither scores in the full game.
cfb.first_td_race_rate.rationale: First team to score a touchdown is a race between two hazards with a deterministic head start for the receiving team on the opening possession, and with a small chance that neither scores (low-scoring game); overtime still counts for this market.
cfb.first_td_race_rate.measurement: From games since 2014, model time to first TD per team as a piecewise-constant hazard by drive index; hazard depends on team TD per trip, drive pace, opening possession order (receive-first adds probability mass at drive 1) and opponent's early defence; shrink to league hazard with k = 10 games; compute P(team A first) = integral; add P(no TD in 60 min + overtime) from low-total regimes (calibrated on FBS history). As-of kickoff with opening possession probability from cfb.opening_poss. Non-offensive and overtime components: add a defensive/special-teams touchdown arrival hazard per possession of the opponent (from cfb.dst_td_propensity) that can fire before any offensive possession ends; the No-team-scores outcome mass = P(no TD in regulation, from the hazards) x [1 - P(tie after 60 minutes, cfb.ot_model) x P(a touchdown in overtime periods 1-2 | tie)], since the contract settles the first touchdown in the full game including overtime.
free_sources: CFBD plays and scoring plays (free key)
raw_data: scoring plays with time and drive index
cfb.first_td_race_rate.why: KXNCAAFFIRSTTDTEAM is a race between the two teams' touchdown arrival processes with a No-TD outcome, priced from first-TD hazard rates.

cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.label: Goal-to-go and short-yardage run/pass mix
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.mechanism: Share of goal-line and short-field plays that are runs (including quarterback sneaks and designed runs) versus passes.
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.rationale: Within the same number of touchdowns, the split between rushing and receiving depends on goal-line play calling: option and power-run offences score rushing touchdowns at close range where spread passing offences score receiving touchdowns, and trailing or leading status shifts the mix.
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.measurement: Compute run share on plays inside the opponent 10 and on 3rd/4th-and-short, by team over 2 seasons with decay 0.5 per season and shrinkage k = 40 plays to the conference mean; add TD conversion rate by type; condition on score state with a logistic model (leading by 14+ increases run share by 0.10-0.15 in the fit). Output expected rushing and receiving TD counts given expected total TDs.
raw_data: plays inside opponent 10 with run/pass and result
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.why: Splits touchdowns into rushing versus receiving for TEAMRSHTD and TEAMRECTD; a fumble-recovery TD is credited to neither.

cfb.pace.reason: Plays per game bound every counting stat, but the single season average hides that tempo changes with score state; the state-dependent version (cfb.state_dependent_pace) is what actually sets how many dropbacks a team gets.

cfb.pass_rate.reason: Pass share is the direct multiplier between plays and receiving yards; keep, but as the script-adjusted pass attempts, since a raw season pass rate is dominated by games that were blowouts one way or the other. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.rush_efficiency.reason: Since the reconciliation added KXNCAAFTEAMYDS, KXNCAAFTEAMRSHTD and KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT, rushing yards per carry, line yards and stuff rate set half of total offense (stage s9) and the goal-line rushing finish; the earlier IRRELEVANT verdict was written for receiving yards only.

cfb.pass_efficiency.reason: Opponent-adjusted yards per attempt and PPA per dropback directly generate receiving yards; sack rate in the label is a different outcome (sack yards count against rushing under NCAA rules and do not subtract from receiving yards).

cfb.run_defense.reason: The opposing front sets rushing yards allowed for KXNCAAFTEAMYDS and rushing-touchdown finishing for KXNCAAFTEAMRSHTD, and pushes the offence toward passing for receiving yards; secondary to own rushing efficiency, used as the opponent adjustment in stage s9.

cfb.secondary_coverage.reason: Opposing explosive-pass-allowed and yards per attempt allowed set yards per completion; strongest for deep-passing offences, so it should be used in a product with the team's average depth of target.

cfb.pass_rush.reason: Pressure converts attempts into incompletions and throwaways (lower completions) but sacks do not count as negative receiving yards; effect runs through completion rate and yards per attempt, not through a sack term.

cfb.havoc.reason: Opponent tackles for loss and sacks subtract from KXNCAAFTEAMYDS and forced fumbles feed KXNCAAFDSTTD return touchdowns, but the sack component is carried by cfb.qb_sack_proneness and the return component by cfb.dst_td_propensity, so havoc is context, not a staged input.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: Fumble-recovery and interception luck regresses, which matters slightly for KXNCAAFDSTTD (fewer returnable turnovers than a lucky season suggests) and for drives lost; the effect is carried by cfb.dst_td_propensity shrinkage and is negligible for yardage and offensive touchdown rungs.

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Defined as the split of the game total and spread, i.e. a price-derived expected score; it is a benchmark for the expected game script, to be replaced here by a rating-based expected margin that is not a function of any quote.

cfb.script.reason: Expected score state drives pass attempts (trailing teams throw and snap faster); needs to be built from rating gap and coach tendencies, and label's 'garbage-time behaviour' mixes two different effects. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind above roughly 15 mph and precipitation cut deep passing and completion rate; forecast vintage is correct, but the effect depends on the team's average depth of target.

cfb.player_stat_variance.reason: Label says player stat shape but this contract is a team aggregate; the useful content is the team-level dispersion of receiving yards (right-skewed, explosive-play driven), which the threshold probability depends on.

m.rules_text.reason: Settlement wording is decisive here: overtime periods 1 and 2 count, successful 2-point conversions do not, and the 48-hour postponement clause applies; versioning matters because stat definitions can change by season.

m.stat_source_mismatch.reason: Not pregame-knowable but needed to build labels: the official provider can differ from CFBD or ESPN box scores by a few yards on lateral and review plays, which matters near the strike.

cfb.corr.reason: Correlation of passing volume, game total and period script is needed for joint use with other ladders, but for a single team yardage rung it only matters through shared expected plays.

cfb.skill_avail.reason: A missing WR1 or tight end moves yards per target more than volume (targets redistribute); labelled primary but for a team aggregate the quarterback matters more than any one receiver.

cfb.injuries.reason: No official college injury feed; as an untimestamped concept it adds nothing beyond skill_avail and qb status, which are the specific absence terms.

cfb.player_usage.reason: Target and carry share allocate yards among players, but this contract sums the whole team; usage only matters as the replacement-receiver quality term, which skill_avail already approximates.

interactions.mechanism: A team's dropback response to being a big underdog depends on its own pass-rate slope and tempo: an air-raid, up-tempo offence converts a deficit into many extra pass snaps, while a run-first or slow team under the same deficit still burns clock; so extra receiving yards from the trailing script appear only where pass_rate slope and pace are high.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress dropbacks on the SP+ expected-margin gap interacted with the team neutral pass-rate-over-expected slope and seconds per play; compare the gap coefficient across pass-rate-slope terciles.

interactions.mechanism: An offence that lives on deep completions has yards per completion multiplied by the opposing safeties' explosive-allowed rate, while a short-pass offence is almost insensitive to it; the product, not the sum, determines the right tail above a high strike.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit yards per completion on depth-of-target x opponent explosive rate and compare to an additive model on held-out games.

interactions.mechanism: Sustained wind above about 15 mph reduces deep-ball completion and shifts calls to the run, but the cut-in only appears past the threshold and is largest for vertical offences; mild weather has no effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team receiving yards in games with forecast wind above 15 mph against calm games, split by depth-of-target tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Loss of a top receiver costs more yards in a four-wide scheme (where he is on the field for 90 percent of snaps and targets concentrate) than in a heavy-set scheme where targets spread across tight ends and backs; a backup quarterback shrinks the yards per target of every remaining receiver at once.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the yards-per-attempt drop when a top-2 receiver or the starting quarterback is absent, split by 3+ WR snap-share tercile.

interactions.mechanism: A team's rushing-touchdown count is its touchdown total times the share credited to runs inside the ten; a designed-run quarterback raises that share, and the effect is largest for offences that reach the red zone often, so the 5+ rushing-touchdown rung depends on the product rather than on either factor.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team rushing touchdowns on expected touchdowns, goal-to-go run share and quarterback designed-run rate with their product term; compare fit of additive and multiplicative forms.

interactions.mechanism: Rushing attempts respond to the non-market expected lead with a hinge: below a two-score expected lead the count tracks tempo, above it clock-killing run calls add attempts while total snaps fall, so tempo and expected margin offset each other in heavy favourites.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit attempts on expected margin bins with and without a pace interaction; test a slope change near a 14-point expected margin.

interactions.mechanism: Under the KXNCAAFTEAMYDS accounting a sack subtracts yards from total offense, so the cost of a sack-prone quarterback scales with dropback volume: a trailing team that passes 45 times loses far more net yards to sacks than a leading team passing 20 times, and the same quarterback pulls total yards down more in chase scripts.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team total yards residuals on sack rate x dropbacks versus additive sack rate and dropbacks terms; compare held-out error by expected-margin bin.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: pass share rises about 10 points when trailing by two scores and falls sharply when leading by 21+
nonlinearities.why: Dropback volume is the main driver of the right tail and responds non-linearly to lead size, so a linear score-state term understates both extremes.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy right tail in yards per completion
nonlinearities.why: A few 50+ yard completions can add 100 yards; threshold probabilities near the mean are sensitive to the tail share of explosive plays rather than the mean yards per attempt.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating: extra snaps convert into pass attempts at a falling rate as clock-burning kicks in
nonlinearities.why: Beyond about 75 snaps the added plays are disproportionately runs in clock-killing situations, so yards do not scale with tempo one-for-one.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise-convex in expected margin with hinges near -10 and +14 to +21
nonlinearities.why: Dropbacks rise faster than linearly as the expected deficit grows (trailing teams pass and hurry), and flatten or fall for large favourites that run the clock; the hinge sits in the SP+ margin, not in a second input, so it is a single-input response shape.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance above Poisson that grows with expected touchdowns; fat right tail for 8+ combined
nonlinearities.why: High touchdown rungs are reached in mismatch and shootout regimes where scoring drives cluster, so a Poisson with the right mean understates the tail probability of 8+ total or 5+ team touchdowns.

nonlinearities.shape: Step in expected late lead: near zero when trailing, a fixed few-yard loss once the team is likely to lead at the two-minute mark
nonlinearities.why: A kneel series occurs only when the offence leads with the clock nearly out, so the deduction switches on as P(lead late) crosses roughly one half rather than growing smoothly with margin.
