contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFTOTAL settles YES if the two teams collectively score more than the half-point strike (for example over 25.5 for Nebraska vs Illinois) in the game; the title says Full Game but the sampled rules text does not state whether overtime points are included. A postponed game that begins within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official final result; if it does not start within 48 hours the market resolves to a fair price. Rungs are strict greater-than on .5 strikes, so there is no push. KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE (moved here by the reconciliation) settles YES if any Division I game in the 2026 regular season, overtime included, has more than 144.5 combined points; conference championship, bowl and CFP games are excluded, so it is a season maximum over several hundred FBS and FCS game totals.

rules_evidence.quote: If the teams collectively score more than 25.5 points in the Nebraska vs Illinois college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike is strictly greater than a half-point number on combined points, so settlement requires 26 or more total points.

rules_evidence.quote: Full Game: Over 25.5 points scored
rules_evidence.establishes: This is the market title, not rules text: it labels the market a full-game total but establishes nothing about overtime, which the rules text is silent on.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: Short postponements keep the market open; beyond 48 hours the same text says fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: If there is a Division I game (including overtime) with over 144.5 total points scored in the 2026 college football regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: HIGHSCORE is a season-maximum event over every Division I regular-season game with overtime points counted, unlike KXNCAAFTOTAL whose text is silent on overtime.

rules_evidence.quote: Conference championship games, Bowl games, and College Football Playoff games are not part of the regular season.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postseason games cannot trigger HIGHSCORE, so exposure ends with the last regular-season weekend.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime treatment is unstated in the sampled KXNCAAFTOTAL text, whereas KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE says 'including overtime' (and the sibling 4Q total in quarter_and_half_totals says excluding); the Full Game title suggests inclusion but this is not verified.
The sampled rung of 25.5 for a Power-conference game is an extreme low rung of a ladder; the ladder runs from low to high strikes and each rung is a nested event.
Cancelled or non-started games after 48 hours resolve to a fair price, not to NO, so weather cancellations do not pay the under.
Totals have mass at certain sums (3, 6, 7, 10, 13, 14...) so the distance between consecutive .5 rungs carries very different probability.
FBS vs FCS games are included in the series with very high totals possible when a large mismatch occurs.

KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE counts overtime explicitly and spans every Division I game (FBS and FCS, including FCS-FCS games); whether a game between a Division I team and a non-Division I opponent counts as 'a Division I game' is not stated.

Since the 2021 overtime rule (two-point attempts only from the third overtime) long overtimes add about 2-4 points per extra period, so pre-2021 multi-overtime totals overstate today's extreme-total tail for HIGHSCORE.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final result per the Kalshi wording; the stats provider is not named in the sampled text, so the final score as published by the NCAA or the schools is assumed.

mechanism.summary: Total points = number of possessions x expected points per possession summed over both offences, plus non-offensive scores, with overtime as an optional extra if the contract counts it. Possessions come from tempo (seconds per play), run-pass mix and clock management, and are shared between the two teams so the slower side dominates; points per possession come from opponent-adjusted efficiency, finishing (touchdown versus field goal), field position and special teams. Late information (quarterback, weather) and game script (blowouts compress the favourite, garbage time adds underdog points) shape the distribution, which is right-skewed with key-number lumps. The HIGHSCORE series is a different functional of the same per-game process: the maximum of several hundred regular-season game totals, governed by the extreme right tail (mismatch shootouts, multi-overtime games) rather than by the centre of any one game.

stages.name: Possession count from joint tempo
stages.description: A game contains roughly 22 to 26 combined possessions in modern FBS. The count is set by both offences' seconds per play, plays per drive, run share and the clock regime (running clock after first downs since 2023), and by the lead size late; a slow ball-control team pulls a fast team's possessions down, so tempo combines harmonically rather than additively.
stages.distribution: Near-Gaussian count with SD of about 2 possessions; right tail in shootouts with turnovers and quick scores.

stages.name: Points per possession for each offence
stages.description: For each side, expected points per drive combine ability to move the ball (opponent-adjusted success and explosive plays), the quality of the opposing defence, starting field position and the finishing rate inside the 40. Finishing includes the touchdown versus field-goal choice and kicker range, and so the same yardage yields different points.
stages.distribution: Per-drive points are a 0/3/7 mixture; the sum over ~12 drives gives a total with SD of roughly 13 points, right-skewed by explosive drives.

stages.name: Late information on personnel and conditions
stages.description: Quarterback identity, kicker status and weather are confirmed late and move the total more than any rating. Wind and rain reduce passing and field-goal range but only at open stadiums; temperature and dome status matter at the margins. Officials contribute a small amount through penalty rate.
stages.distribution: Discrete shocks (QB change) plus continuous weather effects; weather impact is threshold-like in wind speed.

stages.name: Script compression and non-offensive scores
stages.description: When a favourite builds a large lead, starters leave and the clock runs, trimming its late scoring, while the underdog gets garbage-time possessions; the net depends on the coach. Defensive and special-teams touchdowns add points without an offensive drive and add dispersion; they are mostly luck with a small skill component.
stages.distribution: Mixture: the central mass is truncated by script compression, while rare 6-8 point lumps (return touchdowns) fatten the right tail.

stages.name: Overtime and contract definition
stages.description: If regulation ends tied (about 5 to 8 percent of games) overtime adds points: a two-possession period starting at the 25-yard line with about 4 to 5 expected points per side; whether those count is not stated in the sampled rules, which changes the probability of crossing a rung near the median by a few percentage points. Conditional input set: if overtime counts in KXNCAAFTOTAL, the total needs cfb.ot_model (P(tie after 60 minutes) from the margin and total distribution, overtime possession scoring, number of overtimes; the same inputs are defined in the overtime archetype as cfb.regulation_tie_curve and cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate); if it does not, the series is regulation-only and cfb.ot_model drops out.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli tie event with discrete additive points in 3/6/7/8 lattice.

stages.name: Season maximum over all Division I game totals (HIGHSCORE)
stages.description: HIGHSCORE resolves on the largest single-game total of the regular season, so the quantity is an upper order statistic: the per-game exceedance probability above 144.5 is tiny and is driven by fast-tempo, weak-defence pairings and by overtime, then compounded across all remaining Division I games. Exposure (games left, maximum already observed) matters as much as the tail shape, and the modern two-point overtime format caps how much a long overtime adds.
stages.distribution: Generalised Pareto tail above roughly 95 points per game; season union probability 1 - prod(1 - p_g) over remaining games, with a multi-overtime mixture component.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted efficiency of both offences and defences; talent composite is in the catalog but not attached.

opponent_matchup.note: Style pairing and defensive havoc against the opposing line and protection.

availability_news.note: Late quarterback confirmation and bowl opt-outs; other injuries rely on catalog inputs not attached here.

coaching_scheme.note: Scheme and lead-management tendencies; fourth-down aggression is untested for totals.

efficiency_conversion.note: Moving the ball versus finishing; field-goal conversion.

distribution_variance.note: Right-skewed total with lumps at 3/7 and a return-touchdown tail. HIGHSCORE uses the season-maximum tail (cfb.season_max_total_tail).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, lookahead, rivalry and conference-championship stakes shift effort and tempo but nothing in this archetype's inputs captures them for totals; their effect size on totals is unmeasured.

officiating_rules.note: Crew penalty tendency and the season clock regime.

settlement_contract.note: Strict greater-than, overtime inclusion unresolved, 48-hour postponement clause.

cfb.expected_possessions.label: Expected combined possessions per game
cfb.expected_possessions.mechanism: Number of drives in the game computed from both teams' seconds per drive rather than from averaged plays.
cfb.expected_possessions.rationale: Total points scale with the number of possessions, roughly 22-26 combined in modern FBS games. Seconds per play, plays per drive and run/pass mix interact: two slow teams produce fewer possessions than the average of their individual paces implies, because clock-killing drives are shared.
cfb.expected_possessions.measurement: Per team: mean drive duration d (seconds, excluding drives that end a half or occur in garbage time) over the last 10 games with weight 0.8 per game back, shrunk to the FBS mean with k = 5 games. Expected combined drives = (T_eff) / (0.5 x (d_A_own + d_B_allowed + d_B_own + d_A_allowed)/2) where T_eff = 3600 seconds minus mean untimed seconds (stoppages and halftime excluded) fitted on the season clock regime, with the clock regime as a covariate and no-huddle rate as a regressor, not a fixed +1. Report mean and SD fitted on residuals. As-of last completed game.
free_sources: CFBD drives (start time, duration, plays; free key)
raw_data: drive table with start/end clock, plays, yards, result
cfb.expected_possessions.why: Replaces the average-of-paces approach with the structural number of scoring trials, the strongest single driver of a game total.

cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.label: Points per scoring opportunity (drives crossing opponent 40)
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.mechanism: Average points on drives that reach the opponent 40 or closer, opponent-adjusted, separating finishing from moving the ball.
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.rationale: A team can have strong PPA and still score few points if it settles for field goals; conversely, strong finishers outperform yardage. Scoring-trip efficiency regresses less than red-zone TD rate because it pools more drives and includes field-goal-range situations.
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.measurement: Per team: sum of points on drives with first down inside the opponent 40 divided by number of such drives (over 10 games, 0.85 per-game decay), adjusted by opponent allowed value and by kicker field-goal value; shrink with k = 25 drives toward conference mean. Output mean and SE; combine own offence and opposing defence by an additive deviation model.
raw_data: drive start/end yard line, result, points
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.why: Splits efficiency into moving and finishing, important because totals depend on 3-versus-7 outcomes rather than yardage.

cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.label: Defensive and special-teams touchdown rate
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.mechanism: Rate at which a team scores on interception returns, fumble returns, kickoff and punt returns, and blocked kicks, and allows them.
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.rationale: These touchdowns add 6-8 points without using an offensive possession, are partly skill (returners, ball-hawks) and mostly luck, and fatten the right tail of the total. The market's total rarely prices them separately.
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.measurement: For each team: defensive plus special-teams touchdowns scored and allowed per game over 2 seasons with 0.5 season decay, shrunk with k = 12 games toward the FBS mean per team-game (to be measured, plausibly 0.1 to 0.2); add a return-specialist indicator from kick returner yards over expected. Output expected points = 7 x rate (own) + 7 x rate allowed by opponent minus offence replaced.
raw_data: plays with type: interception TD, fumble TD, kickoff/punt return TD, blocked kick
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.why: Fat-tail component of the total not captured by drive-based efficiency.

cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.label: Stadium wind exposure and forecast bias
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.mechanism: Translates a forecast wind speed into expected on-field wind by stadium (open bowl, enclosed, dome, orientation).
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.rationale: A 20 mph forecast at a closed or dome stadium is irrelevant while the same forecast at an open lakeside stadium cuts passing and field-goal range materially; the forecast vintage alone is not predictive without the exposure factor.
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.measurement: Per stadium: roof type (open, retractable, dome), historical ratio of observed on-field wind (from nearest airport station via NOAA ISD or Meteostat) to forecast at issue 6 hours out, fitted by month over 8 seasons; exposure = ratio x forecast. Outputs adjusted wind in mph and an indicator of >15 mph. Apply only at kickoff plus 3 hours.
raw_data: venue table with roof, orientation, lat/long
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.why: Makes the weather vintage input usable for totals by linking forecast to actual game conditions in the specific building.

cfb.season_max_total_tail.label: Season maximum-total tail model across all Division I games
cfb.season_max_total_tail.mechanism: KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE settles on the single largest combined score over every Division I regular-season game including overtime, so it is an extreme-value quantity of roughly 850 game totals, driven by FBS-vs-FCS mismatches, multi-overtime games and pace-and-defence-poor matchups.
cfb.season_max_total_tail.rationale: The rung 144.5 sits far in the tail; the maximum total is governed by rare pairings (two fast, weak defences, or a long overtime game where each overtime adds up to 8 points) rather than the mean total. A Gaussian game-total model badly understates it, so the tail needs an empirical or Poisson-compound fit with a separate overtime-length component.
cfb.season_max_total_tail.measurement: Collect the maximum regular-season Division I total per season 2005-2025 (FBS and FCS games, including overtime) and the full set of per-game totals above 100. Fit a generalised Pareto tail to game totals above 95 points with a threshold chosen by mean-excess plot; scale the exceedance rate by the number of games (about 850 FBS-involved and more with FCS-FCS games) and add a multi-overtime component: P(k overtimes) from cfb.ot_model, with 2-point-only possessions after the second overtime. Output P(max total > K) for K in 120..160 and the number of games expected above 100. As-of date uses only completed seasons plus current-season games already played.
free_sources: CFBD games (FBS and some FCS, free key)
raw_data: final scores with overtime periods by game 2005 onward
cfb.season_max_total_tail.why: KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE settles on whether any Division I regular-season game (overtime included) exceeds the strike, an extreme-value quantity over all game totals that a one-game total model cannot price.

cfb.pace.reason: Plays per game from both teams is the volume term of the total, but a season average ignores that the slower team and the score state control the clock; it should feed an expected-possessions computation rather than be added to the opponent's value.

cfb.drives.reason: Drives per game is the unit of scoring trials and is more direct than plays; the label mixes drives, explosiveness and finishing drives into one, which should be separated (possessions, points per drive, drive success).

cfb.pass_rate.reason: Pass share affects clock use and variance (incompletions stop the clock) but is already inside pace and offense_style; marginal value is small once drive duration is modelled. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.clock_rules.reason: The clock-rule regime changes only between seasons (running clock after first downs, 2023 onwards), so within a season it is constant; it is a training-set stratifier and a level shift, not a game-level predictor, and was mislabelled secondary.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Points per drive for each side flows from opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency; PPA is a model-based quantity, so it should be paired with a direct points-per-drive from actual scoring to keep a non-modelled check.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Opposing defensive efficiency suppresses points per drive; conference connectivity makes G5 defence values noisy, so a shrinkage prior (cross_conf_calibration) should be applied before use.

cfb.success_explosiveness.reason: Success rate versus explosiveness changes drive length and the variance of the total at the same mean PPA; useful mostly for the width of the distribution.

cfb.redzone.reason: Red-zone TD-versus-FG rate shifts points per trip but regresses heavily on 30 or so trips per season; use shrunk expected points per scoring opportunity instead of a raw rate.

cfb.havoc.reason: Havoc creates negative plays and short fields, hitting both teams' drive outcomes; partly duplicate with def_ppa success rate, retained for turnover/short-field effect.

cfb.field_pos.reason: Average starting field position and special-teams quality shift points per drive; punt and kickoff-return strength are stable enough to carry weight.

cfb.kicker.reason: Kicker range and accuracy decide how many stalled drives become 3 points and shape key-number mass in the total; kicker change is a late news item.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: Quarterback identity affects both efficiency and tempo; for totals the change in pace and in explosive-play rate is as important as the efficiency shift.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind, precipitation and temperature are the best-known late-information drivers of totals; the forecast vintage is correct but the stadium-specific wind exposure (open bowl, closed, dome) is missing.

cfb.offense_style.reason: Option, air-raid and RPO labels overlap with pace and pass_rate; keep as a categorical regime to catch atypical plays-per-game that rating-based models mispredict. Reverification: the catalog measurement uses style-specific residuals of spread/total, which are residuals around market lines (the same defect as cfb.score_resid); only residuals against own non-market ratings are admissible, the line-residual version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Starter removal lowers favourite late scoring while the underdog gets garbage-time points; net effect on totals is ambiguous and coach-specific, so it is secondary to the pregame mismatch regime. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.officials.reason: Penalty-heavy crews lengthen drives and add replays, worth a fraction of a point to the total; weak but real, and crew assignments are announced late in the week for most conferences.

cfb.score_resid.reason: Residuals of totals around lines are market-derived by construction; they calibrate the benchmark's error shape but cannot serve as a fundamentals input.

m.external_lines.reason: Sharp sportsbook totals embed weather, lineup and sharp money; use as the comparator after de-vig, never as an input to a model claiming independent information.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Monotonicity and kinks across total rungs (the quotes at 25.5, 45.5, 55.5...) are a diagnostic of stale quotes and of the market's implied distribution, not a cause of the total.

cfb.opt_out_departures.reason: Relevant to bowl and CFP totals where opt-outs lower scoring versus regular-season ratings; absent for regular-season games.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price history is the market's own output; it measures when information was absorbed (useful for timing studies and closing-line value) but is not a cause of the game total outcome and must not enter a fundamentals model.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread govern whether a game total edge is tradable, not whether the event occurs; keep for execution and sizing, not as an outcome input.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule changes net edge on game total contracts (largest near 50c) but has no causal link to the result; an execution parameter, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe liquidity and price reliability for game total quotes; useful to weight benchmark trust, irrelevant to the outcome process.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades show informed flow and fill realism for game total contracts; it is market microstructure used to validate fills, not a determinant of the outcome.

m.lifecycle.reason: Open/close/halt/postponement events matter here because the 48-hour postponement clause converts a delayed game total market to a fair-price settlement; needed to define the information set and void handling.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Labels must use the official settled total and the contract's overtime treatment; not available pregame but essential to build correct training targets.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: Turnovers create short fields and drive-ending events; regression-to-expected recovers true offensive efficiency, but the effect on totals is smaller than on sides because both teams' luck partially offsets.

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on cfb.blowout_management x cfb.team_total_split x cfb.score_resid: Blowout management x spread: large spreads lower the favorite's second-half scoring but raise underdog garbage) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.ot_model.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s5; stage s6) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.season_ot_exposure.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s6) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: Possession count depends on run share through the clock rules: a run-heavy team that keeps the clock moving after first downs shortens the game for both sides, and a pass-heavy opponent cannot restore the possessions because incompletions stop the clock only for its own snaps; so tempo of the faster team matters less when the slower team has a high run share.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress realised total possessions on each team seconds per play interacted with the combined run share and season clock regime; check whether the tempo coefficient shrinks as combined run share rises.

interactions.mechanism: Wind above roughly 15 mph at an open stadium reduces both deep passing and field-goal range beyond 40 yards; the cut in total is minimal below the threshold and then steep, and is amplified when the kicker is already marginal.
interactions.how_to_test: Bucket games by adjusted on-field wind and kicker long-range accuracy; compare average total versus ratings-implied total.

interactions.mechanism: In a one-sided game the total follows a different regime: the leader's scoring drops but the trailing team's garbage-time possessions and return touchdowns add points; whether the total goes up or down depends on the coach's pull point and on trailing-team passing.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the total residual for games with pre-game rating gap above 21 split by coach pull-point tercile and by trailing offence pass rate.

interactions.mechanism: A high-explosiveness offence facing a high-havoc defence produces many failed drives but occasional long scores; the mean total changes little while its variance and right tail increase, which matters for high rungs.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the variance of totals by explosiveness x havoc bucket; test with quantile regression at the 80th and 90th percentiles.

interactions.mechanism: A quarterback change lowers both efficiency and tempo (backups run a simpler script), so the effect on the total is the product of a smaller points-per-drive and fewer possessions, and it is bigger for up-tempo offences.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast pre/post-change totals for teams by tempo tercile, controlling for opponent and weather.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold near 15 mph on-field wind, steep beyond 20 mph
nonlinearities.why: Passing and kicking degrade slowly until wind affects the ball's flight, then drop steeply; a linear wind term misprices both calm and gale games.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in count but with SD that grows with tempo; total points concave in possessions at high counts
nonlinearities.why: Extra possessions are not equal: late extra possessions occur in blowouts or garbage time with lower scoring rates, so marginal points per added possession declines.

nonlinearities.shape: Lumpy 0/3/7 per trip with convex value of touchdown conversion near the goal line
nonlinearities.why: Moving a trip from field goal to touchdown adds 4 points, and the probability gain is concentrated near the 10-yard line; small efficiency shifts have large point effects when concentrated there.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFOT settles YES if at least one overtime period is played in the named game (strike 1); an overtime period counts as played once it commences, via a legal snap in the first two overtimes or a first two-point attempt from the third overtime onward, and once started counts in full whether or not both teams get a possession. KXNCAAFMOSTOT settles YES if any Division I game in the 2026 regular season goes to at least 9 overtime periods. A game postponed but started within 48 hours stays open and uses the official final result; outside that window the markets resolve to a fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: An overtime period counts as played once it commences, via a legal snap (in the first two overtimes) or a first two-point attempt (in the third overtime and onward).
rules_evidence.establishes: Period counting is event-based: a started period counts even if the game ends on the first possession, and OT 3+ periods are two-point attempts.

rules_evidence.quote: If there is a Division I game that goes to 9+ overtime periods in the 2026 college football regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: The season-extreme contract covers every Division I game (FBS and FCS) in the regular season, strike 9 with greater-or-equal construction.

rules_evidence.quote: If at least 1 overtime period is played in the Illinois vs UCLA college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: Per-game contract is the indicator that the game was tied after regulation (overtime period one commenced).

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNCAAFOT is equivalent to regulation tie; KXNCAAFMOSTOT is an aggregate over all Division I games with a rule-regime change at the third overtime (alternating two-point attempts), so the per-period survival is not constant.
A period counts as played once started even if the game ends on the first snap of that period, so a sudden-death result in period k still counts k periods.
Overtime periods scheduled but never started do not count, which matters only for weather suspensions or ties after curfew; the rules do not say how a suspended overtime is treated.

KXNCAAFMOSTOT primary text scopes the market to 'the 2026 college football regular season', and the sibling HIGHSCORE rules state conference championship, bowl and CFP games are not part of the regular season, so conference championship games are reasonably excluded; the sampled MOSTOT text is truncated and how a game halted by weather during overtime counts is still not addressed.
The 9+ strike is greater-or-equal on count of periods; a 9-overtime game with the ninth period commenced counts, even if the ninth ends the game on the first snap.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game records (final box score with periods) as reported by the NCAA or the participating schools; Kalshi text does not name a provider for these two series.

mechanism.summary: Overtime happens if and only if the game is tied after four quarters, so P(OT) is the point mass of the regulation margin distribution at exactly zero: roughly the margin density at zero (large when teams are evenly matched and the total is low) adjusted for the scoring lattice, plus an excess created by late-game decisions to tie rather than win. How many periods follow is a separate renewal process: each period from the 25-yard line ends tied only if both teams score the same, with a rule change at the third overtime to alternating two-point attempts, so the count of periods is nearly geometric and the 9+ strike is a long-tail event across hundreds of games in the season.

stages.name: Regulation margin distribution near zero
stages.description: The final regulation margin has centre equal to the expected rating gap and spread equal to the sum of game-level noise and rating uncertainty; the tie probability is the mass at exactly zero, which falls roughly Gaussianly with the absolute gap and is highest when the gap is within three points. Fewer possessions or lower totals reduce the margin SD and therefore raise the mass at zero for close matchups.
stages.distribution: Point mass of a discrete lattice, approximately density at 0 times lattice factor; peaks at zero gap and decays like exp(-gap^2/(2 sigma^2)).

stages.name: Scoring lattice and low-scoring conditions
stages.description: Points arrive as 3, 6, 7 and 8 (and occasionally 2), so some margins are far more reachable than others; field-goal-heavy games produce ties more easily because both teams accumulate multiples of three. Wind and rain make scoring lower and lumpier, and kickers with limited range convert drives to threes.
stages.distribution: Lumpy discrete distribution with elevated mass on margins reachable by equal numbers of three-point scores; weather lowers the total and raises lumpiness.

stages.name: End-of-regulation decisions that create or avoid ties
stages.description: In the last two minutes the team trailing by three can kick the tying field goal, a team trailing by eight needs a touchdown and a two-point conversion, and a team with the ball in a tie may kneel into overtime. These choices put extra mass at zero relative to a smooth margin density and differ by coach.
stages.distribution: Binary decisions at specific score and clock states; excess mass at tie created by coach-specific decision rules.

stages.name: Overtime period renewal process
stages.description: Once in overtime, each period gives each team a possession from the 25-yard line; the period is tied if both score the same number of points (both touchdown with equal conversion, both field goal, both none). Scoring probabilities per possession are far higher than ordinary drives, so a tie after period one is the exception, giving a decay by period with a modest per-period continuation probability.
stages.distribution: Geometric-like renewal with continuation probability depending on team scoring rates, roughly a quarter to a third per period in early periods (to be fitted).

stages.name: Rule regime change and season-extreme aggregation
stages.description: From the third overtime periods are single alternating two-point attempts, so each period ends tied only if both succeed or both fail, near one half; reaching nine periods requires six consecutive such ties after two ordinary overtimes. Across several hundred games the contract is a rare-event union, so exposure (games remaining, maximum already seen) matters as much as per-game probability.
stages.distribution: Piecewise geometric survival with a regime break at period 3; season-level union probability 1-(1-q)^N for a very small q.

talent_strength.note: Only the absolute non-market rating gap (SP+ or own rating) matters for the tie curve; market ratings are BENCHMARK_ONLY and removed from the input list.

opponent_matchup.note: Overtime incidence depends on the margin distribution and on both teams' scoring rates from the 25, which is carried by ot_possession_scoring_rate; no separate matchup structure beyond those rates is justified for an event decided by margin equal to zero.

role_personnel.note: Kicker quality drives tying field goals and OT field-goal outcomes; quarterback and others enter through expected margin.

availability_news.note: Availability matters only through the margin mean, margin SD and expected total that feed the tie curve (a quarterback change or late scratch widens the SD and lowers the total); cfb.qb_status_pit is wired into stage s1 through the expected-margin inputs.

coaching_scheme.note: End-of-game decision tendencies create or avoid ties.

environment.note: Wind and rain lower totals and make scoring lumpier.

game_context_script.note: Late-game states are where ties are created (kneel-to-overtime, last-possession decisions); blowouts remove the event but cfb.blowout_management is WEAK and not wired.

pace_volume.note: Possession count sets margin SD; season exposure counts games remaining.

efficiency_conversion.note: Scoring probabilities in overtime and two-point conversion rate.

distribution_variance.note: Point mass at zero margin on the scoring lattice, set by the regulation tie curve and possession-count variance.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry and standings stakes alter the margin mean slightly but do not specifically produce ties; the incremental effect would be below the sampling noise of roughly fifty overtime games a year.

officiating_rules.note: Overtime rules (25-yard start, two-point alternation from the third period) and their version by season.

settlement_contract.note: Period-counting rule read from the sampled rules; regular-season scope for MOSTOT unconfirmed.

cfb.regulation_tie_curve.label: Regulation tie probability curve from non-market expected margin and total
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.mechanism: Empirical P(margin = 0 after four quarters) as a function of absolute expected margin and expected total points.
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.rationale: A tie is a point mass on a lumpy lattice: the probability is roughly the margin density at zero adjusted for the fact that football scores come in 3, 6, 7, 8 and so ties occur preferentially at combined patterns that are reachable by both sides. The curve is peaked at zero gap and decays quickly, and the expected total changes the margin SD.
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.measurement: From all FBS games since 2005 (about 15,000 games: roughly 750 per season over 21 seasons), fit logistic/GAM of tie indicator on |expected margin| (from SP+ or own rating, not market) and expected total with monotone smoothing; bucket |gap| in 2-point bins (0-2, 2-4, ... 14+) and expected total in 8-point bins; shrink bins to pooled curve with prior strength 200 games. Evaluate as-of kickoff. Output P(tie) with 95 percent interval; for FCS fit separately.
free_sources: CFBD games with period line scores (free key)
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.why: Tie incidence is the entire target of KXNCAAFOT and the entry condition for KXNCAAFMOSTOT; direct estimation from non-market axes avoids circularity with the price.

cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.label: End-of-regulation decision profile
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.mechanism: How often a coach settles for a tie (kneel, kick the tying field goal) versus plays for the win in the last two minutes.
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.rationale: Tied games are created or avoided in the final minutes: a trailing team that kicks a field goal to tie creates overtime, and a team with the ball tied with 40 seconds left may kneel. Coaches differ systematically, so two matchups with equal margin distributions can differ in tie incidence.
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.measurement: Situations: Q4 plays with clock <= 2:00 where the offence trails by 1-3 (FG ties), trails by 8 (needs TD+2), or the score is tied. Fit a logistic model on 2014-2025 of aggressive choice (go for TD / pass on 4th, no kneel) on score diff, time, timeouts, field position, down, distance. For each head coach compute observed minus predicted aggressive rate over the last 3 seasons, shrunk with k = 15 situations to the conference mean; z-score = shrunk excess / SE. Coach change resets to coordinator plus career data prior. As-of previous Sunday.
free_sources: CFBD plays with clock and play_type (free key)
raw_data: play-by-play final 2:00 of Q4 with down, distance, score, timeouts, clock
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.why: The existing coaching input measures tenure and scheme but not the one decision that converts a close game into overtime.

cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.label: Overtime possession scoring rates (touchdown, field goal, none)
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.mechanism: Per-team probabilities of touchdown, field goal or no score from the 25-yard line, offence and defence, opponent-adjusted.
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.rationale: Overtime ends when one team outscores the other in a period; probability a period ends tied depends on the pair of scoring outcome distributions, and overtime offence differs from ordinary offence (short field, no clock, kicker at 42 yards).
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.measurement: Per team: P(TD), P(FG), P(none) on first-and-10 from the 25 with no clock pressure, estimated from non-OT drives starting inside the opponent 30 with shrinkage k = 20 drives plus actual OT possessions with weight 3; opponent-adjust by the same quantity for defences. Period tie probability = sum over outcomes of own x opponent matched scores (TD-TD with equal conversion, FG-FG, none-none). Compute as-of date.
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.why: Sets the conditional probability of a second and later overtime period, which compounds geometrically into the 9+ period contract.

cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.label: Two-point conversion success rate for the alternating-attempt overtimes
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.mechanism: Team probability of converting a two-point attempt from the 3-yard line, offence and defence, used from the third overtime.
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.rationale: From the third overtime onward periods are single two-point attempts; a period ends tied whenever both teams convert or both fail, so the per-period tie chance is p_a p_b + (1 - p_a)(1 - p_b), close to one half for any plausible p, which keeps the process nearly memoryless and makes 9+ periods a power of about one half.
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.measurement: Per team: successful two-point attempts divided by attempts, offence and defence, over 3 seasons with beta prior at league mean of roughly 0.47-0.50 (to be estimated) and prior strength 25 attempts; use goal-to-go 3-yard plays with 2 or fewer yards to go as proxy where attempts are few. Combine as p_a = (off_a + (1 - def_b)) / 2. As-of date.
free_sources: CFBD plays: two-point conversion play types (free key)
raw_data: two-point attempts with result and play type
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.why: Only the rule regime of OT 3+ makes 9+ periods possible, and its per-period tie probability depends on exactly this quantity.

cfb.season_ot_exposure.label: Season overtime exposure (games remaining and current maximum)
cfb.season_ot_exposure.mechanism: Number of remaining Division I games in the regular season and the maximum overtime periods already seen.
cfb.season_ot_exposure.rationale: KXNCAAFMOSTOT is a season-extreme event: if a nine-overtime game has already occurred the market is decided, otherwise the number of remaining games times the per-game probability of reaching 9+ periods determines the price. The decay of exposure through the season is a deterministic input.
cfb.season_ot_exposure.measurement: For a contract 'some game reaches at least K overtimes' in scope S (FBS or all D-I): per remaining game q_K = P(tie after 60) x P(game lasts >= K OT periods | OT) with P(tie) from cfb.regulation_tie_curve and period continuation probability r (fitted on OT games, with a separate r from OT3 for the 2-point regime), q_K = P(tie) x r^(K-1). P(YES) = 1 - prod over remaining games (1 - q_K), or 1.0 if the current-season maximum is already >= K. Update weekly with the remaining schedule.
raw_data: season schedule with game dates and divisions
cfb.season_ot_exposure.why: Turns a per-game tail probability into the season contract and handles the monotone state variable (record already set).

cfb.score_resid.reason: Defined as residuals around lines, so it is a market-conditioned table; the tie mass it is meant to deliver is better estimated directly as the historical frequency of regulation ties in non-market expected-margin and expected-total buckets (cfb.regulation_tie_curve).

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Implied team points derived from the game total and spread are price outputs; they are useful as a cross-check for tie-probability buckets but cannot be an input without circularity.

cfb.market_ratings.reason: A rating backed out of lines is a price-derived quantity; only the absolute value of the rating gap matters for tie probability and a non-market SP+ or own rating gives the same information independent of the quote.

cfb.ot_model.reason: Overtime procedure (alternating possessions from the 25, 2-point alternation from the third period) is deterministic and defines length; the label conflates rules with a tie-probability model, which should be split into tie incidence and period-length parts.

cfb.kicker.reason: Kicker quality affects regulation scoring lumps, tying-field-goal success at the end and overtime period scoring; needs separate definitions for each use (regulation range, 42-yard OT kick).

cfb.coaching.reason: End-of-regulation decisions (kneel to go to overtime, kick the tying field goal, go for two) are the coaching lever; the generic coaching-change label does not measure them, so replace with a late-game decision profile.

cfb.pace.reason: Original claim that fewer possessions raises tie variance is imprecise: fewer possessions shrinks margin SD, which raises P(margin = 0) only when expected margin is near zero; keep as a driver of margin SD, not as a standalone tie predictor.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind and rain reduce scoring and increase lumpiness of 3-point scores, which slightly raises tie incidence; small and indirect through expected total.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: A large expected margin already makes tie probability near zero; blowout management adds nothing for the 1-in-20 games that stay close, where it is irrelevant by definition.

m.rules_text.reason: The rules text defines when an overtime period counts as played (legal snap in OT 1-2, first two-point attempt from OT 3), which is the core of both series and of period counting for the most-overtimes strike.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: The catalog definition is realized hit rates of settled Kalshi contracts by strike and a price-versus-realized calibration curve, i.e. market-derived with only a season or two of history; the overtime base rate it was credited with comes from game history via cfb.regulation_tie_curve. Keep only as a calibration benchmark.

cfb.drives.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on cfb.pace x cfb.score_resid x cfb.drives: Pace x variance: fewer possessions increase the share of games within a score at the end, boosting tie probabi) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.sp_plus.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s1) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s1) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: Tie probability depends jointly on the absolute rating gap and the margin SD, which in turn depends on possessions and weather; at a gap of zero the probability rises as SD falls, but at a gap of seven it rises with SD, so the sign of the SD effect flips with the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit tie probability on gap, SD proxy and their product; contrast the SD slope in gap<3 versus gap>7 games.

interactions.mechanism: A coach who habitually kicks the tying field goal creates overtime only if his kicker is accurate from 35-45 yards; a poor kicker makes the decision pointless, so incidence of created ties depends on the product of intent and capability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare tie rates in games where the trailing team had a late tying-FG opportunity by decision-profile tercile x kicker accuracy tercile.

interactions.mechanism: The probability that a period ends tied switches regime at the third overtime from a score-matching process (0.25-0.35) to a two-point match (about 0.5), so survival to 9 periods multiplies a small early factor by a roughly 0.5^6 tail; both the regime and the number of games enter the season probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate period-tie rates separately for OT1-2 and OT3+ from historical long games; compare the geometric prediction with the observed count of 6+ OT games.

interactions.mechanism: Overtime ties are more likely when both offences are poor from the 25 or both kickers are reliable (both score a field goal), and wind lowers touchdown probability while leaving short field goals reachable; the period tie probability is a product-sum of both teams' scoring distributions.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute predicted period tie probability from team distributions and evaluate calibration against realised OT1 outcomes by weather bucket.

nonlinearities.shape: Gaussian-like decay in absolute rating gap with a long thin tail; flat near zero gap
nonlinearities.why: A gap of 10 points has about one third of the tie probability of a gap of 3, but not zero because of volatile late scoring, so a linear gap term misprices both ends.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise with regime break at overtime period 3; period tie probability bounded near 0.5
nonlinearities.why: Because p_a p_b + (1 - p_a)(1 - p_b) stays between about 0.45 and 0.55 for all realistic rates, the probability of long overtimes is insensitive to team quality but very sensitive to the number of periods.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in games remaining: 1-(1-q)^N is nearly linear for tiny q and saturating only at very large N
nonlinearities.why: The market price should decay almost linearly as games complete, then jump to 1 if a qualifying game happens; a smooth hazard model misrepresents the step.

contract.settlement_definition: Period winner markets (KXNCAAF1H, 1Q, 2Q, 3Q, 4Q, 2H) settle YES if the named team wins the stated period; the complete rules text has no tie clause, so on a tied period neither team 'wins' and both team markets should resolve No (a reading of the text, not stated). KXNCAAF1HWINNER (historical) is a three-way half-time market: 'If the score is tied at the conclusion of the first-half, all team strikes resolve to No and the Tie strike resolves to Yes'. Only points in the stated period count; the 2nd half includes overtime (KXNCAAF2H, KXNCAAF2HSPREAD) and the 4th quarter excludes it. Spread markets (1Q-4Q, 1H, 2H) settle YES if the team wins the period by more than the half-point strike (for example 7.5). Postponement under 48 hours stays open, otherwise a fair price; KXNCAAF1HWINNER stays open for a rescheduled game within two weeks.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 4th quarter (excluding overtime) of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Fourth-quarter markets exclude overtime points, so a game tied after regulation does not add to the 4Q margin.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 2nd half (including overtime) of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Second-half markets include overtime points, making them depend on regulation tie probability.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 1st quarter of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: First-quarter spread uses only Q1 points; the strike 7.5 means a margin of 8 or more in 15 minutes.

rules_evidence.quote: If the score is tied at the conclusion of the first-half, all team strikes resolve to No and the Tie strike resolves to Yes
rules_evidence.establishes: The half-time winner market is three-way: a tied half pays the Tie strike and makes both team strikes lose.

rules_evidence.quote: If Texas St. wins by more than 7.5 points in the 3rd quarter
rules_evidence.establishes: Quarter spreads are strict greater-than on a half-point strike computed on that quarter's points only.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 1st half of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: First-half spreads use only first-half points, so overtime and second-half script never enter.

variants_and_edge_cases: Tied period: KXNCAAF1H and 1Q-4Q texts (complete in the sample, about 530 characters) contain no tie clause, so a tied period most plausibly resolves both team markets No; KXNCAAF1HWINNER states this explicitly and adds a Tie strike.
Overtime scope differs across series within the archetype: 2H and 2HSPREAD include it, 4Q and 4QSPREAD exclude it, 1H, 1HSPREAD and Q1-Q3 cannot include it.
Two postponement regimes: current series use a 48-hour start window then fair price; the historical KXNCAAF1HWINNER keeps the market open for a game rescheduled within two weeks.
KXNCAAF1H and KXNCAAF1HWINNER both settle on the first-half result but with different tie handling (implicit No versus an explicit Tie strike), so their prices are not interchangeable.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official play-by-play and period scoring in the final box score as published by the NCAA or the schools; the sampled text says official final result but not which provider.

mechanism.summary: A quarter or half margin is the difference between two short compound-Poisson scoring processes: the number of possessions each team gets in the period (set by tempo, who received the opening kick, and end-of-half clock behaviour) times the probability that a possession ends in a 3-, 6-, 7- or 8-point score. Period mean margin is a fraction of the game margin, but variance relative to mean is very large and there is a big point mass at zero, so winner markets are trinomial (win, tie, lose), with the tie paying a separate Tie strike in KXNCAAF1HWINNER and neither side elsewhere and spreads sit in a thin lumpy tail. Second-half and fourth-quarter periods are distorted by blowout management and by the contract's overtime scope.

stages.name: Possession order and tempo within the period
stages.description: Each period contains only two or three possessions per team. The team receiving the opening kickoff takes the first quarter's opening drive, and the team that deferred (or kicked off) normally receives the second-half kickoff and so opens the third quarter; deferral is a coach habit. Which team holds the ball at the end of the second quarter depends on the drive sequence, giving a last end-of-half scoring chance. Possession counts differ by period and drive times differ by tempo.
stages.distribution: Small-integer counts (about 2 to 3 per team per quarter) with a deterministic order effect; variance relative to the mean is high.

stages.name: Scoring rate per possession by period
stages.description: Per-possession scoring probability equals the team's opponent-adjusted offence against the opposing defence, but with period-specific modifiers: scripted openers in Q1, end-of-half two-minute drills in Q2, halftime adjustments in Q3, and clock-driven decisions in Q4. Quarter scoring history is mostly noise around the game-level rate.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcomes per possession with 3/7 payoff; period-level differences mostly random; real structural effects are a fraction of a point.

stages.name: Availability and the game-level margin prior
stages.description: The game-level expected margin from team ratings and the late quarterback decision supplies the mean from which period means are derived; the translation from game margin to period margin is roughly proportional to the period's share of scoring, but not exactly because favourites score disproportionately in first halves and clock-burn late.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like prior on game margin scaled by period fraction; period mean about 1/4 (quarter) or 1/2 (half) of game margin, with period noise far exceeding the mean shift.

stages.name: Script effects: blowout management and correlation across periods
stages.description: Second-half and fourth-quarter margins depend on halftime lead: favourites with large leads pull starters and run the ball, compressing their margin, while the first half is played at full strength. Period margins are positively correlated with the game margin and with each other through script and team strength.
stages.distribution: Conditional distribution given halftime lead; correlated joint distribution across periods with sign-flipping mean reversion in blowouts.

stages.name: Period margin lattice and settlement scope
stages.description: The period margin is lumpy: large mass at zero, then 3, 6, 7, with spread rungs at 7.5 needing at least an eight-point period margin. The period winner texts (1Q-4Q, 1H, 2H) say only 'wins the <period>', with no tie clause in the complete text, so a tied period pays neither side; KXNCAAF1HWINNER instead lists a Tie strike that resolves YES on a tied half. The second half includes overtime and the fourth quarter does not.
stages.distribution: Discrete lattice with point mass at 0 (roughly a quarter of quarters for even teams, less for halves) priced explicitly as the Tie leg; series-specific overtime scope.

talent_strength.note: Game-level non-market strength (SP+, PPA, talent) supplies the mean; market ratings are BENCHMARK_ONLY and removed; period conversion is the unresolved piece.

opponent_matchup.note: No input captures period-specific matchups such as a defence that starts slowly against tempo or a team that shows a different formation after halftime; the quarter matchup structure is not defined anywhere in this archetype.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback and starter-removal timing; depth chart effects are not separately defined.

availability_news.note: Quarterback vintage only; other late news enters through the game-level margin.

coaching_scheme.note: Deferral habits, two-minute management and tempo.

environment.note: Weather and venue mostly change full-game scoring level; their period-specific effect (wind late) is second-order against the possession-count noise of a quarter and is not separately modelled here.

game_context_script.note: Lead-dependent behaviour in H2 and possession order in Q1/Q3.

pace_volume.note: Possessions per period for each team.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-possession scoring in specific period contexts.

distribution_variance.note: Margin lattice and tie mass for the side markets plus cross-period correlation; the four-quarter joint scoring pmf moved with QHIGHSCORE and BTTS to quarter_and_half_totals.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry and bowl stakes shift the game-level mean margin but there is no evidence they redistribute scoring across quarters; any such effect is far below the possession-count noise of a 15-minute period.

officiating_rules.note: Overtime scope and tie handling by series are rules facts; targeting-ejection rules matter only for 2H sides, via the game-level model.

settlement_contract.note: 2H includes overtime, 4Q excludes it; KXNCAAF1HWINNER pays a Tie strike while the other winner texts have no tie clause.

cfb.period_possession_allocation.label: Period possession allocation (opening kick, deferral and end-of-half order)
cfb.period_possession_allocation.mechanism: Expected possessions per team in each quarter given who receives the opening kickoff, deferral habits and tempo.
cfb.period_possession_allocation.rationale: A quarter has only about 2-3 possessions per team, and receiving the opening kickoff gives one extra drive in Q1 (and typically ends Q2 with the other team holding the ball); the share swings expected quarter margin by 0.3 to 0.8 points between the two possession orders. The toss itself is only known at kickoff, so the input must be probabilistic.
cfb.period_possession_allocation.measurement: Per head coach: P(defer | wins toss) over last 3 seasons, shrunk with k = 10 tosses to the conference mean (remaining mass = receive; ignore choosing the end). P(win toss) = 0.5. P(team A receives first) = 0.5 x (1 - defer_A) + 0.5 x defer_B, and P(team A receives second half) = 1 - that. Expected drives in quarter k per team = season mean drives per team x quarter share (0.24-0.26) with Q1 and Q3 adjusted by +0.5 drive for the receiving-first team (Q1) or second-half receiver (Q3). Record realised toss only after kickoff; before that use the probabilities.
free_sources: CFBD games and plays (kickoff and coin toss from play text, free key)
cfb.period_possession_allocation.why: Possession count in a quarter is the dominant source of difference between a quarter spread and a share of the game spread.

cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.label: Two-minute and end-of-half drive efficiency
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.mechanism: Points per drive in the final two minutes of the first half and of the game, plus the share of drives where the leader runs out the clock.
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.rationale: Quarters 2 and 4 end with clock-driven scoring chances that are not representative of normal drives; a good two-minute offence with a reliable kicker produces points at a much higher rate, and teams differ in whether they play to score or hold the ball at the end of the half.
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.measurement: For each team: points per drive in the last 2:00 of Q2 and Q4 when score within 14 and at least one timeout, over 2 seasons, with 0.5 decay per season and shrinkage k = 20 drives to the conference mean; include kneel-down rate (drives ending in kneels when leading) and no-timeout slot. Compute opponent-adjusted by the opponent's allowed value.
free_sources: CFBD plays and drives with clock (free key)
raw_data: drive records with start time, clock at start, timeouts, result
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.why: Q2 and Q4 spreads and highest-scoring-quarter markets depend on these abnormal drives, which are not in a season efficiency rating.

cfb.period_margin_lattice.label: Period margin lattice and tie mass by expected margin and total
cfb.period_margin_lattice.mechanism: Empirical probabilities of period margin = 0, positive margins up to 8+, by period and by pre-game expected margin and total.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.rationale: In a single quarter the most likely outcome for evenly matched teams is a tie (0-0 or equal scores) and the winner market loses on ties; spread rungs at 7.5 correspond to a touchdown-plus-two margin or more, so they live in the thin right tail of a lumpy distribution. A Gaussian misprices both the mass at zero and the key numbers.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.measurement: From FBS games since 2014 take the line scores by period; for each period and for each of expected-margin bins (-14 to +14 in 3-point bins, from non-market ratings) and expected-total bins (3 bins) estimate P(margin = k) for k in {-14..14} with Dirichlet smoothing (prior strength 100 games, centred on a compound-Poisson model). Evaluate as of kickoff and output joint probabilities of tie, win and cover at each rung.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.why: Direct empirical shape for period winner and period spread contracts, whose ties and rung settlement (>7.5) hinge on lattice probabilities.

cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.label: Second-half overtime spillover
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.mechanism: Expected effect of overtime on the second-half margin, which includes overtime points by contract.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.rationale: For second-half sides, overtime points are added to each team's second-half total; a game that is tied after regulation is decided by overtime, so the second-half margin equals the overtime result plus second-half regulation margin; ignoring this biases second-half winner probabilities for the close games where it matters.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.measurement: P(OT) from a tie curve (bucketed by non-market expected margin and total) x distribution of OT margin (home/away first possession, points scored by period one: roughly 7 versus 3 versus 0); output expected spillover to the second-half margin = P(OT) x E[OT margin | team] and a variance increment. For 4Q and Q1-Q3 contracts set to zero because they exclude overtime.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.why: The same rules text contrast (2H includes OT, 4Q excludes it) changes the target distribution by series; a series-specific spillover makes the difference explicit.

cfb.market_ratings.reason: A full-game strength backed out of quotes is a benchmark; period markets are priced off it by sportsbooks, so using it as an input makes any period edge a statement about the sportsbook's period conversion, not about football.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Full-season opponent-adjusted offence is the right mean for the game but not for a single quarter; needs period-specific splits and scripted-opening effects, and its signal is diluted in a 15-minute window with 2-4 possessions.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Same limitation as off_ppa: defensive quality drives the scoring rate in every period but period-level noise dominates, so it enters only as the mean of a per-period rate.

cfb.half_split.reason: First-versus-second-half scoring share is the sum of quarter shares already in q_scoring; keeping both double-counts the same sample, and the half split has even fewer games per team than needed to be reliable.

cfb.q_scoring.reason: Team quarter scoring history is the direct target proxy, but a 12-game sample per quarter is mostly noise, so it must be shrunk heavily toward the game-level rate and used only for the structural (not random) component of quarter differences.

cfb.opening_poss.reason: Who receives the opening kickoff (and thus the second-half kickoff) decides the possession order in Q1 and Q3; the toss happens just before kickoff so this is not pregame-knowable, only forecastable from each coach's deferral tendency.

cfb.first_drive.reason: Opening-drive tendency matters for Q1 but the sample is one drive per game (about 12 per team-season), so its reliability is low; use only as a minor shrunk adjustment to Q1 scoring.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Relevant to third and fourth quarters and second-half sides, not to the first half where starters play; the label presents it as primary for all periods, which overstates its role. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: Quarterback change shifts expected period margin proportionally to the game effect, but is also a late-news driver for the quote; no period-specific effect has been shown, so secondary.

cfb.talent.reason: The claim that depth wins second halves is a plausible hypothesis, not a demonstrated effect; keep as a context variable to test whether depth shifts H2 share, not as an assumed driver.

cfb.coaching.reason: Halftime adjustment and tempo claims have no supporting measure in the label; define through measurable items (two-minute management, second-half pace change) before treating as informative.

cfb.score_resid.reason: Residuals around lines are tied to the quote; the period margin lattice with mass at zero must be built from historical period scores by expected margin, not from market residuals.

m.rules_text.reason: The rules text decides ties and overtime scope by series: the 2nd half includes overtime, the 4th quarter excludes it, the period winner texts have no tie clause while KXNCAAF1HWINNER pays a Tie strike; every series needs its own parameterisation.

cfb.corr.reason: Needed to keep Q1-Q4, 1H, 2H and full-game ladders mutually consistent and to price the KXNCAAF1HWINNER Tie leg jointly with the team legs; its estimation requires period-level history of both teams.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: Regressing fumble-recovery luck changes expected period margin by well under half a point; one early turnover is a realised random event, not a repeatable team trait that the pregame input can predict.

cfb.half_tie_conditional_win.reason: Written for KXNCAAF1HFT (first-half/full-game double), which the reconciliation moved to unreg:half_full_double_result; no series here settles on a conditional full-game winner.

cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.reason: Serves KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE and the quarter BTTS series, which are filed under quarter_and_half_totals; the side markets here settle on period margins, priced by cfb.period_margin_lattice.

cfb.sp_plus.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on cfb.blowout_management x cfb.sp_plus x cfb.period_margin_lattice: Hypothesis, not a demonstrated effect: second-half margins depend on halftime state: when the leader is up thr; stage s3) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: Expected points in a period equal possessions times scoring rate, so receiving the opening kickoff matters much more for an offence with a high touchdown rate: the extra drive is worth about 0.5 times that team's points per drive, a bigger edge for an elite offence than for a poor one.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress Q1 and Q3 margin on receive-first indicator interacted with team points per drive terciles; compare slopes.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis, not a demonstrated effect: second-half margins depend on halftime state: when the leader is up three scores, depth and rotation determine whether the margin shrinks, grows or stays; below that lead the first-half dynamics persist, so the regime switches at roughly 21 points. The input cfb.blowout_management is itself audited WEAK, so this regime switch is a conjecture to test, not a basis for the model.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition on halftime lead bins and estimate the second-half margin distribution separately for leads above and below 21.

interactions.mechanism: End-of-half scoring depends on possession order and whether a team plays to score or holds the ball: the team receiving the second-half kickoff has an incentive to hold for a field goal before the half, raising the other team's chance of scoring in Q2.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q2 margins when the first-half receiver holds the last possession vs not, split by two-minute efficiency terciles.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis, not a demonstrated effect: a backup quarterback is scripted conservatively in Q1, so Q1 margin shrinks toward zero, but only if the offence's opening script was prepared for him; once the game opens up in later quarters the penalty grows, so the effect of a QB change on period margin depends on the period index.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the margin residual of backup-quarterback games by period; test a monotone increase in the penalty from Q1 to Q4.

interactions.mechanism: The 2H winner and the full-game winner are strongly dependent through overtime, and 2H sides depend on the 1H result through halftime-lead script; marginal quarters are positively correlated through team strength but only weakly so, which defeats independent-leg pricing.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the empirical correlation matrix of period margins by expected margin bin and test independence on pairs (1H, 2H) and (Q3, Q4).

interactions.mechanism: The KXNCAAF1HWINNER Tie strike and the two team strikes partition the half-time margin, so their probabilities must sum to one; the tie mass at the half is raised by end-of-half field-goal drives that equalise 7-10 or 14-17 scores and lowered when the team holding the last first-half possession is an efficient two-minute offence, so the three legs move jointly with the end-of-half possession order.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate tied halves by whether the trailing team held the last first-half possession and by its two-minute efficiency tercile; check that predicted team and tie legs sum to one and are calibrated.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at zero margin plus lumps at 3, 6-8; probability of a margin >= 8 within a quarter is far below a Gaussian prediction
nonlinearities.why: A quarter has only 5-6 combined drives, so margins above 7 require multiple scores; a continuous model misprices tie probability and rung 7.5 by several percentage points.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold near a 21-point lead; weak effect below, strong compression above
nonlinearities.why: Starters stay in until the game is effectively decided; the effect on second-half margin appears only past a lead of about three scores.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function: one extra possession (about 0.5 drive) for the receiving team in Q1 and Q3, none elsewhere
nonlinearities.why: The possession order effect is binary rather than continuous and is concentrated in specific quarters; averaging across periods hides it.
