unresolved.description: The complete KXNCAAF1H/1Q-4Q rules text has no tie clause; reading 'wins the period' literally, a tied quarter (roughly 20-30 percent for even teams) resolves both team markets No, but this is inferred, not stated, unlike the explicit Tie strike of KXNCAAF1HWINNER.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Inspect settlement of past KXNCAAF1Q-4Q markets on tied quarters (both No versus refund) or obtain Kalshi's confirmation.

unresolved.description: No existing input captures period-specific matchup structure (scripted openers versus fast starters, halftime adjustment quality, second-half tempo changes); evidence that such effects exist beyond noise is thin in a 12-game sample per team.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Estimate team-level persistence of period-share residuals across seasons; if the year-to-year correlation is near zero, document the gap as noise.

contract.settlement_definition: Quarter and half total markets (KXNCAAF1QTOTAL, 2QTOTAL, 3QTOTAL, 4QTOTAL, 1HTOTAL, 2HTOTAL) settle YES if the two teams collectively score more than the half-point strike in that period, counting only points in that period; the 2nd half includes overtime (as the 2HTOTAL rules state) and the 4th quarter excludes overtime. KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL settles YES if the named team alone scores over its strike in the first half. Postponed games starting within 48 hours remain open and settle on the official final result; otherwise a fair price. Moved here by the reconciliation: KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE settles on which quarter has the most combined points (overtime excluded from Q4), paying $1/N to each of N tied quarters; the both-teams-to-score series KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS and 3QBTTS have no listed market and no rules text.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 4th quarter (excluding overtime) of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Fourth-quarter totals exclude overtime, so the distribution is regulation-only and unaffected by ties.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 2nd half (including overtime) of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Second-half totals include overtime periods, adding a rare positive increment from tied games.

rules_evidence.quote: If the teams collectively score more than 7.5 points in the 1st quarter
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike construction is strictly greater than a half-point value, so a total of 8 or more points in 15 minutes is needed.

rules_evidence.quote: If Notre Dame scores over 6.5 points in the 1st half of the Miami (FL) vs Notre Dame college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: The team-total variant counts only one team's points in the first half with a half-point strike.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple quarters are tied for the most points scored
rules_evidence.establishes: Highest-scoring quarter pays 1/N to each tied quarter (rounded down), so the target is an expected payout over the joint four-quarter distribution, not a binary event.

rules_evidence.quote: Any points scored in overtime do not count toward 4th quarter points.
rules_evidence.establishes: The fourth quarter competes for highest-scoring quarter on regulation points only.

rules_evidence.quote: If the teams collectively score more than 6.5 points in the 1st half
rules_evidence.establishes: The first-half total is a strict greater-than on combined first-half points with a half-point strike.

variants_and_edge_cases: Period scope by series: 1Q to 3Q and 1H cannot include overtime, 4Q explicitly excludes it, 2H explicitly includes it; the 1HTEAMTOTAL primary text states the scope ('scores over 6.5 points in the 1st half'), what is unstated is how a suspension is handled.

Strike levels in the samples are very low for halves (6.5 for 1H and 2H totals) relative to typical first-half totals (not quantified here: the left-tail frequency of 1H totals of 6 or fewer points must be measured, see cfb.period_total_dispersion validation), so the ladders have many rungs and the sampled rung is one of many nested events.
Safeties, two-point conversions and defensive scores count as points for the team or game; the sampled text does not say otherwise, but extra-point returns are not discussed.
Quarter totals have large mass at 0 and 7, meaning .5 strikes at 6.5 and 7.5 carve very different probabilities (P(total >= 7) versus P(total >= 8)).
A postponed or suspended game starting within 48 hours remains open; a game suspended mid-period (weather) with resumed play affects period labelling and is not addressed.
QHIGHSCORE payouts are fractional on ties (1/N rounded down to the cent), so tied low-scoring quarters (for example two 7-point quarters) split value.
KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS and 3QBTTS are NO_LISTING: whether a safety or a defensive score counts as a team scoring is not read.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official period scoring from the final box score; Kalshi text says official final result but does not name the stats provider.

mechanism.summary: A period total is the sum of points from both teams in a short window: the number of combined scoring chances (drives that fit in the period, capped by clock) times the probability and size of scores, which come in lumps of 3, 6, 7 and 8, so the distribution is a compound count with a large mass at zero and at the key sums. The mean is a non-uniform share of the game total (end-of-half drives, scripted openers, lead-dependent late periods), while variance is large relative to mean. Overtime matters only for the second half, and for team-total variants only one side's scoring process enters.

stages.name: Game-level scoring expectation allocated to the period
stages.description: A pregame expected total (from opponent-adjusted offences and defences and conditions) is allocated across periods by a share that depends on expected game script: Q2 and Q4 hold two-minute drives and are scored at higher rates per minute, Q1 starts with scripted plays, Q3 starts after halftime adjustments. The share also depends on the gap, since big leads reduce Q4.
stages.distribution: Allocation shares vary around 0.2-0.3 per quarter with game-level dependence; shares are estimated from league history and have sampling noise of a few percentage points.

stages.name: Drive budget inside the period
stages.description: How many drives fit into 15 minutes is set by both teams' seconds per drive, run-pass mix, turnovers and end-of-period truncation; Q2 and Q4 end with abrupt clock stops and sometimes kneel-downs, while Q1 and Q3 usually do not. A slow period of four combined drives caps the total in a way that a mean-based approach hides.
stages.distribution: Count of drives (4 to 7 combined) with threshold effects at low counts; truncation of the last drive at the period end.

stages.name: Points per scoring chance and lumpy scoring
stages.description: Each drive ends in 0, 3, 6, 7 or 8 points with team-specific touchdown-versus-field-goal mix; the period total is the sum of those jumps. End-of-half field-goal decisions, scripted openers and turnovers shift the probability of scoring; kickers matter at the margins because a 3 versus a 0 flips a low rung.
stages.distribution: Compound count with lumps at 3 and 7 and a negative-binomial-like number of scoring drives; overdispersed relative to Poisson.

stages.name: Script and personnel shocks late in the game
stages.description: In Q3 and Q4, lead-dependent behaviour (clock burning, starter removal, garbage-time scoring by the trailing team) reshapes the total; quarterback status and weather change scoring rates in every period but with period-specific timing (wind rising in the second half).
stages.distribution: Conditional mixture: tight totals in competitive games versus bimodal totals in blowouts; discrete shocks from quarterback and weather.

stages.name: Series scope and settlement
stages.description: Series differ in scope: 2H includes overtime, 4Q excludes it, 1H team total counts a single team, and the rung strike lies on the half-point so the settlement threshold is a specific integer of points. The ladder of rungs for one period is a nested family and must be internally consistent.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the pmf to rung probabilities; consistency constraint across rungs (monotone survival).

stages.name: Joint four-quarter scoring for highest quarter and both-teams-to-score
stages.description: QHIGHSCORE needs the joint distribution of all four quarter totals, because the payout depends on which quarter is the argmax and on how many quarters tie for it; BTTS needs each team's probability of a scoreless quarter, which is a per-team zero mass rather than a combined total. Quarter totals are positively correlated through game pace and strength, and Q2/Q4 carry end-of-half drives, so treating quarters as independent misprices both the argmax and the tie split.
stages.distribution: Correlated negative-binomial scoring-drive counts per team and quarter with 3/6/7/8 lumps; argmax with N-way tie split; per-team zero mass of roughly a third to a half per quarter.

talent_strength.note: Game-level scoring expectation from offence and defence, allocated by league-baseline shares.

opponent_matchup.note: No input defines how a specific offence matches a specific defence inside a period (for example an opponent that starts slowly or an offence that scripts well), beyond season-level adjusted efficiencies; period matchup structure is unmodelled.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback and kicker identity; backups' snap share in late periods enters via the garbage-time profile.

availability_news.note: Late quarterback status; other availability enters through game-level expectation.

environment.note: Forecast vintage; second-half wind evolution is only partly captured.

pace_volume.note: Combined drive count in the period.

efficiency_conversion.note: Points per scoring drive and field-goal conversion.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersion, zero mass and lumpy sums. The joint four-quarter pmf covers QHIGHSCORE and BTTS.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and motivational stakes change the game-level mean slightly but there is no argument they redistribute scoring across periods, and their effect is far below the sampling noise of a single quarter total.

officiating_rules.note: Overtime scope by series and the period-scoring rule definitions.

settlement_contract.note: Overtime scope per series read from the rules text (2H includes overtime, 4Q excludes it); ladder consistency is a benchmark check, not an input.

cfb.period_share_of_total.label: League-baseline share of scoring by period conditional on expected total and gap
cfb.period_share_of_total.mechanism: Fraction of regulation points scored in each quarter by games with similar expected total and rating gap.
cfb.period_share_of_total.rationale: Allocating a game total to quarters with equal quarters is wrong: end-of-half possessions, scripted openers and lead-dependent second halves make shares unequal and dependent on the gap (blowouts cut Q4 scoring) and on the total. The share is a structural baseline separate from team-specific history.
cfb.period_share_of_total.measurement: From FBS games since 2014 compute E[points in period k] / E[regulation points] by bins of expected total (non-market, 4 bins) and absolute expected margin (5 bins), with shrinkage k = 150 games to the pooled share; also store the variance and the share of games with zero points in the period. Apply to the pre-game expected total from a ratings model; exclude overtime from all quarters and add it only to 2H for the 2H contract.
cfb.period_share_of_total.why: Directly produces the mean of every quarter, half and 1H team-total rung from one game-level estimate.

cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.label: Combined drives and clock budget per period
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.mechanism: Expected number of combined drives that fit in the period and the probability that a possession is cut off by the clock.
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.rationale: A quarter holds about five or six combined drives, and the last drive of Q2 and Q4 is truncated by the clock; slow, run-heavy teams can reduce the combined drive count in the first period to four, which lowers the total in a threshold manner at the 7.5 rung.
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.measurement: For each team compute seconds per non-garbage drive by period (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 separately) over the last 10 games with 0.8 decay; combined drives in period k = 900 / (0.5 (d_a + d_b)) minus end-of-period truncation fraction (empirical 0.1-0.3 drive for Q2 and Q4), with the 2023-onward running-clock regime as a covariate. Output mean and SD of combined drives and P(drives <= 4).
free_sources: CFBD drives with clock fields (free key)
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.why: Quarter and half totals need a count of scoring trials inside a short window; this input gives that count and its threshold behaviour.

cfb.period_total_dispersion.label: Period-total dispersion and zero-scoring mass
cfb.period_total_dispersion.mechanism: Variance-to-mean ratio and the probability of a scoreless period for team pairs, given expected points.
cfb.period_total_dispersion.rationale: Single-quarter totals are overdispersed relative to Poisson in points but heavily mass-concentrated at 0, 3 and 7; rungs at 7.5 are sensitive to whether the probability of scoring zero in the period is 15 or 25 percent. Explosive teams and field-goal teams differ in the lumpiness for the same mean.
cfb.period_total_dispersion.measurement: Fit a compound model per period: number of scoring drives N ~ negative binomial with mean mu_k and dispersion r (fit on FBS 2014 onward), points per scoring drive from a 3/6/7/8 mixture with team-specific touchdown share (touchdown share shrunk k = 25 scoring drives). Output P(total = 0), P(total >= 8), and the full pmf up to 28. As-of last completed game. Left-tail validation: on held-out seasons compare predicted P(1H total <= 6), P(2H regulation total <= 6) and P(quarter total = 0) to realised frequencies by expected-total bin (reliability table with binomial intervals); refit the negative-binomial dispersion if the left tail is miscalibrated.
raw_data: scoring drives by period with points
cfb.period_total_dispersion.why: Gives the exact probability of crossing 6.5 / 7.5 / 13.5 rungs rather than a normal approximation to a lumpy count.

cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.label: Garbage-time scoring profile
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.mechanism: How many points the trailing team and the backups score late when the margin exceeds the garbage-time threshold, and how fast the leader burns clock.
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.rationale: In Q4 totals the effect of a lead is double-edged: the leader scores less and runs the clock, the trailer scores late against backups; the net effect depends on coach pull-point, backup quality and defensive depth, and differs across the 4Q-only and 2H contracts.
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.measurement: Define garbage time by margin thresholds above (Q3 > 27, Q4 > 21; verify against published practice); for each team compute points scored and allowed per garbage-time minute and seconds per play when leading, over 2 seasons with 0.5 decay and shrinkage k = 100 snaps; combine with the probability of reaching garbage time from the pre-game rating gap.
free_sources: CFBD plays with score state (free key)
raw_data: plays with period, clock, score diff, offense
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.why: Fourth-quarter and second-half totals diverge from a share-of-total rule precisely in games with large gaps; this input quantifies that divergence.

cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.label: Overtime points increment to the second-half total
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.mechanism: KXNCAAF2HTOTAL counts overtime points, so the 2H total is regulation second-half points plus, with probability P(tied after 60 minutes), the combined points of all overtime periods.
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.rationale: With roughly a 6 percent chance of overtime and around 7 to 10 combined overtime points when it happens, the 2H mean shifts by about half a point and the variance and right tail grow, which matters for a 6.5 rung on a low count; 1Q-3Q, 1H and 4Q contracts exclude overtime and get zero increment.
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.measurement: P(OT) from cfb.ot_model: logistic/GAM of tie after regulation on absolute non-market expected margin (SP+ or own rating) and expected total, fitted on FBS games 2005 onward with prior strength 200 games. Conditional on OT, combined overtime points = sum over periods of per-possession scoring (touchdown about 0.65 per possession from the 25 with 7 points plus a field-goal share, two-point attempts from the third overtime onward); fit the pmf of combined overtime points on FBS overtime games 2005 onward (about 1,000 games), shrunk to pooled with prior strength 50 games. Output E[increment] = P(OT) x E[OT total] and the pmf to convolve with the regulation 2H pmf. Set to zero for non-2H contracts. As-of last completed game.
free_sources: CFBD games line scores with overtime (free key)
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.why: KXNCAAF2HTOTAL (sampled rung 6.5, text states the 2nd half includes overtime) is shifted and fattened in the right tail by overtime; the other quarter and half totals are not.

cfb.team_period_points_share.label: Team share of period points from non-market team strengths
cfb.team_period_points_share.mechanism: Splits the game-level expected points in a half between the two teams using each offence points per drive against the opposing defence, plus the receiving team in the half, for KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL.
cfb.team_period_points_share.rationale: The team-side 1H total is not half of a team full-game total: the share depends on who receives the opening kickoff and which team has the stronger offence against the weaker defence, and first-half scoring is lumpy. Without a non-market allocation the series would need the benchmark team-total split.
cfb.team_period_points_share.measurement: Expected 1H points for team A = (E[game 1H points] from cfb.period_share_of_total) x w_A, with w_A = A expected game points / (A + B expected game points) where expected points come from opponent-adjusted off_ppa and def_ppa (current season with 6-game half-life shrunk to prior season with k=4 games), then add 0.5 x A points per drive if A receives the first-half kickoff and subtract 0.5 x B points per drive if B does not receive. Output mean and a negative-binomial scoring-drive dispersion fitted on FBS 2014 onward. As-of the Saturday preceding kickoff; no price or line input.
free_sources: CFBD games, drives and PPA (free key)
raw_data: team points per drive and opponent-adjusted PPA
cfb.team_period_points_share.why: KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL needs a team-side allocation of first-half points that does not use any market total split.

cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.label: Joint four-quarter scoring pmf with per-team scoreless mass and highest-quarter argmax
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.mechanism: Distribution of each quarter combined points and each team points jointly across Q1-Q4, with quarter-to-quarter correlation, used to price both-teams-to-score in a quarter and the highest-scoring-quarter contract with its 1/N tie split.
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.rationale: KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE pays 1/N (rounded down to a cent) when N quarters tie for the most combined points and excludes overtime from Q4; the BTTS series (1Q, 2Q, 3Q) need the per-team probability of scoring at least once in that quarter. Neither is a margin event, so a margin lattice cannot price them: they need the pmf of period totals, the probability each team is held scoreless in the quarter, and the negative dependence between a heavy first half and a compressed second half.
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.measurement: From FBS games 2014 onward (CFBD line scores and drives), for each team and quarter fit scoring drives N ~ negative binomial with mean from cfb.q_scoring times expected possessions, dispersion fitted pooled; points per scoring drive from a 3/6/7/8 mixture with team touchdown share shrunk k=25 drives; combine the four quarters with a Gaussian copula whose Spearman correlations are estimated by bins of expected total (3 bins) and absolute expected margin (3 bins), shrunk to the pooled matrix with prior strength 200 games. Simulate 50,000 games: output P(team scores >=1 in quarter k) for each team, the pmf of combined points per quarter, and for QHIGHSCORE the expected payout sum over quarters of P(k is the argmax with N-way tie)/N, Q4 regulation points only. As-of last completed game before kickoff.
free_sources: CFBD games line scores and drives (free key)
raw_data: line scores by period for both teams
scoring drives by quarter with points
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.why: KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE (1/N payout on tied quarters, overtime excluded from Q4) and KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS, 3QBTTS need the joint four-quarter pmf and per-team scoreless mass, not totals or margins.

cfb.q_scoring.reason: Team quarter scoring history is the target-matched feature, but 12 games per quarter is a tiny sample; needed in a shrunk form where the signal is the structural share (end-of-half, scripted opener) not the realised noise.

cfb.half_split.reason: First-half share of scoring is a sum of Q1+Q2 shares already in q_scoring; the half is also less volatile than quarters but needs no separate input, only a different aggregation.

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Defined from the game total and spread, which are prices; for period totals the expected game points should come from non-market ratings and the quote used only to measure edge.

cfb.opening_poss.reason: For a combined total the number of Q1 possessions is the same regardless of who receives; the order matters for who holds the ball at the end of Q2 (a small change in expected scoring), so the effect on totals is far smaller than on period sides.

cfb.first_drive.reason: Scripted opening drives can lift Q1 scoring for both teams, but one drive per game makes this a very noisy feature; use only a shrunk average of both opening-drive point rates.

cfb.pace.reason: Plays and drives in a 15-minute period scale directly with tempo; however pace differs between periods (end-of-half hurry-up, clock-killing in Q4), so a season average must be period-adjusted.

cfb.script.reason: Expected score state alters tempo and pass rate within the period; for Q1 it is nearly irrelevant (the score is level), for Q4 it is the dominant context. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Primary only for Q3/Q4 and second-half totals; for Q1 and Q2 the starters are in and the input has no role, which the original primary label hides. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.coaching.reason: Tempo and halftime management claims need measurable definitions (second-half seconds per play versus first-half, end-of-half aggressiveness) before they carry weight.

cfb.kicker.reason: Field-goal chances at the end of each half add points in Q2 and Q4 totals; kicker range matters, but effect is limited to a single drive per half.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind picks up or fades during games, so period-specific effects exist, but the pregame forecast resolves only the average conditions; second-half wind forecast is less reliable.

m.rules_text.reason: Series differ: the 2H total includes overtime, the 4Q total excludes it, and the team-total 1H is stated in the title; each rung must be parameterised by its text.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung consistency of period total quotes diagnoses stale quotes and the market's implied lattice, but it is price-derived and not an outcome driver.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: A backup quarterback lowers all period totals and widens uncertainty, but the period-specific effect is not shown; because period totals are noisy the signal-to-noise is low.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency sets points per possession in each period; PPA for a single period is not stable, so the full-season value is scaled by the period's possession budget.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Defensive counterpart; same use, scaled by the possession budget; connectivity and sample caveats as in sides and totals archetypes.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: A single early turnover can settle a quarter total, but it is a realised event; regressing past turnover luck shifts the expected period total by tenths of a point and does not repay the complexity.

cfb.ot_model.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s5) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: Probability of crossing the 7.5 rung in a quarter jumps when the combined drive count falls from six to four, because with four drives it takes two scoring drives for more than seven points and the zero-scoring mass rises sharply; the effect of tempo is non-linear and strongest for slow-tempo pairings.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(quarter total >= 8) by predicted combined drives count and test a break at five drives.

interactions.mechanism: Fourth-quarter share of the game total depends on the expected gap: when the gap is small, Q4 holds the highest share (two-minute drills, urgency); when large, the leader's rate falls and the trailer's garbage-time scores partially offset, so Q4 share turns down.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate Q4 share by gap bins; compare to the pooled share and fit a piecewise function.

interactions.mechanism: End-of-half field-goal decisions interact with kicker range: a coach with a reliable kicker takes three points before the half, which raises Q2 and Q4 totals in lumps of three and thickens the pmf at 3 and 10, while an unreliable kicker leads to turnovers on downs and thinner mass at 3.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the Q2 total pmf by kicker accuracy tercile and decision-aggressiveness tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Wind that rises in the second half cuts the passing offence's scoring rate and the effect is amplified for fast-tempo pass-heavy offences, so the second-half total responds to the product of forecast wind trend and offensive pass reliance, not to the average forecast.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact forecast wind trend (late minus early) with pass-reliance terciles in a model of 2H and 4Q totals.

interactions.mechanism: The overtime increment exists only in games tied after regulation, which are close games where starters stay in and the 2H regulation total is least compressed by blowout management; so the increment is not independent of the regulation second-half total and adds right-tail mass exactly where the 6.5 rung is least at risk.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare 2H totals including overtime against regulation 2H totals, split by pre-game absolute margin bins, and test whether adding the increment to a regulation pmf reproduces the empirical 2H distribution.

interactions.mechanism: Q2 and Q4 gain end-of-half drives and tempo spikes, so in high-total games they are the likeliest argmax, while in low-total games a single touchdown decides the highest quarter and ties among 7-point quarters are common; the drive budget per quarter therefore changes both the argmax probability and the expected tie split.
interactions.how_to_test: By expected-total bin, compare the empirical distribution of the highest-scoring quarter and its tie frequency against the copula simulation and against an independent-quarters simulation.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at about four combined drives, weak above six
nonlinearities.why: The count of scoring trials is small, so each lost drive removes a large fraction of expected points; the probability of a scoreless period is convex in drive count.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at 0 and lumps at 3, 6, 7, 10; survival function is stair-stepped, not smooth
nonlinearities.why: The probability that a quarter total exceeds 7.5 differs by about a third from the probability it exceeds 6.5 because 7 is the most common touchdown outcome; a continuous distribution cannot reproduce that.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: no effect until lead exceeds about three scores, then offsetting declines and increases
nonlinearities.why: Late leads change who scores and how fast the clock moves only beyond a threshold; below it the quarter looks like a competitive one.

unresolved.description: Whether quarter-specific structural effects (scripted openers, two-minute drills, halftime adjustment) are large enough to beat a simple share-of-game-total model is unknown; with 5-6 drives per quarter much of the variation may be irreducible noise.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Out-of-sample comparison on 5 seasons of quarter totals of the share model against a model with period-specific features, scored by log loss at the .5 rungs.

unresolved.description: The KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL primary text sets first-half scope ('scores over 6.5 points in the 1st half'), so only suspension handling is unstated; no sampled series covers team totals for quarters or second halves.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the full live KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL rules for a suspension clause and list any team-total series for other periods.

unresolved.description: No definition exists for a period-specific matchup effect between an offence and a defence; season-level adjusted efficiencies may suffice but period variation in defensive scheme (nickel vs base) is not captured in available data.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Test whether adding period-specific opponent-adjusted efficiency improves out-of-sample period-total log loss.

unresolved.description: The garbage-time thresholds by quarter (for example Q3 margin above 27, Q4 above 21) are assumed from published practice and not verified here; the proper definition could differ for FCS or for rule-regime changes.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Verify thresholds from the published SP+ methodology and test sensitivity by changing them by plus or minus 7 points.

unresolved.description: Period line scores and drive start/end clock are assumed available from CFBD games and drives endpoints for 2014 onward, but clock fields at drive boundaries are inconsistent in public play data, especially for the last drive of each half, and the end-of-period truncation fraction (0.1 to 0.3) depends on them.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Audit CFBD drive clock fields against official play-by-play for a sample of games per season and measure missing or inconsistent last-drive clocks by half.

unresolved.description: The both-teams-to-score series (KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS, 3QBTTS), moved here by the reconciliation, have no listed market and no rules text, so whether a safety, a defensive touchdown or a two-point return counts as the team scoring in the quarter cannot be stated.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: A listed BTTS market with rules text or a Kalshi statement of what counts as scoring in a quarter.

contract.settlement_definition: Season futures settle on resolved season results. Win totals (KXNCAAFWINS, 12+ wins) count official regular-season games only and 'Ties do not count as wins'; UNDEFEATED counts regular-season games only; UNDEFEATEDHOME counts games at the official home stadium (neutral sites excluded); H2HWINS compares two teams' regular-season wins with a Tie outcome when equal; the conference count series (SECWINS, BIGTENWINS, BIG12WINS, ACCWINS) settle YES if at least N conference teams win 10+ regular-season games. Conference champion series (SEC, ACC, B10, B12, AAC, MAC, MWC, SBELT, CUSA, PAC12) settle on winning the 2026 conference championship game and qualifier series on qualifying for it; CONFMATCHUP resolves when the named pair secures the title-game slots; REGTOP top-5 finishes count all teams tied on conference record as achieving the position. CFP series settle on qualifying (PLAYOFF), reaching the quarterfinals, semifinals or final (QF, SF, FINALIST), winning (KXNCAAF), seed (#12 SEED, top-4 TOPSEED), Group of Six count (CFPCONF, Pac-12 included), champion's conference (CONF) and the LSU-Texas double (LSUTEX2X: regular-season win and a national-final win over Texas). BOWLGAME settles on selection to an NCAA-certified bowl or the CFP (FCS playoffs excluded); TFUT on CFP qualification after issuance and before 2030-31; FCS, CS and D3 on winning the respective national championship. KXNCAAFBACC, BSEC, BB10, BB12, IVY and PAC10 are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: Only official regular season games count towards the team's win total. Ties do not count as wins.
rules_evidence.establishes: Win totals exclude conference title, bowl and playoff games, so the contract is a count over the regular-season schedule.

rules_evidence.quote: The market resolves to Yes if Wyoming has been selected to play, regardless of whether they actually compete in a bowl game or the College Football Playoff.
rules_evidence.establishes: Bowl contracts settle on selection, so opt-outs and cancellations after selection do not matter and the decision-maker (bowl committees) matters.

rules_evidence.quote: all tied teams will resolve as having achieved that position
rules_evidence.establishes: Regular-season top-5 finishes are decided by conference record and ties pay every tied team, which makes the market monotone in ties.

rules_evidence.quote: Neutral site games do not count as a home game for either team.
rules_evidence.establishes: Home-undefeated contracts need the venue designation of each game, so neutral and bowl-week sites alter the product of probabilities.

rules_evidence.quote: Conference championships, bowl games, and College Football Playoff games do not count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Head-to-head win markets compare regular-season win counts only and include a Tie leg when equal.

rules_evidence.quote: after Issuance and before the 2030-31 college football season
rules_evidence.establishes: Qualification-before-2030 market spans multiple seasons, so it is a multi-year hazard of making the playoff rather than a single-season probability. It also depends on the Issuance date (only qualification events after issuance count) and on the CFP format over 2026-2029 (12 or 24 teams), neither of which the sampled text fixes.

rules_evidence.quote: If at least 8 teams in the Southeastern Conference win 10+ games in the 2026 college football regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Conference count contracts are a threshold on the number of teams reaching 10 regular-season wins, a correlated count over the whole conference schedule.

rules_evidence.quote: wins the FCS National Championship in the 2026-27 season
rules_evidence.establishes: The FCS champion series settles on the FCS playoff final, so it needs an FCS rating and bracket model, not FBS ratings.

rules_evidence.quote: including teams from the American Athletic Conference, Conference USA, Mid-American Conference, Mountain West Conference, Sun Belt Conference, and Pac-12 Conference
rules_evidence.establishes: The Group of Six count includes the Pac-12, so the reconstituted Pac-12 champion counts toward the 2+ rung.

rules_evidence.quote: LSU and Texas do not meet again in the National Championship game
rules_evidence.establishes: The double needs a rematch in the national final specifically; a second win in the SEC title game or an earlier CFP round does not count.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution occurs immediately upon qualification, not when the game is actually played.
rules_evidence.establishes: Title-game pair contracts settle on both teams securing slots, so tiebreaker outcomes, not the title game itself, decide them.

rules_evidence.quote: If Vanderbilt wins the 2026 College Football SEC Championship Game
rules_evidence.establishes: Conference champion series settle on the conference championship game result, not on regular-season standings.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington is selected as the #12 seed in the 2026-27 College Football Playoff
rules_evidence.establishes: Seed contracts settle on the exact seed assigned by the selection committee.

variants_and_edge_cases: The archetype contains single-season counts (WINS, UNDEFEATED), conference structure events (SEC/ACC/B12/B10/MAC/AAC... champion and qualifier), selection outcomes (BOWLGAME, PLAYOFF, QF, SF, FINALIST, SEED, TOPSEED, CFPCONF), a multi-year event (TFUT before 2030) and a combination event (KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X: LSU beats Texas in the regular season and beats Texas again in the national championship game specifically).
Selection-versus-participation: BOWLGAME settles on being selected, whereas PLAYOFF and QF depend on committee selection and format rules that differ by season (number of teams, auto bids, seeding).
Regular-season top-N finish markets pay all tied teams, a ties rule that makes probabilities sum above one across teams.

Six series are TITLE_ONLY with no rules text: KXNCAAFBACC, BSEC, BB10, BB12 (older duplicates of conference champion tickers), KXNCAAFIVY (the Ivy League has no championship game) and KXNCAAFPAC10 (defunct conference name).
Realignment: the Pac-12 champion and qualifier markets in 2026 imply a reconstituted conference with new members and game formats not in historical data.

Conference 10-win count series count all regular-season wins (an FCS win counts) and exclude the conference title game; head-to-head games between conference members make the teams' win counts negatively dependent.

KXNCAAFCS and KXNCAAFD3 are historical 2025-26 FCS and Division III champion texts ('wins the 2025-26 College Football FCS National Championship'); KXNCAAFFCS is the 2026-27 FCS series, so the same event is listed under two tickers across seasons.
H2HWINS counts total regular-season wins even if the two teams play different numbers of games, so an extra scheduled game (Hawaii rule, a replacement game) changes the comparison.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NCAA, conference and CFP committee results (final standings, official conference championship result, CFP selection show); the Kalshi text cites Source Agencies for some markets but names no provider for win counts.

mechanism.summary: Season-level outcomes are functions of the whole schedule and of several layers of rules: team strengths are uncertain and correlated draws (with shocks from quarterback injury), each game is a noisy contest whose probability depends on site, rest and matchup, regular-season wins determine conference standings through unbalanced schedules and tiebreakers, conference champions and ranked teams are selected by committee into a bracket whose size and seeding rules vary by season, and long-dated contracts add a random walk of program strength. Settlement wording (regular season only, selection not participation, ties paid to all) changes which function of the simulation is the target.

stages.name: Team-strength prior with correlated uncertainty
stages.description: Start-of-season ratings combine last year's performance regressed by returning production, recruiting talent and portal changes; the uncertainty is large (several points) and shared across a team's games, and connectivity is thin across conferences. In-season, ratings update by results, but the same posterior draw affects every remaining game, which creates correlation that drives the tails of win-count contracts.
stages.distribution: Latent Gaussian rating vector with prior SD 5-6 points, shrinking with games; joint posterior with positive correlation across a team's games.

stages.name: Quarterback and key-player shocks
stages.description: Single-player availability alters a contender's rating by several points; the probability of the starting quarterback missing at least one regular-season game is large enough to matter, and the replacement quality varies widely. These shocks generate the heavy lower tail of team strength and lower the favourite's title concentration.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per game with heavy-tailed rating impact; mixture over games missed.

stages.name: Schedule path and game outcomes
stages.description: Each remaining game has a win probability from the rating difference, home-field edge and rest; the regular season win count is a Poisson-binomial with correlated draws, and special counts (undefeated, home-undefeated, head-to-head wins) are products or comparisons of these. Unbalanced conference schedules matter because teams in the same conference do not play each other equally. The conference 10-win count series add a second layer: the number of teams over a threshold depends on the whole conference grid, where every intra-conference game hands one team a win and the other a loss, plus a shared conference-strength shock, so cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence simulates the grid jointly.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial (correlated) counts; undefeated probabilities are products of per-game probabilities so tiny differences compound.

stages.name: Conference standings, tiebreakers and title game
stages.description: Conference records determine standings; ties are broken by head-to-head, common opponents and other conference-specific rules, which are nonlinear in the remaining schedule. The title game pairs the top teams under the season's format; the champion is the winner of that game or the top team under the format, and a tied top-N finish pays every tied team.
stages.distribution: Discrete order statistics with tiebreaker thresholds; probabilities depend on small differences in head-to-head results.

stages.name: Committee selection and bracket path
stages.description: The CFP committee ranks teams by resume rather than by rating; conference champions and a seeding rule determine who enters the bracket and where; rank moves slowly week to week and is sensitive to who loses to whom. Berth, seed, quarterfinal, semifinal and finalist probabilities are bracket-path products and depend on the format in force that season. SEED and TOPSEED settle on the exact seed assigned (for example #12, or a top-4 seed), so the seeding rule in force (champion-protected versus straight seeding by ranking) changes which teams can occupy a seed.
stages.distribution: Ordinal selection with inertia; bracket progression product of conditional win probabilities with seed-dependent opponents.

stages.name: Multi-year horizon and cross-contract coherence
stages.description: Long-dated contracts such as qualifying before 2030 require a multi-season random walk of program strength with coach exits and recruiting momentum; all futures are linked by shared draws, so probabilities across contracts must be coherent. Settlement wording choices (regular season only, ties) determine which function of the draws is evaluated.
stages.distribution: AR(1)-type mean reversion of team strength across seasons; union probability over four seasons.

stages.name: Bowl eligibility and selection
stages.description: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME is settled on selection, not participation. Eligibility is on countable wins, not raw wins (NCAA Bylaw 18.7.2, 2025-26 Postseason Bowl Handbook): wins over FBS opponents must at least equal overall losses, and at most one win over an FCS opponent counts, only if that opponent averaged 90 percent of the maximum football grants-in-aid over a rolling two-year period (56.7 per year) or a waiver is granted; a deserving team that loses its conference title game stays deserving. When deserving teams are fewer than open slots, alternates come in a legislated order: denied-waiver FCS-win teams, 13-game 6-7 teams, then 5-7 teams with a postseason-eligible multiyear APR; Proposal 2026-30 (FBSOC May 2026 adoption; the Cabinet took no action on 2026-30) ends the descending-APR release of 5-7 alternates and Proposal 2026-31 (Cabinet 'Adopted (Final)') made reclassifying FCS-to-FBS programs bowl-eligible. The CFP takes its field first and conference tie-ins allocate the rest.
stages.distribution: Threshold event on a win count (>=6) combined with a slot-shortage regime; bubble teams (5-7 to 6-6) carry the probability mass while 8-win teams are near-certain.

stages.name: Lower-division and Ivy champion mechanics
stages.description: FCS, D3 and Ivy League champion markets are filed here but follow different formats: FCS has a seeded playoff bracket, D3 a larger bracket, and the Ivy League has no championship game and decides the title on conference record with possible shared titles; each needs division-specific ratings rather than SP+.
stages.distribution: Single-elimination bracket survival for FCS and D3; a conference-record race with ties for the Ivy League.

stages.name: Compound events: title-game pairs, rematches and conference counts in the CFP
stages.description: Several futures settle on joint outcomes rather than one team's path: KXNCAAFCONFMATCHUP pays when a named pair secures both title-game slots (resolving at qualification, not when played); KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X needs LSU to beat Texas in the regular season and again in the national final specifically; KXNCAAFCFPCONF counts Group of Six teams in the field; KXNCAAFCONF asks whether the champion comes from a given conference. Each must be read off one season simulation that preserves the dependence between legs.
stages.distribution: Joint events from a correlated simulation; rare compound events (rematch-final) with probabilities of a few percent and large Monte Carlo relative error.

talent_strength.note: Preseason and in-season ratings with correlated uncertainty plus a multi-year trajectory.

opponent_matchup.note: Season-level outcomes aggregate dozens of games, so unit-level matchups are second-order relative to schedule composition and rating uncertainty; matchup effects are absorbed into game win probabilities in the schedule vector.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback identity and replacement quality; other positions are not separately modelled for season contracts.

availability_news.note: Injury hazard and portal/eligibility events; no official injury feed exists.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach quality and coaching changes affect multi-year program strength and in-season stability, but no input defines coach effects separately from team ratings for futures; the program trajectory index only includes tenure and contract status.

environment.note: Weather and venue effects act per game and wash out over a season-long schedule except for the home-field component, which is carried in game win probabilities through the site term.

game_context_script.note: In-game script matters for margins but season contracts depend on win/loss only, so score-state effects do not enter beyond the game win probability; scoring margin affects only ratings.

pace_volume.note: Pace and possession counts determine per-game scores, not season outcomes directly; the count of games is fixed by the schedule and counted without volume.

efficiency_conversion.note: Efficiency enters through opponent-adjusted ratings and luck-adjusted records.

distribution_variance.note: Correlated rating draws and the Poisson-binomial distribution of wins; the simulation output (season_sim_distribution) is WEAK as an input and futures_coherence is BENCHMARK_ONLY, both removed.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Schedule path, bye and rest, and committee behaviour.

officiating_rules.note: Format, tiebreaker and title-game rules are the rule layer.

settlement_contract.note: Regular-season-only counts, selection not participation, ties paid to all, neutral exclusion and multi-year window.

cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.label: Remaining-schedule game win probability vector
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.mechanism: Game-by-game win probabilities for every unplayed game, from non-market ratings with site, rest and injury state.
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.rationale: Futures contracts on wins, undefeated seasons, conference title and playoff berth are functions of the whole schedule: a team's chance of 12 wins depends on the order, site and quality of each remaining game, and on correlated rating uncertainty; a scalar strength-of-schedule loses the product structure that drives P(undefeated).
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.measurement: For each team and each unplayed game: margin mean m = rating_team - rating_opponent + site_effect (2.5 points home, 0 neutral, -2.5 away; fitted per season) in points; P(win) = Phi(m / sigma_g), sigma_g = 13.5 points (game SD fitted on FBS 2014-2025), using non-market ratings (SP+ or own) as of the most recent Sunday. For uncertainty use posterior draws from cfb.rating_posterior_draws (draw-wise P). Output the vector and its Poisson-binomial win distribution; rest adjustment only for known byes.
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.why: Win-total, undefeated, home-undefeated, head-to-head wins and conference-title contracts all reduce to this vector plus rules.

cfb.rating_posterior_draws.label: Correlated rating posterior draws for season simulation
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.mechanism: Joint posterior samples of all team ratings so that uncertainty is shared across the games of a team and across teams in a conference.
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.rationale: Treating game outcomes as independent given point estimates understates the variance of season totals: a team whose true strength is 3 points above the estimate wins more of every remaining game. Joint draws also propagate connectivity uncertainty across conferences, which matters for conference win counts and playoff selection of Group-of-Five teams.
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.measurement: Bayesian rating model fitted to FBS game margins with team-level latent strength, home-field and prior from last season (shrinkage by returning production); draw 4000 posterior samples of the rating vector as of the latest week; for each sample simulate remaining games with game noise SD 13 points and add portal-churn variance inflation to the prior. Keep draw ID for cross-contract consistency.
free_sources: CFBD games and returning production (free key)
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.why: Correlated uncertainty is the main reason conference win-count markets and champion probabilities are fatter-tailed than independent-game simulations.

cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.label: CFP committee selection and ranking model from resume metrics
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.mechanism: Canonical CFP committee rank model (alias: cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features): predicted committee rank at each release from record, strength of record and schedule, quality wins and losses, head-to-head and common opponents, conference champion status, key injuries and the previous ranking.
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.rationale: Playoff berth, seed and top-N ranking contracts are decided by a committee, not by the ratings: the committee emphasises wins over ranked teams and conference championships, penalises losses depending on opponent and timing, and moves slowly week to week. A rating-only model misses the selection layer.
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.measurement: Fit an ordered-response rank model on every CFP committee release 2014 to latest: rank_t ~ rank_(t-1) (inertia), ESPN Strength of Record or own resume metric from non-market ratings, strength of schedule, wins over top-25 and top-50 opponents, losses (count, margin, opponent quality, week of loss), head-to-head and common-opponent results versus adjacent-ranked teams, conference-champion flag (set only after title games), starting-quarterback injury flag, week index, with separate weights before and after championship week. Calibrate by rank error, pairwise ordering accuracy for adjacent ranks and probability of making the field. Output the rank distribution per team for every future release date (labelled weekly releases such as Nov 24 and the selection-day ranking). Serves season_futures (field, seed) and polls_and_cfp_rankings (exact and top-N rank).
free_sources: ESPN FPI/Strength of Record pages (free scrape)
ESPN college-football injuries and game summaries JSON (free limited) plus team depth charts for QB status
raw_data: starting-quarterback availability by game (point-in-time injury and depth-chart status)
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.why: The contracts on playoff, quarterfinal, semifinal, seed and conference representation are selection outcomes whose mapping from results is committee-specific.

cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.label: Conference membership, schedule format and title-game rules by season
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.mechanism: Season-specific table of conference members, number of conference games, title game participants rule and tiebreakers.
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.rationale: Realignment changes the set of teams and the format of every conference contract (for example a reconstituted Pac-12, divisionless Big Ten and SEC, Big 12 title game with the top two teams); a historical conference average built on old membership misprices strengths and tiebreaker paths.
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.measurement: Maintain a table keyed by (season, conference, team) with membership dates, number of conference games (8 or 9), who plays whom (unbalanced scheduling), title game qualification rule (top two by conference winning percentage with tiebreak order), and champion determination. Update on realignment announcements; version by effective date; use to compute valid conference simulations.
free_sources: CFBD teams and conferences endpoints (free key)
raw_data: conference membership by season with effective dates
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.why: Conference champion, qualifier and top-finisher markets depend on structure, and the 2026 season contains markets for conferences with changed membership.

cfb.program_trajectory_index.label: Program trajectory index for multi-year contracts
cfb.program_trajectory_index.mechanism: Composite of coach tenure, recruiting trend, portal net value, financial resources and past performance for the next four seasons.
cfb.program_trajectory_index.rationale: KXNCAAFTFUT asks whether a team makes the CFP before 2030, which cannot be answered with this year's rating alone: it depends on coach stability, talent pipeline, and revenue-sharing resources over four seasons, and on a random walk of team strength with regression to the mean.
cfb.program_trajectory_index.measurement: Estimate by regression on 2014-2025 team-seasons: rating_{t+1} - mu = phi x (rating_t - mu) + b1 x (3-year recruiting composite z) + b2 x (net portal rating change z) + b3 x (new head coach flag) + e, with phi, b1-b3 and the residual SD fitted (report values and CI), rating = non-market SP+ or own. Simulate 4 seasons ahead from the as-of preseason rating; add coach-exit hazard and conference membership as stated. P(at least one CFP berth) uses cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model. As-of preseason, update after portal window.
free_sources: CFBD talent and portal endpoints (free key)
cfb.program_trajectory_index.why: Only a multi-season strength process with program inputs can price long-dated qualification contracts.

cfb.qb_availability_hazard.label: Starting-quarterback availability hazard and replacement path
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.mechanism: Probability distribution of quarterback games missed for each contender over the remaining schedule, with the backup's quality.
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.rationale: Top-heavy playoff and title contracts depend on single-quarterback injuries: with an annual per-game miss rate near several percent the chance of losing the starter for at least one game across 12 games is substantial, and the drop to the backup's strength is large; ignoring it makes title probabilities too concentrated.
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.measurement: Per-game probability that the starter misses a game = base rate estimated from FBS history (to be measured, assume a few percent per game) x mobility/rushing-volume multiplier (designed rushes per game relative to norm) x prior injury history flag; backup rating from prior-year snaps and recruiting composite with shrinkage k = 100 dropbacks; combine in the rating draw to get a mixture over games missed. As-of weekly.
free_sources: CFBD player usage and rosters (free key)
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.why: Supplies the injury-driven fat tails to team strength draws used in all season-level contracts.

cfb.bowl_selection_state.label: Bowl eligibility, slot balance and conference tie-in selection model
cfb.bowl_selection_state.mechanism: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME settles on being selected (not playing) for a certified bowl or the CFP. Chain: countable wins (wins over FBS opponents plus at most one win over an FCS opponent averaging 90% of the maximum football grants-in-aid over two years, Bylaw 18.7.2.1.1) -> deserving status (countable wins >= overall losses, e.g. 6-6; a deserving team that loses its conference title game stays deserving) -> CFP field removed -> conference tie-in allocation -> if deserving teams < open slots, legislated alternates (denied-waiver FCS-win teams, 13-game 6-7 teams, then 5-7 teams with a postseason-eligible multiyear APR, no longer in APR order after Proposal 2026-30).
cfb.bowl_selection_state.rationale: Selection is not a function of raw wins: a second FCS win, or a win over an FCS team that did not average 90 percent of the permissible maximum grants-in-aid over a rolling two-year period (56.7 per year under the post-House-settlement Q&A; waiver possible for catastrophic cases), does not count, so a 6-6 team can be ineligible. Tie or forfeited games do not count. When slots exceed deserving teams, alternates follow a legislated order; Proposal 2026-30 (FBSOC May 2026 adoption; the DI Cabinet took no action on 2026-30 at its June 23-24 2026 meeting, so the FBSOC adoption stands) removed the descending-APR ordering of 5-7 alternates, so the conference with the unfilled tie-in chooses among its APR-eligible 5-7 teams, and Proposal 2026-31 (DI Cabinet June 2026 'Adopted (Final)') made programs reclassifying from FCS to FBS bowl-eligible. A 6-6 mid-major is a bubble case while a 7-5 power team is safe.
cfb.bowl_selection_state.measurement: For each draw of cfb.rating_posterior_draws simulate remaining games. Per team: countable_wins = wins over FBS opponents + min(1, wins over FCS opponents that averaged >= 90% of the permissible maximum football grants-in-aid per year over the rolling two-year period, i.e. >= 56.7, or hold an approved waiver); wins over non-Division I opponents, ties and forfeits = 0. Deserving if countable_wins >= overall regular-season losses (12 games: 6-6; 13 games: 7-6, a 6-7 team is an alternate); a loss in the conference championship game does not remove deserving status. Reclassifying FCS-to-FBS programs are treated as regular FBS members from 2026 (Proposal 2026-31). Remove the CFP field first, then allocate deserving teams in each season's bowl pick order: each bowl takes the best remaining team of its tie-in conference by score = countable_wins + 0.5 x (AP-ranked flag) + logit draw term (multinomial logit on wins, rank, conference, travel distance fitted on 2014-2025 selections). If deserving teams < open slots, fill in the legislated order: (1) teams whose only shortfall is a non-qualifying FCS win with a denied waiver, (2) 13-game 6-7 teams, (3) 5-7 teams with a multiyear APR permitting postseason play; for 2026 onward the unfilled tie-in's conference picks its own 5-7 team by the same score (no APR order), for 2014-2025 backtests use descending multiyear APR. Output P(selected) per team and P(deserving < slots) per season. Re-run weekly as of latest results; no market input.

cfb.bowl_selection_state.why: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME (sampled WYO, rules text: selected to play in a bowl game or the CFP, regardless of whether they actually compete; only NCAA-certified Division I bowls count) needs eligibility and slot-balance logic that no win-total or title model supplies.

cfb.lower_division_title_model.label: FCS, Ivy and lower-division title bracket model
cfb.lower_division_title_model.mechanism: For FCS, D3 and Ivy League champion markets: team strength from FCS-specific results and the postseason format (FCS playoff bracket and seeds; Ivy League has no title game and awards titles on conference record, possibly shared).
cfb.lower_division_title_model.rationale: FBS ratings (SP+) do not cover these teams; FCS results require their own rating from scores with large mismatch capping, a 24-team bracket with seeds and byes, and the Ivy champion is decided by conference record with possible co-champions, so a market on a single Ivy champion depends on tie handling in the contract (unread, title only).
cfb.lower_division_title_model.measurement: Use the single score-based rating of cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model (ridge margin rating per division, margin cap 35, home edge fitted, game weight halving each 1.5 seasons, preseason = 0.6 x prior final shrunk to conference mean) with its posterior SD. Simulate 20,000 seasons: remaining conference games, then conference title by that conference's tiebreak rule (Ivy: best conference record, ties shared and reported as co-champion), then the FCS playoff bracket from announced seeds with neutral/home site per round. Output P(champion) and P(co-champion) per team. Weekly as-of last completed game; no market input.
free_sources: NCAA statistics and FCS schedules (free scrape)
raw_data: FCS, D3 and Ivy game results
FCS playoff bracket and seeds by season
cfb.lower_division_title_model.why: KXNCAAFCS, KXNCAAFFCS and KXNCAAFD3 (rules text: win the FCS or Division III national championship) and the TITLE_ONLY KXNCAAFIVY are outright markets on divisions and a conference that the FBS-centred inputs do not cover.

cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.label: Conference schedule grid and correlated win-count simulation inputs
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.mechanism: For the count-of-teams-with-10+-wins contracts: the conference game grid (who plays whom, home/away, byes) plus non-conference opponents define each team win probability vector, and shared rating uncertainty plus intra-conference head-to-head games make team outcomes dependent.
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.rationale: The count is not a Poisson-binomial of independent teams: every intra-conference game gives one team a win and another a loss, so wins are negatively dependent within the conference, while a shared conference-strength error (cross-conference calibration) makes them positively dependent. The two forces change the variance of the count and therefore the tail rung (5+ Big 12, 7+ Big Ten, 8+ SEC). Regular season only, so championship games and bowls are excluded from the count.
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.measurement: For each conference, take the 2026 schedule as of the as-of date: for every game g compute P(home win) from a non-market rating difference (cfb.sp_plus or own rating) plus venue term, with each team rating drawn once per simulation from N(rating, cfb.rating_posterior_sd^2) and a conference-level shift drawn from N(0, tau_c^2) with tau_c estimated from the historical dispersion of cross-conference results (start tau_c=1.5 points, to be fitted). Simulate 20,000 seasons, count teams with >=10 regular-season wins (FCS opponents count as wins) and read P(count>=K). Re-run weekly using results to date as fixed; report the simulated count variance against the independent-Poisson-binomial variance as a diagnostic.
free_sources: CFBD games and schedule endpoints (free key)
raw_data: team rating and rating SD as-of date
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.why: KXNCAAFSECWINS, BIGTENWINS, BIG12WINS and ACCWINS (rungs 8+, 7+, 5+, 4+ teams with 10+ regular-season wins) need a joint conference-grid simulation in which every intra-conference game hands one team a win and the other a loss.

cfb.g6_cfp_berth_count_model.label: Group of Six CFP berth count model
cfb.g6_cfp_berth_count_model.mechanism: Distribution of the number of Group of Six teams (AAC, C-USA, MAC, Mountain West, Sun Belt, Pac-12 per the contract) in the CFP field, from simulated conference champions, their committee ranking and the automatic-bid rule in force.
cfb.g6_cfp_berth_count_model.rationale: KXNCAAFCFPCONF (2+ Group of Six teams) is not a sum of independent team probabilities: the automatic-bid rule gives a bid to the highest-ranked conference champions, so usually one G6 champion gets in and a second needs either an at-large ranking or a second G6 champion ranked above a Power champion; the contract's G6 list includes the Pac-12, whose reconstituted membership changes the count, and the berths are negatively dependent through limited slots.
cfb.g6_cfp_berth_count_model.measurement: Per simulation draw (20,000 runs, shared rating draws from cfb.rating_posterior_draws): simulate remaining games and conference title games; rank teams by the committee resume model; apply the season's bid rule (five highest-ranked conference champions plus at-large by rank under the 12-team format, alternative branch for any adopted change); count teams from the contract's six conferences. Output P(count >= k) for k = 1..3. Weekly as-of the latest CFP ranking release; no market input.
free_sources: CFBD games and rankings endpoints (free key)
raw_data: remaining schedule and conference title game rules
CFP bid and seeding rule text
cfb.g6_cfp_berth_count_model.why: Prices the KXNCAAFCFPCONF count rungs, where slot competition and the conference-champion bid rule dominate.

cfb.joint_path_event_model.label: Joint path events across regular season, title games and CFP bracket
cfb.joint_path_event_model.mechanism: Joint probability of compound season events, such as a specific pair meeting in a conference title game (KXNCAAFCONFMATCHUP) or the same pair meeting twice with one result each time (KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X), computed inside one season simulation rather than as products of marginals.
cfb.joint_path_event_model.rationale: Compound contracts are dominated by dependence: beating Texas in the regular season raises LSU's chance of making the CFP and lowers Texas's, and a rematch in the national final requires both to win opposite bracket halves; title-game pair contracts require both teams to finish top two under the conference tiebreakers, which are positively or negatively correlated through head-to-head results. Multiplying marginal probabilities misprices these by large factors.
cfb.joint_path_event_model.measurement: From the shared season simulation (20,000 runs, same rating draws as cfb.rating_posterior_draws, conference tiebreaker logic from cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_map, CFP selection and bracket from cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model and cfb.playoff_format): count runs in which the compound condition holds exactly as written (e.g. LSU beats Texas on Nov 14 AND both reach the CFP final AND LSU wins it; specific pair finishes top two and qualifies). Report the probability with its Monte Carlo SE; as-of the latest completed week; no market input.
cfb.joint_path_event_model.why: KXNCAAFCONFMATCHUP and KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X settle on compound events whose legs are strongly dependent.

cfb.standings.reason: Conference standing and tiebreaker state decides title-game and champion contracts, but the label bundles three different things (standings arithmetic, tiebreaker rules and a CFP ranking model); the tiebreaker and championship-game qualification rules should be separate rule tables by season and conference.

cfb.playoff_format.reason: Format rules (number of teams, automatic bids for conference champions, seeding method) determine how strength becomes berth, seed and finalist probabilities and change by season; it is a rule table mislabelled as market structure, and 2026-27 details beyond the 12-team model are not verified.

cfb.market_ratings.reason: Strength backed out of futures or game prices is the comparator for edge; as an input it removes the possibility of independent information and imports the quote's errors into every conditional probability.

cfb.sp_plus.reason: A second independent estimate of team strength; for futures the preseason SP+ is mostly a function of returning production and recruiting, so it is correlated with roster_continuity and talent.

cfb.roster_continuity.reason: Returning production sets the preseason prior width; its weight decays as games are played, and it overlaps with transfer_roster which should be merged into a net production measure.

cfb.talent.reason: Recruiting composite gives a durable ceiling and depth prior; most useful for multi-year contracts (KXNCAAFTFUT before 2030) where it persists, much less for a team whose current-year rating is known.

cfb.schedule_strength.reason: A scalar summary of remaining difficulty loses the sequence, home/away and rest of each game; the simulation needs a game-by-game vector of win probabilities (cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities) of which this scalar is a derived summary.

cfb.pythag_luck.reason: Close-game record luck regresses; matters for ranking resume (committee looks at record) and for expected wins when only the record is observed, but small by comparison with the schedule path.

cfb.polls.reason: Generic label (category other); the useful part is a measurable model of how committee and AP rank respond to results, which is separately handled in the polls archetype; attach as a feature of committee behaviour, not as a mood indicator.

cfb.qb.reason: Quarterback injury and regime drives title-odds variance for top-heavy contenders; as defined it mixes status and performance, and a hazard rate with replacement quality is the missing structural piece.

cfb.award_narrative.reason: No award series is attached to this archetype in the ledger (awards live in the awards_and_honors archetype), so Heisman narrative has no path into season-level conference, playoff or win-total contracts.

cfb.futures_coherence.reason: Sum-to-one and implication constraints across linked futures are price relationships used to detect stale quotes; they say nothing about team strength or schedule and cannot be inputs.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures de-vigged give a comparator for each contract; again a benchmark, not an input, and futures books carry large holds that must be removed.

m.rules_text.reason: Settlement wording differs across series: regular-season only (wins, undefeated), selection not participation (bowl), ties resolved to all-tied-yes (regular season top N), neutral sites excluded (home undefeated), multi-year window (TFUT).

cfb.transfer_roster.reason: Portal churn drives preseason rating changes and can swing a futures prior by multiple points; it is only valid for the roster known at the vintage date and needs a timestamped transfer table.

m.quote_history.reason: Futures quote history reveals when and how strongly the market reacted to results and injuries; useful to study efficiency and information timing, not an input.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Futures books are thin; depth governs executable size and not any determinant of the season outcome.

m.fees.reason: Fees matter more for long-dated futures held for months (capital lock-up) but have no relation to the football outcome.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest in futures indicate liquidity and crowding in popular contenders; not a determinant of results.

m.trade_tape.reason: Tape of futures trades shows informed flow around injuries or committee rankings; a validation tool, not a feature.

m.lifecycle.reason: For futures the lifecycle matters because contracts can settle early once mathematically decided (e.g., a team eliminated from a conference title) and because determination dates (bowl selection, CFP committee release) fix the information set.

cfb.season_sim_distribution.reason: This is the output of the season simulation, the thing being estimated, not an input; listing it as an input risks leakage and circularity, and it should be replaced by the simulation's ingredients (game win vectors, rating draws, rules).

interactions.mechanism: Playoff berth probability is a steep step in the number of losses: a team with zero or one loss is very likely in, a team with three losses rarely, and which side of the step the team lands on depends on who the losses came against and when; the committee's treatment of one loss also depends on conference championship status.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(berth) by loss count and quality of losses on historical committee years; fit a step with conference champion and loss-timing interactions.

interactions.mechanism: A contender's title odds are a mixture over quarterback health states: with the starter its rating is high, with the backup it falls several points, and the draws shared across games produce fat tails; top-heavy contenders (one dominant quarterback) have more mass in the downside branch.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate title odds with and without the hazard, and test whether realised outcomes of teams with elite QBs show larger deviations from rating-implied expectations.

interactions.mechanism: Conference championship qualification depends on unbalanced schedules and head-to-head tiebreakers: a team that has already beaten its closest rival holds the tiebreaker and needs fewer wins, so remaining head-to-head games have asymmetric value that a simple expected-wins model misses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare conference qualifier probabilities from a full tiebreaker simulation against a ranking by expected wins on historical seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Over a four-year horizon the contribution of current talent decays toward a program mean while portal and revenue resources renew it; the incremental value of an extra recruiting-class point is large in year one and small by year four.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit multi-season rating AR(1) with recruiting and portal covariates and test the lag structure of their coefficients.

interactions.mechanism: Selection rules differ between seasons (field size, automatic bids for champions, seed construction) so the same resume gives different berth probability under different formats; contracts for the same season must use the format regime in force, and the 24-team expansion market implies a possible future regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit berth probability separately by regime and test if pooling across formats worsens calibration.

interactions.mechanism: For KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X the regular-season result changes the second leg: an LSU win lifts LSU's CFP odds and lowers Texas's, and the two must then land in opposite bracket halves; the probability of the rematch final conditional on the first result is far from the unconditional rematch probability, so the product of marginals misprices it.
interactions.how_to_test: In the season simulation, compare P(rematch final | LSU wins on Nov 14) with P(rematch final) and with the independence product.

nonlinearities.shape: Product structure: P(undefeated) = prod p_i; small per-game changes compound exponentially
nonlinearities.why: A team with 85 percent win probability in each of 12 games has a 14 percent chance of an undefeated season but at 90 percent it is 28 percent; the market price must reflect compounding, not averaging.

nonlinearities.shape: Steep logistic in loss count with a conference-champion shift
nonlinearities.why: Berth probability falls from near certainty at 0-1 losses to a small fraction at 3, and a shifted threshold for champions of strong conferences.

nonlinearities.shape: Positive skew in aggregate win-count variance from correlated draws
nonlinearities.why: The variance of the total of wins across a conference is greater than the sum of independent game variances because of shared rating uncertainty, producing fat tails in count markets.
