contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL settles YES if the named team scores more than the half-point strike (for example New Mexico over 45.5) in the game; the sampled rules text does not state whether overtime points count. A game postponed but started within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official final result; otherwise a fair price. This archetype holds only KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL.

rules_evidence.quote: If New Mexico scores over 45.5 points in the New Mexico vs Nevada college football game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The strike is a strict greater-than on one team's points, so 46 or more points are required; no push is possible.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponements under 48 hours do not void; beyond that the market resolves to a fair price per the same text.

rules_evidence.quote: New Mexico over 45.5 points scored
rules_evidence.establishes: This is the market title, not rules text: it confirms a one-team points total with a half-point strike and says nothing about overtime.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime treatment is not stated in the sampled KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL text (unlike 4Q and 2H contracts); a team that scores in overtime could cross the strike, and overtime frequency is asserted rather than sourced (to be measured by cfb.ot_model).
Points scored by a team include defensive and special-teams touchdowns and safeties; the sampled text says scores over without exclusion of non-offensive scores.
A very high strike (45.5) for a team belongs to a mismatch or an elite offence and the ladder is nested with rungs down to the low teens.
Cancellation or non-start within 48 hours resolves to a fair price, so weather suspension of an unfinished game is a distinct edge case not covered by the sample.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final result of the game per the Kalshi wording; the stats provider is not named in the sampled text.

mechanism.summary: A team's points equal its own drives times points per drive (plus non-offensive scores), where its drives are a share of the game's possessions that depends on the opponent's clock control and turnovers, and where points per drive come from the team's offence against the opponent's defence with a style-dependent split between passing and rushing. The central problem is that the team total is a one-sided slice of a game with a script: a favourite's scoring is capped by blowout management while the underdog's total is lifted by garbage-time drives and constrained by its own offence. The distribution is lumpy (3 and 7 multiples) with a long right tail from short fields and return touchdowns.

stages.name: Own possession count after opponent control
stages.description: The team does not get half the combined drives: the opponent's slow, clock-burning offence trims its chances, turnovers and special-teams plays create asymmetry, and quick scores return possession to the opponent sooner. Own expected drives equal a share of game drives that is estimated from drive-level records rather than from season plays per game.
stages.distribution: Count of own drives, roughly 10 to 14, Gaussian-like with SD of about 1.5; share varies with matchup tempo.

stages.name: Points per drive from offence against defence
stages.description: Own points per drive depend on the opponent-adjusted offence, the opposing defence's pass and rush components, red-zone finishing and kicker range; strengths are not symmetric because a pass-first offence meets only the secondary's quality while a run-first offence meets the front. Late personnel news on quarterback, line and skill players moves this term.
stages.distribution: Per-drive 0/3/7 mixture with team-specific TD share; mean points per drive about 2.0-2.4 for typical FBS offences with wide cross-team spread.

stages.name: Script cap or lift on the team's scoring
stages.description: Once the team leads by three scores the coach substitutes and runs the clock, capping its total; the trailing team passes more and benefits from garbage possessions. Persistence of scoring after a lead is coach-specific and creates a bimodal relationship between rating gap and team total: elite teams vs weak ones either reach 50 or stall at 38.
stages.distribution: Mixture: competitive-game regime (tight, near its mean) versus blowout regime (capped for leaders, lifted for trailers).

stages.name: Conditions and dependence on opponent score
stages.description: Weather affects pass-heavy attacks more, and the relationship between the team's points and the opponent's points (positive via pace, negative via clock control and script) determines the variance of the team total relative to the game total. The ladder must be consistent with the game total and spread distributions.
stages.distribution: Bivariate score distribution with regime-dependent correlation; wind effect threshold-like.

stages.name: Contract mechanics and overtime scope
stages.description: The strike is a half-point greater-than on one team's points and the ladder of rungs is nested, from low teens to the 40s; overtime treatment is not stated. Conditional input set: if overtime counts in KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL, cfb.ot_model (P(tie after 60 minutes), overtime possession scoring; see the overtime archetype tie curve) adds an increment to the team points distribution; if not, it drops out.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the team points pmf to rungs; overtime adds a small mixture component with probability P(tie after regulation).

talent_strength.note: Own offence and opposing defence opponent-adjusted efficiency; broader strength measures are in the catalog but not attached to this archetype.

opponent_matchup.note: Both halves of the opposing defence are attached: secondary coverage for pass-first offences and cfb.run_defense (line yards allowed, stuff rate, rushing PPA allowed) for run-first offences, crossed with the offence style share.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback, receivers and backs, line and kicker.

availability_news.note: Late availability, with the usual absence of an official feed.

coaching_scheme.note: Scheme identity and lead-dependent play calling.

environment.note: Forecast wind and rain applied by team style.

game_context_script.note: Score-state effect on own scoring through starter-removal timing and persistence of scoring by the leader; the benchmark team-total split is removed.

pace_volume.note: Own possessions from tempo and drive share.

distribution_variance.note: Lumpy team-score pmf and its covariance with the opponent; cfb.score_resid (market-derived, WEAK) is removed.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, lookahead and rivalry/revenge spots can lower or raise a team's scoring intensity but no input in the archetype represents them for team totals; their effect on a single team's points is not quantified.

officiating_rules.note: Crew tendencies change penalty counts marginally and so own scoring by well under a point; the clock-rule regime is a season-level constant that enters via pace, so no officiating input is needed for a team-total rung.

settlement_contract.note: Greater-than half-point strike and the 48-hour postponement rule; overtime scope unresolved and m.ladder_structure (price-derived, BENCHMARK_ONLY) is not an input.

cfb.own_drive_share.label: Own share of combined possessions
cfb.own_drive_share.mechanism: Fraction of the game's total drives that the team receives, after turnovers, special-teams outcomes and the opponent's clock use.
cfb.own_drive_share.rationale: A team's points equal its drives times points per drive; its drive count is not half of the game total because turnover and quick-score differences give one side extra possessions, and a team that burns clock on its own drives reduces the opponent's possessions. A team total rung depends on its own count, not on the average pace.
cfb.own_drive_share.measurement: For each team compute its drive share = own drives / (own + opponent drives) in each of the last 10 games, opponent-adjusted by the opponent's mean share allowed, with 0.8 decay and shrinkage k = 5 games to 0.5; add components: average drive duration (own), opponent drive duration allowed, turnover differential per drive. Expected own drives = share x expected combined drives (non-market total pace). As-of last completed game.
raw_data: drive table with start/end clock and results
cfb.own_drive_share.why: Separates the team's scoring trials from the game's, which the existing pace input (plays per game) does not.

cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.label: Leader scoring persistence (points per minute when leading by 14+)
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.mechanism: How much a team keeps scoring after taking a large lead, versus pulling starters and running the clock.
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.rationale: A heavy favourite's team total lies in the tail of its ability: coaches like some that keep their offence on the field, while others run the ball and substitute early; the same rating produces team totals that differ by 7-10 points depending on persistence. The underdog's mirror image is garbage-time scoring.
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.measurement: For each team, points scored per minute of game time when leading by 14 or more in Q2-Q4, over 2 seasons with decay 0.5 per season, relative to the points per minute when within one score; shrinkage k = 60 minutes to the FBS mean; compute also the time of first substitution by backups (depth-chart snap shift) when available. Combine with the probability of reaching a 14-point lead from the rating gap to obtain expected own points.
free_sources: CFBD plays with score state (free key)
raw_data: plays with period, clock, score diff, offense
backup quarterback and running back snaps
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.why: Directly governs the high rungs where a favourite is expected to reach 45+ points.

cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.label: Own-versus-opponent score covariance
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.mechanism: Covariance between a team's points and its opponent's points given the expected margin and total.
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.rationale: Own and opponent scores are positively correlated through pace and negatively through script and clock control, so the variance of own points depends on the regime; a team total over 45.5 is more likely in shootouts where both score, and less likely when the opponent runs the clock.
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.measurement: From FBS games since 2014, compute residual correlation between team points and opponent points after removing expected team points from non-market ratings, by bin of expected margin (-14 to +14) and expected total; shrink bin correlations to pooled correlation with k = 150 games. Use the covariance matrix to turn a game-level total and margin model into a joint bivariate distribution; check consistency with the team total ladder. Functional form: team points as negative-binomial scoring-drive counts joined by a Gaussian copula with rho = rho0 + rho1 x |expected margin| + rho2 x expected total (coefficients fitted by maximum likelihood on FBS 2014 onward; the sign change of rho is a hypothesis to test, not an assumption). Tail check: validate P(team points > 45) calibration on held-out games with expected team points above 38, since rungs like 45.5 sit in the far right tail.
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.why: Ensures the own-score distribution is consistent with game total and spread distributions instead of being fitted separately.

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Defined as implied team means from game total and spread, which are both prices; the same split can be rebuilt from non-market expected margin and total, and the quoted version is useful only as the comparator for edge.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Own opponent-adjusted offence is the strongest determinant of the team's mean, but PPA converts to points only through drives and finishing, so it must be paired with drive count and scoring-trip finishing, not treated as a points estimate.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Opponent defence suppresses own points; its pass and rush components affect different offences differently, so the aggregate value understates the matchup term that the interactions below address.

cfb.pace.reason: Own tempo matters but the opponent's clock use limits possessions; own possession share, not own plays per game, is the relevant volume and the original label ignores the opponent's effect.

cfb.redzone.reason: Red-zone TD rate moves points per trip by up to a point per game but regresses heavily; a high rung like 45.5 requires several touchdowns where the rate matters, though the sample per season is small.

cfb.kicker.reason: Own kicker range and accuracy set the share of drives that end in 3; matters for mid rungs where a field goal decides the integer outcome, less for tail rungs.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: Own starting quarterback explains a large share of own-team scoring variance and is the main late news item; a backup also affects tempo and run share.

cfb.skill_avail.reason: Absent receivers or backs lower the ceiling and need replacement-quality estimates; effect smaller than quarterback and usually smaller than offensive line.

cfb.ol.reason: Own line continuity affects sack rate and run efficiency and thereby points; label mixes offensive and defensive lines, and the defensive-line part belongs to the opponent's matchup, not to own scoring.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Strongly relevant here: a heavy favourite's team total is capped by starter removal and clock running, and an underdog's total rises with late garbage drives; the behaviour is coach-specific and sets the upper tail of the rung distribution. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind and rain affect own scoring according to the team's pass or run reliance; the effect must be crossed with style, not applied uniformly.

cfb.score_resid.reason: Residuals relative to lines tie the calibration to the market; the intended clustering at multiples of 3 and 7 can be modelled directly from team score pmf by drive outcomes without reference to quotes.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook team totals and spread-total implied splits are the comparator for edge; not an input for the same reason as for game totals.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Consistency of the team total ladder with the game total and spread ladders is a diagnostic of staleness; derived from prices and cannot explain scoring.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price history is the market's own output; it measures when information was absorbed (useful for timing studies and closing-line value) but is not a cause of the team total outcome and must not enter a fundamentals model.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread govern whether a team total edge is tradable, not whether the event occurs; keep for execution and sizing, not as an outcome input.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule changes net edge on team total contracts (largest near 50c) but has no causal link to the result; an execution parameter, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe liquidity and price reliability for team total quotes; useful to weight benchmark trust, irrelevant to the outcome process.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades show informed flow and fill realism for team total contracts; it is market microstructure used to validate fills, not a determinant of the outcome.

m.lifecycle.reason: Open/close/halt/postponement events matter here because the 48-hour postponement clause converts a delayed team total market to a fair-price settlement; needed to define the information set and void handling.

cfb.offense_style.reason: Option, air-raid and RPO styles change possession count and explosiveness; relevant to variance as much as to mean, and overlaps with pace and pass-rate descriptors. Reverification: the catalog measurement uses style-specific residuals of spread/total, which are residuals around market lines (the same defect as cfb.score_resid); only residuals against own non-market ratings are admissible, the line-residual version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.secondary_coverage.reason: The pass half of the opponent defence; paired with cfb.run_defense (now attached) so the style x opposing unit interaction can be tested on both halves.

cfb.script_rush_attempts.reason: Team rushing attempts (KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT) are filed under game_stat_props after the reconciliation; the team points total does not settle on attempts, and run share already enters via script effects on drives.

cfb.pass_rate.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on cfb.off_ppa x cfb.secondary_coverage x cfb.pass_rate: Own offense x opponent defense style: pass-heavy offense vs strong secondary is hurt more than vs run defense) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.pass_rush.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on cfb.qb_status_pit x cfb.ol x cfb.pass_rush: QB and OL availability: unknown QB or OL changes sack rates and efficiency simultaneously, so team total adjus) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.run_defense.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on cfb.off_ppa x cfb.secondary_coverage x cfb.run_defense x cfb.offense_style: A pass-first offence is hurt by a good secondary but not by a good front, and a run-first offence the reverse;; stage s2) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

cfb.ot_model.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s5) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: A strong offence's expected total keeps rising with rating gap only until a three-score lead; beyond that, conservative coaches cut the team's points while persistent coaches keep scoring, so the response to rating gap flattens at a coach-specific level.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot team points versus pre-game gap by persistence tercile and test for a break at gap 21-24.

interactions.mechanism: A pass-first offence is hurt by a good secondary but not by a good front, and a run-first offence the reverse; the appropriate matchup term is the product of style share with the opposing unit's quality, not the sum of overall offence and defence.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit own points on style share x opposing unit allowed values; compare with additive offence-plus-defence baseline.

interactions.mechanism: A backup quarterback behind a depleted line loses more than either shock alone, while a healthy line with a backup can still produce points through the run game; the effect is conditional on the other components of the offence.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast team totals in games with QB change plus OL loss versus QB change alone and OL loss alone.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis, not an established effect: own and opponent points move together through pace but diverge through clock control; the correlation changes sign across regimes, so team total variance cannot be obtained from the game total variance by a fixed fraction.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation of own and opponent points by expected margin and expected pace buckets; confirm sign flip.

interactions.mechanism: Above a wind threshold a pass-first team's scoring regime switches to short fields and field goals which are also limited by wind, while a run-first team is mostly unaffected; the team total's sensitivity to forecast wind is thus regime-dependent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team points in windy versus calm games by pass reliance and kicker range.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave with a cap: team points flatten once the lead exceeds roughly 21
nonlinearities.why: A favourite does not keep scoring proportionally to its rating edge because starters leave and the clock runs; the cap differs by coach, so the high rungs are less probable than a linear rating-to-points map suggests.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in drives but with threshold at about 9 drives: below that, the team total rarely exceeds mid rungs
nonlinearities.why: A team with few drives needs high efficiency to reach a high rung, and below some drive count the probability collapses faster than the mean implies.

nonlinearities.shape: Sign changes from positive (shootouts) to negative (clock control) across expected-pace regimes
nonlinearities.why: The variance of team points depends on the covariance regime, which alters tail probabilities of high rungs independently of the mean.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Completed games before as-of date; ratings as-of the preceding week.
required_data.history_needed: 2014 onward

required_data.dataset: Play-level run/pass and sack accounting
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Plays up to the as-of date; NCAA stat-definition vintage for sacks.
required_data.history_needed: 2014 onward

required_data.dataset: Availability, kicker and weather vintages
required_data.grain: player x game x capture time; game x issue time
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Capture time stamped; use at least 1 hour before kickoff.
required_data.history_needed: Self-capture forward

unresolved.description: The sampled KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL rules do not state whether overtime points count; with overtime in a few percent of games and a lumpy score distribution, ignoring or including overtime changes rung probabilities near the median. Resolution selects the input set: overtime counted requires cfb.ot_model and the overtime archetype tie curve; regulation-only does not.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the full rules text of live team-total tickers and check the settlement of a past overtime game.

unresolved.description: cfb.run_defense is now attached to stage s2 and the opponent_matchup coverage, but its weight against overall def_ppa rushing and the need for a separate opponent rush-yards-allowed measure are untested; run-first offences were previously handled by overall def_ppa only.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Test whether run_defense adds explanatory power for run-first offences beyond def_ppa on historical team scoring, and whether rush yards allowed adds anything beyond rushing PPA allowed.

unresolved.description: Rest, rivalry, lookahead and revenge effects on individual team scoring are not represented; large effects are plausible in particular games (rivalry week, trap games) but not established.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Test residual regressions of team points on rest and rivalry flags across seasons using non-market expectations.

contract.settlement_definition: After the market-universe reconciliation no live series is filed under touchdown_scorer: the six team and game touchdown series previously here (TEAMTD, TOTALTD, TEAMRSHTD, TEAMRECTD, DSTTD, FIRSTTDTEAM) were assigned to game_stat_props, whose record now carries their settlement reading. A named-player anytime or first-touchdown-scorer contract would settle on official scoring credit, but no such contract text exists to read, so no settlement detail is asserted.
variants_and_edge_cases: No live series: the team/game touchdown counts and the first-team race were reassigned to game_stat_props; the mechanism and inputs below remain as the catalog definition for a future named-player scorer market and are reused by game_stat_props stage s7.
A future named-player market would need its own reading of fumble-recovery credit, overtime and the treatment of a player who does not play (void versus No), none of which can be read now.
Two-point conversions never count in any sampled sibling touchdown series, including in overtime; a player market could differ.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game statistics and scoring summaries of the final result; Kalshi text refers to numbers recorded by the team during the game and names no provider in the sampled rules.

mechanism.summary: Touchdown counts equal the number of scoring trips times the probability each trip ends in a six-point score, plus non-offensive touchdowns (the game_stat_props rules texts include them for total and first-touchdown counts; the team-count text is silent), split into rushing, receiving and returns by goal-line play calling and turnover returns. Scoring trips follow possessions and efficiency (the same machinery as team and game totals), but the live contracts settle on counts of touchdowns and not points, so finishing (touchdown versus field goal) is the central variable. First-touchdown markets are a race between two arrival processes with a head start for the receiving team, and counts above the mean live in a heavy tail created by mismatches and shootouts. Reconciliation note: the archetype currently has no live series; the team/game touchdown series were reassigned to game_stat_props, which reuses these inputs.

stages.name: Scoring trips and touchdown conversion
stages.description: A team produces scoring trips (first downs inside the opponent 40) in proportion to its possessions and efficiency against the opposing defence; each trip ends in a touchdown with probability set by goal-line efficiency, play calling and kicker alternatives. Touchdown count rather than points is the quantity, so a field-goal-heavy offence has the same points but fewer touchdowns.
stages.distribution: Binomial or compound count of touchdowns per trip with overdispersion across teams and games.

stages.name: Touchdown type: rushing versus receiving
stages.description: Close-range plays favour runs and quarterback sneaks, longer scores favour receiving; the split depends on the offence's scheme, quarterback mobility and score state (leaders run, trailers pass). Backups and depth-chart roles change who scores but only marginally change the team's rushing count, and the fumble-credit rules decide edge cases.
stages.distribution: Multinomial split of touchdowns by type with team-specific share; shares shift with lead size.

stages.name: Race for the first touchdown
stages.description: The first team to score a touchdown is determined by the order in which two hazard processes first fire; the opening possession order, scripted opening drives and defensive scores matter, and there is a probability that neither team scores in the full game. For a future named-player first-scorer market, whether overtime touchdowns count is unread; the sibling team race (KXNCAAFFIRSTTDTEAM, now in game_stat_props) counts them.
stages.distribution: Competing hazards with a deterministic head start for the opening receiver; a small point mass of no-touchdown games.

stages.name: Defensive and special-teams touchdowns
stages.description: Return touchdowns require opposing turnovers or kick-return opportunities and are rare, partly skill (ball-hawking defences, return specialists) and partly luck, with rule changes on kickoffs altering exposure. They add to totals and race markets but are excluded from the rushing and receiving counts.
stages.distribution: Rare-event Poisson with small rate (game probability of at least one on the order of 15 to 25 percent, to be fitted).

stages.name: Count dispersion, availability and settlement
stages.description: High-count rungs (total TDs of 8 or more, rushing TDs of 5 or more) are tail events where clustering in mismatches fattens the distribution; late availability and eligibility news affect team strength rather than the count directly. No live series here: the two-point and overtime treatment of the sibling team-count texts in game_stat_props is not assumed for a future player market.
stages.distribution: Negative binomial with dispersion that increases in expected total and gap; tail sensitivity to blowouts.

talent_strength.note: Team scoring efficiency at the touchdown level plus non-market opponent-adjusted strength (SP+, PPA) now attached; the benchmark team_total_split is removed.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing defence TD per trip allowed by type and overall opponent-adjusted defence; cfb.dvp (named-position matchup, WEAK) removed.

role_personnel.note: Mobile quarterback and skill-player availability for the rushing/receiving type split; depth_chart and player_usage (WEAK, named-player only) removed.

availability_news.note: Quarterback status (the main news item) and skill-player absence shift the trip count and type shares; suspension_eligibility (WEAK) removed.

coaching_scheme.note: Goal-line play calling and scripted openers.

environment.note: Wind and rain (cfb.weather_pit) shift the run/pass touchdown split and the count; the size of the effect is unquantified (weather_effect_on_td_split).

game_context_script.note: Lead-dependent run share and opening possession.

pace_volume.note: Expected scoring trips = possessions (cfb.pace, cfb.drives) x trip rate; cfb.td_per_scoring_trip supplies only the per-trip conversion, so the volume side is measured by the attached pace and drives inputs.

efficiency_conversion.note: TD conversion and type, plus non-offensive scores.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry and bowl stakes shift scoring slightly but there is no argument that they change touchdown-specific outcomes beyond the game-level scoring mean, so no separate input is justified for TD counts.

officiating_rules.note: Settlement rules for two-point conversions, fumble credit and overtime; targeting and other penalties are second-order.

settlement_contract.note: Counts exclude two-point tries, overtime touchdowns count in periods 1-2, race market includes defensive scores.

cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.label: Touchdowns per scoring trip (drives reaching opponent 40) with type split
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.mechanism: Expected touchdown count from the number of drives reaching scoring range and the touchdown conversion rate, split into rushing, receiving and non-offensive.
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.rationale: All live series count touchdowns, not points: a drive that ends in a field goal produces no TD, so TD count depends on finishing (TD versus FG versus turnover) more than on points; the type split determines TEAMRSHTD and TEAMRECTD.
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.measurement: For each team: trips = drives with a first down at or inside the opponent 40; TD per trip over last 10 games with 0.85 decay, opponent-adjusted by the opponent defence's TD per trip allowed, shrinkage k = 25 trips to the FBS mean; split of TDs by type (rush, pass, other) over 2 seasons with shrinkage k = 30 TDs. Expected team TDs = expected trips x TD per trip; variance from negative binomial with fitted dispersion.
raw_data: drives with start/end field position and result
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.why: Converts efficiency into the count variable the live contracts settle on, and separates rushing from receiving touchdowns.

cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.label: Goal-to-go and short-yardage run/pass mix
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.mechanism: Share of goal-line and short-field plays that are runs (including quarterback sneaks and designed runs) versus passes.
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.rationale: Within the same number of touchdowns, the split between rushing and receiving depends on goal-line play calling: option and power-run offences score rushing touchdowns at close range where spread passing offences score receiving touchdowns, and trailing or leading status shifts the mix.
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.measurement: Compute run share on plays inside the opponent 10 and on 3rd/4th-and-short, by team over 2 seasons with decay 0.5 per season and shrinkage k = 40 plays to the conference mean; add TD conversion rate by type; condition on score state with a logistic model (leading by 14+ increases run share by 0.10-0.15 in the fit). Output expected rushing and receiving TD counts given expected total TDs.
raw_data: plays inside opponent 10 with run/pass and result
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.why: Sets which player type is credited near the goal line for a future named-player scorer market; reused by game_stat_props for the rushing/receiving touchdown split.

cfb.first_td_race_rate.label: First-touchdown race (hazard and no-touchdown mass)
cfb.first_td_race_rate.mechanism: Rate at which each team scores its first touchdown, including defensive and special-teams touchdowns, and the probability that neither scores in the full game.
cfb.first_td_race_rate.rationale: First team to score a touchdown is a race between two hazards with a deterministic head start for the receiving team on the opening possession, and with a small chance that neither scores (low-scoring game); overtime still counts for this market.
cfb.first_td_race_rate.measurement: From games since 2014, model time to first TD per team as a piecewise-constant hazard by drive index; hazard depends on team TD per trip, drive pace, opening possession order (receive-first adds probability mass at drive 1) and opponent's early defence; shrink to league hazard with k = 10 games; compute P(team A first) = integral; add P(no TD in 60 min + overtime) from low-total regimes (calibrated on FBS history). As-of kickoff with opening possession probability from cfb.opening_poss. Non-offensive and overtime components: add a defensive/special-teams touchdown arrival hazard per possession of the opponent (from cfb.dst_td_propensity) that can fire before any offensive possession ends; the No-team-scores outcome mass = P(no TD in regulation, from the hazards) x [1 - P(tie after 60 minutes, cfb.ot_model) x P(a touchdown in overtime periods 1-2 | tie)], since the contract settles the first touchdown in the full game including overtime.
free_sources: CFBD plays and scoring plays (free key)
raw_data: scoring plays with time and drive index
cfb.first_td_race_rate.why: The first-TD market needs the order of arrival of two Bernoulli processes, not a count, and has an explicit No TD outcome.

cfb.dst_td_propensity.label: Defensive and special-teams touchdown propensity
cfb.dst_td_propensity.mechanism: Probability that a game contains at least one touchdown scored by a defence or special teams, from turnover returns, kick returns and blocked kicks.
cfb.dst_td_propensity.rationale: DST touchdowns require the opposing offence to turn the ball over in a returnable place or special teams to give returns; they depend on interception and fumble rates, return specialists and the rules for kickoff returns, and are rare events with fat tails.
cfb.dst_td_propensity.measurement: Expected DST TDs per team-game = interceptions forced per game x pick-six rate (shrunk k = 40 INTs to the FBS mean) + fumbles forced x return-TD rate + kick/punt return TD rate for the returner + blocked-kick rate, each opponent-adjusted by the opposing offence's turnover rate; game probability = 1 - exp(-lambda_total) with lambda total = sum of both teams. Kickoff rule regime recorded by season. As-of last game.
raw_data: plays with interception, fumble, return, blocked kick and TD flags
cfb.dst_td_propensity.why: Non-offensive touchdowns remove scoring credit from offensive players in a named-scorer market; reused by game_stat_props for DSTTD and the first-touchdown race.

cfb.td_count_dispersion.label: Touchdown count dispersion and tail probabilities
cfb.td_count_dispersion.mechanism: Variance-to-mean ratio of team and game touchdown counts and tail probability of 5+ team rushing or 8+ game touchdowns.
cfb.td_count_dispersion.rationale: Counts like total touchdowns 8+ and rushing touchdowns 5+ sit in the upper tail where a Poisson underestimates the probability because scoring drives cluster in mismatches and shootouts.
cfb.td_count_dispersion.measurement: Fit a negative binomial to game TD counts by expected-total and gap bins from FBS 2014 onward: mean mu(bin) and dispersion r(bin); report P(N >= k) for k in 1..12 with a 95 percent interval from bootstrapped games; shrinkage to pooled dispersion with k = 150 games. For team rushing TD counts fit separately by team style bucket.
free_sources: CFBD games and scoring plays (free key)
raw_data: touchdowns by game, team and type
cfb.td_count_dispersion.why: Gives tail probabilities for high-count rungs where a continuous model fails.

cfb.td_rates.reason: Role-based anytime and first-TD scoring rates are the core of a named-player scorer market, but no such series is live (the team and game counts moved to game_stat_props); WEAK until a player series is listed, then primary.

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Expected team touchdowns derived from implied team totals are derived from prices; the TD count should be built from drives and TD per scoring trip using non-market ratings, with the quote kept as the comparator.

cfb.player_usage.reason: Target, carry and snap shares allocate touchdowns among players; with no named-player series live they have no settled outcome to feed, and the team-level run/pass split is a play-calling mix carried by goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.

cfb.qb_rushing.reason: Quarterback designed runs and sneaks take a large share of goal-line rushing touchdowns, which lowers the anytime-scorer probability of running backs in a future named-player market; also reused at team level in game_stat_props.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: In lopsided games the leader runs the ball with backups and the trailer passes late, shifting the rushing/receiving split and the total count; relevant to counts above 5 rushing TDs or 8 total. Reverification: the catalog measurement conditions on the spread/total (spread-implied script or lead probability); only a version rebuilt on the non-market expected margin and total (SP+ or own rating) is admissible here, the spread-based version is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

cfb.skill_avail.reason: Absent receivers or backs matter for the type split and for the number of scoring drives only modestly; as a team-level input its effect is much smaller than for named-player markets.

cfb.depth_chart.reason: Which back holds the goal-line role changes the player scorer but not the team's rushing-TD count; relevant only if named-player series are listed, which the ledger does not currently show.

cfb.opening_poss.reason: Receiving the opening kickoff gives the first possession and raises the probability of scoring the first touchdown by a few points; the toss is unknown pregame so it is only a forecastable tendency.

cfb.first_drive.reason: Scripted opening-drive touchdown rate bears directly on the first-TD race but rests on about twelve drives per team-season, so it requires heavy shrinkage.

cfb.dvp.reason: Defence versus position is defined for named receivers and backs; a team-level rushing-TD or receiving-TD count is better matched with the opposing defence's TD rate allowed by type than with positional matchups.

cfb.in_game_exit_risk.reason: In-game injury or removal risk of a starter has little effect on a team's total touchdown count, and is a player-market concept; negligible here.

m.rules_text.reason: No live series in this archetype, so no rules text is read; the sibling team texts (two-point conversions excluded, overtime counted, fumble-recovery credit) are not assumed for a future player market, whose own text would be primary.

cfb.suspension_eligibility.reason: Suspended players change who scores, not the count of team touchdowns; keep only for a future named-player market.

cfb.transfer_roster.reason: New transfers change goal-line roles in named-player markets; for team TD counts the effect is already inside team ratings and offensive style.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price history is the market's own output; it measures when information was absorbed (useful for timing studies and closing-line value) but is not a cause of the touchdown count outcome and must not enter a fundamentals model.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread govern whether a touchdown count edge is tradable, not whether the event occurs; keep for execution and sizing, not as an outcome input.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule changes net edge on touchdown count contracts (largest near 50c) but has no causal link to the result; an execution parameter, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe liquidity and price reliability for touchdown count quotes; useful to weight benchmark trust, irrelevant to the outcome process.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades show informed flow and fill realism for touchdown count contracts; it is market microstructure used to validate fills, not a determinant of the outcome.

m.lifecycle.reason: Lifecycle events would define the information set and postponement handling for a future player market; with no live series the 48-hour clause of the sibling team texts is not assumed here.

interactions.mechanism: Team rushing touchdowns equal TD count times rushing share, and the rushing share is higher with a mobile quarterback and a power-run goal-line mix; both the count and the share vary across teams, so the product has more spread than either factor.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit rushing TD counts with an interaction of expected TDs and goal-line run share; compare with an additive version.

interactions.mechanism: In a one-sided game the leading team runs near the goal line and uses backups, raising the rushing share and total TD count for the leader, while the trailing team throws and adds receiving touchdowns; the combined effect on high-count tails depends on the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rushing and receiving TD counts by gap bin and leader/trailer role.

interactions.mechanism: First-TD probability depends on the receiving team's head start and each team's early hazard, and defensive touchdowns add a third arrival channel that can reverse the order when the opposing offence is turnover-prone; the three are not independent because the same offence both scores and turns over.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(first TD by team) as a function of opening possession and turnover-proneness; test the interaction of receive-first with pick-six rate.

interactions.mechanism: A defensive or special-teams touchdown flips the game script, and the knock-on effect on the opponent's passing and rushing touchdown counts depends on the pre-game expected margin: it is large in an evenly matched game where the scorer's lead changes the trailing team's play mix, and small when the scorer is already a heavy favourite or the opponent is far behind anyway.
interactions.how_to_test: Using SP+ expected margin bins, compare rushing and receiving touchdown counts of the team that conceded a DST touchdown against those in games without one, and test whether the gap shrinks as the absolute expected margin grows.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy right tail: variance exceeds Poisson mean and grows with expected total
nonlinearities.why: The probability of 8 or more touchdowns is several times the Poisson value at the same mean because high-scoring teams cluster in shootouts and mismatches.

nonlinearities.shape: Head-start step for the receiving team plus a small point mass at no touchdown
nonlinearities.why: The opening possession order gives a discrete advantage that cannot be represented by a smooth rate, and some games have no touchdown at all.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in lead size: run share rises sharply beyond a 14-point lead
nonlinearities.why: Leading teams run in short yardage and burn clock, so the type split is sensitive to the lead once it is two scores.

contract.settlement_definition: Voted-award series settle YES if the named person wins the award in the stated season: AP conference awards (KXNCAAFACCAWARD, BIG12AWARD, BIGTENAWARD, SECAWARD; the samples are Defensive Player of the Year), national awards (KXNCAAFAWARD, sampled Biletnikoff) and the Bear Bryant Coach of the Year (KXNCAAFCOTY). For player awards, a player who does not play in the season for any reason resolves No, and if several players share the award YES pays 1/N rounded down. Finalist markets (KXNCAAFAWARDFIN) settle YES if the player is selected as a finalist as reported by a Source Agency, and all resolve No if finalists are not announced before the winner. The COTY text states no tie or participation clause. Statistical-leader series moved to unreg:season_stat_leader and KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE to coaching_and_governance_events.

rules_evidence.quote: If Will Heldt does not play in the 2026 college football season for any reason, the market for that player resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: A player who is injured, transfers or is suspended out of the season resolves No, so participation is part of every voted-award contract.

rules_evidence.quote: In the event that finalists are not announced and reported by one of the Source Agencies prior to the award winner being announced, then all markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Finalist contracts depend on the award body publishing a finalist list, a procedural risk independent of performance.

rules_evidence.quote: If JaMarcus Shephard wins the Bear Bryant Coach of the Year award in 2026-27 college football season
rules_evidence.establishes: Coach awards settle on the award body's selection; no tie or no-play clause appears in the sampled text.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple players are awarded, “Yes” positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent)
rules_evidence.establishes: Co-winners of an AP conference award split the YES payout 1/N, so a shared award is a partial payout, not a push.

rules_evidence.quote: If Gavin Freeman wins the Biletnikoff Award in the 2026 college football season
rules_evidence.establishes: National award series settle on the award body's selection for the named season; the electorate differs by award.

variants_and_edge_cases: Four mechanisms share the archetype: AP-voted conference awards (four conferences), national position awards selected by award bodies (Biletnikoff sampled), finalist selection, and coach of the year.
The sampled AP conference Defensive Player of the Year series have status inactive in the evidence, so trading can lapse before the ballot is known.
Player award texts resolve No when the player does not play in the season for any reason, and pay 1/N to co-winners; the COTY text has neither clause.
Finalist markets resolve No for everyone if no finalist list is reported by a Source Agency before the winner announcement.
KXNCAAFAWARD carries an award code per event (BILE sampled); other national awards (possibly Heisman) may be listed under the same series with different electorates, which the sample does not show.
contract.settlement_data_source: Award bodies' official announcements and Associated Press results for voted awards; finalist lists as reported by Kalshi's Source Agencies.

mechanism.summary: The archetype covers voted awards decided by electorates responding to visible statistics and team success (AP conference awards, national position awards such as the Biletnikoff), finalist selection by award bodies, and a coach-of-the-year decision rewarding overperformance against expectation. Each player contract is filtered by participation (no play resolves No), then by projected production against the remaining schedule up to the ballot date, then by the electorate's weighting of production, team success and visibility; co-winners split the payout. Statistical-leader and draft-declaration series were moved out by the reconciliation.

stages.name: Candidate pool and participation
stages.description: Only players who play contribute; the candidate pool for a voted player award is the few dozen high-production receivers (Biletnikoff) or edge rushers and linebackers (AP Defensive Player of the Year), with injury and benching hazard removing some each week. A candidate who misses games loses visible production and one who sits out the season resolves No, so participation is the first filter for every player series.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli participation per game with fat-tailed season-ending probability; heavier for high-workload positions.

stages.name: Production accumulation that voters see
stages.description: Voted awards respond to visible season production: receiving yards and touchdowns for the Biletnikoff, sacks, tackles for loss and takeaways for the AP Defensive Player of the Year. A candidate's end-of-ballot totals come from per-game usage times efficiency against the remaining schedule and the games left before the ballot, so the projected production race among a handful of candidates shapes the vote, with teammates competing for the same volume.
stages.distribution: Sums of overdispersed per-game counts; maximum of correlated sums; ties possible.

stages.name: Electorate response for voted awards
stages.description: Voters see counting statistics, team record and ranking, and highlights, and award ballots are collected at a fixed date before bowls; electorates differ by award (AP voters for conference awards, a committee for position awards), and positional constraints (receiver for Biletnikoff) filter candidates. Vote share is a multinomial contest with winner-take-all payoff and ties when shared.
stages.distribution: Multinomial vote shares with concentration; winner-take-all contest; ballot date fixes the information set.

stages.name: Coach of the Year outcome
stages.description: Coach of the Year is awarded for exceeding expectation: wins against a preseason non-market expectation, ranking gains and conference outcomes. The ballot is a decision by an electorate, not an output of a game model, so the surprise index and the information available at the ballot date matter more than final strength.
stages.distribution: Logistic winner probability driven by a single latent surprise score with a winner-take-all contest among a few coaches.

stages.name: Settlement mechanics and procedural risk
stages.description: Co-winners pay 1/N, a player who does not play in the season resolves No, and finalist markets resolve No if finalists are not reported before the winner; ballots close before bowls, so postseason production is irrelevant, and an inactive market can stop trading before results are known.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping with discrete tie fractions; procedural risk is a small probability mass.

talent_strength.note: Team success and coach expectation drive votes; individual player talent enters through production.

role_personnel.note: Usage determines volume; quarterback status matters only through a receiver's targets and team success for coach votes.

availability_news.note: Injury, benching and transfer hazard; no official feed exists.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach of the Year; scheme shifts to usage are not separately defined.

environment.note: Venue and weather affect individual game production but over a season-long cumulative stat these wash out except through the opponent-adjusted per-game rates; no separate environmental input is justified.

game_context_script.note: Score-state effects (trailing teams pass more, leading teams run and rotate) change award candidates' cumulative production but no input models the script effect on a candidate's usage; its size relative to injury hazard is unknown.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-game production per opportunity for receiver candidates (inside leader_race_state, used here as the projected award-ballot production race) and sack, TFL and pressure rates per pass-rush snap for defensive awards; the offence-only WEAK inputs are removed.

officiating_rules.note: Officials do not affect award voting or season totals except through statistical corrections; the relevant rules clauses (tie, participation) are carried under settlement_contract, not as an officiating input.

settlement_contract.note: Tie-sharing, participation and finalist-announcement clauses read from rules.

cfb.leader_race_state.label: Statistical-leader race state (current leaderboard plus projected remaining production)
cfb.leader_race_state.mechanism: Cumulative stat as of the query week for each candidate plus a distribution over remaining production, from usage, efficiency, opponents and games left.
cfb.leader_race_state.rationale: Leader contracts (most rushing yards, passing TDs, receiving yards, sacks) resolve at the end of the regular season on cumulative totals, so the price is an order-statistic problem over several candidates with a current lead, a different number of games remaining and different injury exposure; ties pay $1/N. Note: this id bundles the leaderboard state (current total, gap to rivals, games remaining) with a projection; the state is the input and the overtaking probability is a model output built from it.
cfb.leader_race_state.measurement: For each candidate, mean per-game production over the last 6 games weighted 0.8 per game, shrunk toward prior-season rate with k = 4 games; adjust per remaining opponent by the opponent's allowed rate (opponent-adjusted), games remaining from the schedule, P(plays) from the hazard input; simulate remaining totals from negative binomial per game with candidate-specific dispersion, add to current total, and compute P(rank 1) with ties allocated 1/N. Update weekly; as-of the previous Sunday.
free_sources: CFBD player season and game stats (free key)
cfb.leader_race_state.why: Projected end-of-ballot production of each award candidate relative to rivals, the statistical record voters see for the Biletnikoff and defensive awards.

cfb.player_participation_hazard.label: Player participation and season-ending injury hazard
cfb.player_participation_hazard.mechanism: Per-game probability that a candidate plays and the probability of a season-ending injury or benching, by position and usage.
cfb.player_participation_hazard.rationale: Contracts resolve to No if the player does not play in the season, and a candidate who misses games falls out of a counting-stat race; running backs and edge rushers have higher injury exposure than quarterbacks and are the main candidates of leader markets.
cfb.player_participation_hazard.measurement: Fit on FBS 2014-2025 player-games: P(miss game g) = logistic(position, carries per game over position median (z), prior-season games missed share, previous-week missed flag, team games remaining) with a position-specific intercept from the data (no assumed constant); P(season-ending | miss) = fraction of misses followed by all remaining games missed, by position. Remaining-season path = Bernoulli chain over games remaining. Redshirt and transfer eligibility enter as absorbing states. Weekly update with news captured with timestamps; as-of previous Sunday.
cfb.player_participation_hazard.why: Controls how often an award candidate loses production or resolves No under the did-not-play clause, directly shaping late-season probabilities.

cfb.award_vote_feature_model.label: Award-specific vote-share model features
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.mechanism: Candidate-level features that predict vote share for each award: counting stats, team record, ranking, position bias and highlight games.
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.rationale: Different awards have different electorates and different positional constraints: the Biletnikoff goes to a receiver, AP defensive player awards to defenders, and voters see box-score numbers and team results rather than efficiency grades; a position-agnostic Heisman narrative variable misses all of this.
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.measurement: For each award and year since 2010 fit a multinomial logit of vote share on: rank of the candidate's primary counting stat among the position pool (percentile), team win percentage and AP rank at ballot time, games played fraction, prior-year honours, and a position-group indicator; regularise with ridge (lambda chosen by leave-year-out); produce candidate probabilities with ties handled by 1/N rule where voters can share an award. Ballot date as-of cut.
raw_data: award winners and finalists by year
team record and AP rank at ballot date
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.why: Replaces the unmeasurable narrative input by features voters can observe, separately per award.

cfb.coach_overperformance_index.label: Coach overperformance index
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.mechanism: Wins above preseason expectation and rank change for a head coach's team, from non-market preseason ratings.
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.rationale: Coach of the Year voting rewards teams that exceed expectations, not simply the best team; a coach who takes a team expected to win 5 to 11 wins is favoured over one at the top of the polls, but ranking and conference title also matter.
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.measurement: Index = (actual wins to date + sum of remaining-game win probabilities) - (sum of preseason win probabilities over all regular-season games), where every game win probability comes from the frozen preseason non-market rating (SP+ or own, Week 0 vintage) plus site effect; add (AP rank at preseason - AP rank at ballot date)/25 and a conference-title indicator as separate columns. Fit historical Coach of the Year winners 2005-2025 with a logit on index, final record, final rank, first-year flag. As-of ballot date; no market input.
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.why: Coach of the Year (KXNCAAFCOTY) is decided on surprise relative to expectation, which no other input measures.

cfb.defender_production_profile.label: Defender production and pass-rush usage profile
cfb.defender_production_profile.mechanism: For defensive voted awards (AP conference Defensive Player of the Year) and sack/tackle-for-loss leaders: the defender share of pass-rush snaps, pressures, sacks, TFL and havoc plays per game against the remaining schedule.
cfb.defender_production_profile.rationale: Defensive votes follow headline sacks and TFL plus team success, and a leader race in sacks depends on pass-rush snap volume, opponent pass-attempt volume and offensive-line quality rather than on rushing or passing efficiency; offence-centric inputs say nothing about it.
cfb.defender_production_profile.measurement: For each defender: sacks, TFL and pressures per pass-rush snap over the last 6 games with weight 0.8 per game, shrunk to a prior-season rate with k = 150 pass-rush snaps; expected snaps remaining = games remaining x snap share (last 4 games); opponent adjustment = opponent offence sacks-allowed rate relative to the FBS mean, with opponent pass attempts forecast from its pass rate; simulate remaining sacks per game as Poisson with a dispersion fit on 2014-2025 and add to the current total; for award votes include team rank and opponent-adjusted havoc rank. As-of the previous Sunday.
free_sources: CFBD player stats and PPA (free key)
raw_data: defender sacks, TFL and pressures by game
opponent sacks allowed and pass attempts
cfb.defender_production_profile.why: The four AP Defensive Player of the Year series need defender production and pass-rush usage, which the offence-centric inputs do not carry.

cfb.award_narrative.reason: Narrative has no measurable definition as written and is Heisman-centric; the live series are AP conference awards, the Biletnikoff, finalists and coach of the year, which need measured production, team success and electorate features (award_vote_feature_model) instead.

cfb.award_vote_distribution.reason: Historical vote-share distributions by award are the right base for voted contracts, but electorates differ by award (AP writers for conference DPOY, a foundation panel for Biletnikoff, a coaches or writers panel for coach awards), so it must be built per award and not pooled.

cfb.player_usage.reason: Targets and pass-rush snaps are the volume that produces the receiving and sack/TFL production voters see for the Biletnikoff and AP Defensive Player of the Year; the original secondary role understates it, since production is mostly a usage story with an efficiency multiplier.

cfb.pass_efficiency.reason: No live series here is a quarterback award (passing leaders moved to season_stat_leader); per-attempt passing efficiency matters only indirectly through receivers' production for the Biletnikoff.

cfb.qb.reason: Starting quarterback status and regime matter for a Biletnikoff candidate's targets and for team-success-based votes (coach awards), but are irrelevant to defensive awards; scope-limited.

cfb.qb_rushing.reason: Quarterback rushing adds to Heisman narratives but no live series is a Heisman or quarterback award; the live player series turn on receiving and defensive production, so relevance is marginal.

cfb.td_rates.reason: Touchdown rates by role translate usage into headline numbers for offensive voted awards, but none of the live series is an anytime touchdown market and the share of voter weight on touchdowns versus yards is not established.

cfb.standings.reason: Team record and ranking raise voters' support for individual awards and are the dominant input to coach of the year; use rank and wins above expectation rather than raw standing.

cfb.schedule_strength.reason: Voters discount production against weak schedules and the remaining schedule determines games left before the ballot for a candidate's production; two distinct uses that should be separated.

cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.reason: KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE is filed under unreg:coaching_and_governance_events; no award, finalist or coach-of-the-year series here depends on NFL draft declaration.

interactions.mechanism: An award candidate's chance is the product of leading the visible production race and staying healthy: a candidate with a small production lead and high workload faces a higher chance of falling behind because of injury, so the joint of current gap, workload and hazard shapes the probability more than the gap alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the production race with and without the hazard and compare to realised award outcomes of past candidates by workload tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Voters weight statistics by team success and discount production against weak schedules, so a candidate's effective support is production percentile times a team-rank factor times a schedule discount; the same stats on a ranked team and an unranked team yield very different vote shares.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit logit vote share with the product of stat percentile and team rank; compare with additive features.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis to test: a coach who beats expectation by many wins wins only if the team also finishes ranked or wins a title; above a threshold of wins above expectation the probability jumps, and below it conference rank decides.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate winner probability by bins of wins above expectation crossed with final rank across history.

interactions.mechanism: For the AP conference Defensive Player of the Year, voters reward sack and tackle-for-loss leaders much more when the player's team is ranked or contending; a high pass-rush production rate on a losing team converts to fewer votes, so the production effect is conditional on team record.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit historical conference DPOY winners on sack/TFL rank, team win percentage and their product; test whether the production slope rises with team record.

interactions.mechanism: Remaining schedule changes a candidate's projected production before the ballot, and for a receiver it also depends on whether his starting quarterback keeps playing; a Biletnikoff candidate with an easy remaining schedule gains only if his team keeps passing at the same rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised production in remaining games with projections split by remaining opponent rank and team pass rate.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in the gap: probability of overtaking falls rapidly once the lead exceeds about one game's production
nonlinearities.why: Remaining games contribute a bounded amount of production, so a lead above the remaining capacity is effectively decisive, making probabilities approach 0 and 1 faster than a linear lead model.

nonlinearities.shape: Winner-take-all concentration: vote share to winner probability is a steep softmax, not proportional
nonlinearities.why: A candidate with 40 percent share of expected votes wins far more than 40 percent of the time because winner-take-all amplifies leads.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy-tailed: a small probability of immediate elimination with large impact, increasing in workload
nonlinearities.why: Season-ending injuries remove a candidate abruptly; the probability is small per game but compounds across the remaining games and concentrates in the highest-workload players.
